https://www.amnesty.org/fr/latest/news/2.body: Des défenseures des droits humains du monde entier se réuniront à Genève du 21 au 25 septembre 2026, afin d’en apprendre davantage sur le Conseil des droits de l’homme des Nations unies, de plaider en faveur de leurs droits et de faire entendre leurs différentes histoires. Cette formation d’une semaine, intitulée Semaine de plaidoyer pour les femmes défenseures des droits humains , est co-organisée par neuf organisations de défense des droits, dont Amnesty International (voir la liste complète ci-dessous). Elle a pour objectifs de fournir aux participantes des outils pratiques pour mieux comprendre le Conseil des droits de l’homme, tout en leur proposant des lignes directrices sur la manière de dialoguer de manière stratégique avec cette instance et de militer en faveur du changement au sein de leurs communautés. « Les femmes présentes ici risquent leur vie chaque jour pour protéger leurs communautés des effets du changement climatique, de la cupidité des entreprises et de la spoliation des terres, a déclaré Lisa Maracani, chargée de recherche à Amnesty International sur les défenseur·e·s des droits humains. Elles ont des connaissances cruciales pour garantir l’efficacité d’instances telles que le Conseil des droits de l’homme, tandis que la Semaine de plaidoyer pour les femmes défenseures des droits humains a pour but de leur fournir les outils et les stratégies nécessaires pour faire progresser leur plaidoyer sur cette scène mondiale. » Les femmes présentes ici risquent leur vie chaque jour pour protéger leurs communautés des effets du changement climatique, de la cupidité des entreprises et de la spoliation des terres Lisa Maracani, chargée de recherche à Amnesty International sur les défenseur·e·s des droits humains Les participantes sont des défenseures des droits qui œuvrent à la croisée des questions liées au genre, au climat et aux conflits, notamment des militantes engagées dans la protection de l’environnement, la défense des droits des travailleuses migrantes, des droits fonciers des peuples autochtones, ainsi que des droits des populations touchées par les activités des entreprises. Cette formation vise à faciliter la participation des militantes confrontées à de multiples obstacles pour accéder aux instances des Nations unies, à leur permettre d’acquérir une connaissance approfondie du système des droits de l’homme, à favoriser la création de réseaux entre elles et avec des expert·e·s en droits humains, et à amplifier leurs voix et leurs appels en faveur de la responsabilité internationale. Les participantes auront la possibilité de s’exprimer devant le Conseil des droits de l’homme, mais aussi de rencontrer des responsables de l’ONU, des diplomates et des expert·e·s indépendants mandatés par le Conseil, de faire du lobbying auprès d’eux et de les informer. En outre, plusieurs défenseures prendront la parole lors d’un événement public organisé au siège de l’ONU jeudi 24 septembre, aux côtés de la Rapporteuse spéciale des Nations unies sur le droit à un environnement propre, sain et durable. « Le système des droits de l’homme des Nations unies doit être ouvert à celles et ceux qui ont le plus à y apporter, à savoir les défenseur·e·s des droits, et s’inspirer de leur expérience, a déclaré Fabiana Leibl, responsable de programme à l’International Service for Human Rights. Grâce à cette formation, nous cherchons à nous assurer que les points de vue des défenseures des droits soient dûment représentés au Conseil des droits de l’homme et au sein de ses principaux mécanismes. » NOTE Cet événement est organisé par Amnesty International, Asia Pacific Forum on Women (APWLD), Front Line Defenders Rights, International Service for Human (ISHR), Peace Brigade International (PBI), The Association for Women’s Rights in Development (AWID), la Coalition internationale des femmes défenseures des droits humains (WHRDIC), la Coalition des femmes défenseures des droits humains au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord (WHRD MENA Coalition), Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism (UAF).

Réagissant à l’annonce faite par le département d’État des États-Unis, dans une déclaration en date du 16 septembre, indiquant qu’il avait, pour la deuxième année consécutive, interdit à la délégation de haut niveau de l’État de Palestine, notamment au président palestinien, Mahmoud Abbas, d’assister à l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies à New York, la directrice générale des recherches, de l’élaboration des lignes de conduite, du travail de plaidoyer et des campagnes à Amnesty International, Erika Guevara Rosas, a déclaré : « Le département d’État des États-Unis doit revenir sur son refus d’accorder des visas à une délégation de haut niveau de l’État de Palestine qui compte assister à la 81 e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies. La déclaration du département d’État le montre clairement : cette décision vise à punir l’État de Palestine pour avoir cherché à obtenir justice et la reddition de comptes au niveau international auprès d’institutions internationales telles que la Cour pénale internationale (CPI) et la Cour internationale de justice (CIJ). Cette mesure s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une campagne incessante de représailles contre la notion même de justice internationale. Cette mesure s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une campagne incessante de représailles contre la notion même de justice internationale Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International « Le non-respect du droit international, ainsi que les attaques persistantes, notamment au moyen de sanctions unilatérales, contre des personnes ou des organisations de défense des droits humains engagées dans la promotion de la justice internationale, ainsi que le mépris total affiché à l’égard des ordonnances contraignantes et des avis consultatifs de la CIJ, des mandats d’arrêt émis par la CPI et des résolutions de l’Assemblée générale et du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies, portent gravement atteinte à l’ordre juridique international. “Alors que de plus en plus d’États membres prennent enfin des mesures attendues de longue date – qui restent toutefois très insuffisantes – pour mettre fin au commerce avec les colonies illégales d’Israël , ces États doivent également s’opposer fermement aux tentatives des États-Unis visant à démanteler la justice internationale et le multilatéralisme sur lequel se fonde le système des Nations unies. « Ce genre de décision, qui constitue une violation flagrante de l’Accord relatif au siège de l’Organisation des Nations Unies, crée un dangereux précédent où les États-Unis profitent de leur statut de pays hôte pour imposer des restrictions arbitraires à la participation à l’Assemblée générale et à d’autres réunions des Nations unies. « Amnesty International réitère l’appel adressé aux États-Unis pour qu’ils lèvent immédiatement et sans condition les sanctions qu’ils ont imposées concernant la CPI ou contre des personnes et organisations de défense des droits humains qui luttent pour la justice internationale, notamment les sanctions imposées à des juges de la CPI, à des organisations palestiniennes de défense des droits humains et à la rapporteuse spéciale de l’ONU sur la situation des droits de l’homme dans les territoires palestiniens occupés. Au lieu d’affaiblir le droit international, les États-Unis devraient user de leur immense influence pour faire pression sur Israël afin qu’il mette un terme à son occupation illégale du territoire palestinien, démantèle son système d’apartheid et mette fin au génocide qu’il pratique contre les Palestinien·ne·s dans la bande de Gaza occupée. »

Dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), des mineurs artisanaux ont été soumis à d’effroyables atteintes aux droits humains par des combattants du Mouvement du 23 mars (M23), un groupe armé soutenu par le Rwanda qui facilite le trafic d’or et de coltan vers ce pays avec l’aide des autorités. Des mineurs ont fait état d’agissements effroyables tels que des exécutions sommaires, des actes de torture et d’autres formes de mauvais traitements, ainsi que des détentions arbitraires et de faits de travail forcé et de recrutement forcé. Lors de cet entretien, l’un des mineurs a décrit à Amnesty International le calvaire qu’il a enduré dans un puits de mine aux mains de combattants du M23, avec des coups reçus quotidiennement et le fait d’être laissé dans les puits pendant des heures et d’être privé d’une juste rémunération. Voici donc son récit, représentatif de ce qui se passe dans d’autres mines. Depuis la dernière fois que je vous ai parlé, la situation s’est encore aggravée. Je manque d’argent pour de nombreuses raisons [notamment] parce que j’ai été battu dans le puits de mine. À cause des mauvaises conditions [dans la mine], je ne peux pas travailler tous les jours. Je travaille maintenant quatre fois par semaine. Je travaille généralement environ cinq heures par jour et ma rémunération n’est que de 5 000 francs congolais (2,17 dollars des États-Unis). Il y a environ 120 mineurs qui creusent dans chaque puits de mine. Le patron donne l’argent au gérant, et il apporte la nourriture (à ceux qui creusent). On nous donne un beignet et de l’eau pour la journée. Nous avons vu beaucoup de choses que nous ne pouvons pas oublier. Le fait d’être obligés de rester dans le puits de mine contre notre gré, le fait que nos patrons nous battent, qu’ils frappent des gens qui finissent après à l’hôpital. Mineur* , RDC *Le nom n’est pas divulgué. Dans le secteur, il y a des Rwandais qui recourent parfois à la force contre nous. Quand ils viennent, ils portent des habits civils, mais quand il y a une atmosphère de guerre, ils ont des tenus de style militaire. Je les ai vus se changer [remplacer leurs vêtements civils par des uniformes militaires] plusieurs fois. Ils sont mes patrons. Je travaille pour eux. Nous avons vu beaucoup de choses que nous ne pouvons pas oublier. Le fait d’être obligés de rester dans le puits de mine contre notre gré, le fait que nos patrons nous battent, qu’ils frappent des gens qui finissent après à l’hôpital. Ils m’ont battu cette année. J’étais dans le puits de mine et je travaillais depuis trois heures. Tout ce que j’ai entendu, c’est les coups de bâton qui s’abattaient sur moi. Après, j’ai perdu connaissance. C’est le gérant qui m’a battu. Il était congolais, un collègue, mais il venait du Rwanda. Il n’y a pas eu de dispute à l’origine de ces coups. C’est juste que vous croisez quelqu’un, et il se met à vous frapper. Les gérants sont des intermédiaires entre nous et les patrons. On ne devrait pas être battu par nos collègues. C’est pour cela qu’on pense qu’il y a des ordres qui ont été donnés. Quand je me suis réveillé à l’hôpital, j’ai remarqué tous les pansements que j’avais partout sur le corps. À la tête, sur les bras, les pieds, les articulations et aussi sur le ventre. Je suis resté trois jours à l’hôpital. Dans le secteur, il y a des Rwandais qui recourent parfois à la force contre nous. Quand ils viennent, ils portent des habits civils, mais quand il y a une atmosphère de guerre, ils ont des tenus de style militaire. Je les ai vus se changer [remplacer leurs vêtements civils par des uniformes militaires] plusieurs fois. Ils sont mes patrons. Je travaille pour eux. Mineur, RDC Il y en a d’autres aussi qui ont subi la même chose. Ça n’arrive pas tous les jours, mais peut-être quatre fois par semaine. On les emmène à l’hôpital. Parfois, d’autres gens plaident pour eux , et ils sont sauvés. D’autres meurent sur place. J’ai vu des gens mourir et être enterrés dans le puits de mine. Je veux que tout le monde sache que les téléphones payés cher qu’ils utilisent sont fabriqués à partir de minerais coûteux, et que beaucoup de sang a été versé avant que ces téléphones ne leur parviennent. Je veux que des actions de plaidoyer soient menées pour que ces minerais soient extraits de façon légale et pour que les mineurs soient aussi traités dans le respect de la loi. Nous avons donc besoin que quelqu’un porte notre voix loin, afin que, lorsque nous creusons, aucun sang ne soit versé dans le puits de mine. Un mineur artisanal travaille à l’entrée d’un puit dans la mine d’or de Lomera, dans la province du Sud-Kivu (RDC) – © DR Merci [Amnesty] de penser à nous. Poursuivez votre travail, afin de savoir ce que nous endurons. Poursuivez votre travail, afin que nous puissions mener une vie paisible comme tout le monde. Faites savoir au monde entier que nous avons besoin d’une action de plaidoyer pour que les lois du pays soient appliquées ici. Ce serait une bonne chose que des gens surveillent ce qui se passe. S’il y avait des gens chargés de mener un travail d’observation, [le M23] ne pourrait pas commettre d’exactions. Ils commettent beaucoup d’exactions. S’ils les voyaient faire de mauvaises choses, les observateurs pourraient alors écrire des rapports sur eux. Si vous pouvez nous aider à porter notre voix loin d’ici, ce sera bénéfique pour nous. Cela nous aiderait beaucoup. Aidez à mettre fin à l’impunité en RDC appelez le président TSHISEKEDI à créer un mécanisme judiciaire internationalisé. Agissez maintenant

https://bishkek.osce.org/news/programme-.body: News News Item OSCE supported CYBER NOMAD FEST 2026 to strengthen Kyrgyzstan’s cyber resilience Issued on: 25 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Programme Office in Bishkek Bishkek, 22 September 2026 - The OSCE Programme Office in Bishkek joined national partners in supporting CYBER NOMAD FEST 2026, a national cybersecurity festival that brought together more than 700 representatives of government institutions, critical information infrastructure entities, the financial and banking sector, telecommunications and IT companies, academia, international organisations, cybersecurity experts and the professional community. The festival was organised by the State Committee for National Security of the Kyrgyz Republic and the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic, together with SkySOC Beeline and the OSCE Programme Office in Bishkek. The event provided a platform for strengthening co-operation among government institutions, the private sector, the technology and expert communities, and international partners in addressing current and emerging cybersecurity challenges. One of the key events of the festival was the first meeting of the Interagency Commission on Information and Cybersecurity, which focused on effective co-operation between state bodies and local self-government authorities, assessment of current cyber threats, and further development of national co-ordination mechanisms in the field of information and cybersecurity. The programme featured the Cyber Conference, a forum with panel discussions on the protection of government information systems and critical information infrastructure, emerging cyber threats, cybersecurity in the financial and telecommunications sectors, capacity-building and the development of national cybersecurity. The festival also included Cyber EXPO, a technology exhibition showcasing cybersecurity solutions and technologies, as well as the Cyber Nomad CTF, practical cybersecurity exercises and competitions designed to strengthen participants’ technical skills and incident-response capabilities. The final stage of the Cyber Nomad CTF was held in an Attack/Defense format, simulating real-world cyber confrontation scenarios. Teams were required to protect their own infrastructure while identifying vulnerabilities in opponents’ systems, detecting attacks, analysing incidents, responding rapidly and defending their systems against further attacks. The Kyrgyz Republic and the OSCE have been co-operating in the field of cybersecurity for several years. In 2021 and 2025, the OSCE supported the organisation of national cyber exercises, which contributed to strengthening preparedness and developing the capacity of relevant stakeholders to respond to cyber incidents. The OSCE Programme Office in Bishkek’s engagement in CYBER NOMAD FEST 2026 reflected the importance of continued co-operation among national institutions, the private sector, technical and expert communities, and international partners in strengthening Kyrgyzstan’s cyber resilience. https://omik.osce.org/news/mission-kosov.body: News News Item Sharper skills, stronger stories: Kosovo journalists learn through the OSCE Media Fellowship Issued on: 25 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission in Kosovo Between April and September 2026, eight journalists working for Albanian- and Serbian-language media in Kosovo stepped beyond their familiar media environments as part of the OSCE Mission’s Media Fellowship Programme. Through meetings in Prishtinë/Priština and a study visit to Belgrade, Podgorica and Tirana, they exchanged experiences with media professionals and organizations. The fellows met with journalists, media outlets and journalists’ organizations to discuss issues at the heart of journalism today, from media sustainability, working conditions and media independence to regulation, AI and new technologies. Topics also included journalists’ safety, disinformation, professional standards and support mechanisms available to media professionals facing threats and other challenges. The eighth edition also highlighted the value of sustained exchange between journalists from different communities. Comparing newsroom realities helped the fellows recognise shared professional challenges and consider how colleagues working in another language could offer additional perspectives on a story. The contacts made during the programme provide a basis for seeking advice, exchanging information and exploring future co-operation beyond the study visit. “Through the Media Fellowship Programme, we want to create opportunities for young journalists from different communities to learn from one another, broaden their professional perspectives and build connections beyond their immediate media environment,” said Arlinda Osmanaj, Programme Officer at the OSCE Mission in Kosovo. The seven participating journalists were: Arianita Hoti (KOHA), Anastasija Đorđević (Kontakt Plus Radio), Milena Jevtić (Radio Mitrovica Sever), Shqipron Xhema (Kallxo), Sanja Kostić (former Kossev), Diellza Berisha (Klan Kosova), Festim Gërguri (IKD / Betimi për Drejtësi) and Behar Mustafa (BIRN). Established in 2017, the Media Fellowship Programme has brought together 64 young and aspiring journalists as part of the OSCE Mission in Kosovo’s efforts to strengthen professional standards and encourage exchange across communities. For the eighth cohort, the programme combined learning relevant to their daily reporting with direct access to peers across Kosovo and the region, and a shared platform to keep that exchange active. For more visit the @omikmediafellowship page on Instagram. https://odihr.osce.org/news/odihr/667848.body: News News Item ODIHR supports Kyrgyzstan’s parliament in strengthening inclusion of people with disabilities Issued on: 25 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights Fields of work: Democratization , Tolerance and non-discrimination Identifying and addressing barriers to the participation of people with disabilities in parliamentary life was the focus of an assessment in Bishkek from 22 to 24 September 2026, supported by the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR). Organized together with the Jogorku Kenesh, Kyrgyzstan’s parliament, and its Working Group on Accessibility, and with the OSCE Programme Office in Bishkek, the activities brought together parliamentarians, parliamentary staff and organizations of people with disabilities and other representatives of civil society. “Our task is not to conduct a formal inspection or compile a list of shortcomings. We need to obtain an objective picture of the current situation, identify existing barriers, and jointly determine realistic ways to systematically eliminate them,” said Mederbek Aliev, First Deputy Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh and Chair of the Working Group. The assessment combined a workshop, interviews and focus groups with a check of accessibility on the parliament’s premises and in its communications. It examined how people with disabilities are represented and involved in parliamentary work, including in representation, lawmaking, oversight and consultation, as well as the accessibility of parliamentary infrastructure, services and processes. This comprehensive disability inclusion assessment of the Kyrgyz parliament demonstrates not only the identified needs, but also the will to advance inclusion exists alongside the need,” said Tea Jaliashvili, First Deputy Director of ODIHR. “It is particularly encouraging to see the partnerships being developed between the state institution – the parliament – and civil society and international organizations in achieving the objective for the benefit of the society as a whole. Such an effective partnership is already half-way to success.” The involvement of organizations for people with disabilities brought first-hand experience and expertise into the assessment, helping identify obstacles to participation and changes needed to make parliament more inclusive. “In Kyrgyzstan, there is still insufficient understanding of disability as a matter of equal rights and opportunities. The medical and charity-based approach continues to prevail, with persons with disabilities often seen as recipients of assistance rather than as full and equal members of society, with the right to live independently, work and participate in decision-making,” said Askar Turdugulov, Chair of the New Age Public Foundation, Adviser to the Mayor of Bishkek, and Ombudsperson on Disability Issues]. The findings will inform practical recommendations to help the Jogorku Kenesh improve its infrastructure, services and working practices, supporting the equal participation of people with disabilities in parliamentary life. The assessment forms part of ODIHR’s work to advance disability-inclusive parliaments . Through its assessment methodology, ODIHR helps parliaments examine barriers across their work and identify concrete steps towards institutions that better represent and serve everyone. https://dushanbe.osce.org/news/programme.body: News News Item EU and OSCE donated technical equipment to support awareness raising on radiation safety in Tajikistan On 18 September 2026, the European Union (EU) and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) donated technical equipment to the Sughd branch of the Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Safety and Security Agency of the National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan. Issued on: 25 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe Fields of work: Environmental activities On 18 September 2026, the European Union (EU) and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) donated technical equipment to the Sughd branch of the Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Safety and Security Agency of the National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan. The equipment was handed over during an official ceremony in Dushanbe with the aim of strengthening the Agency’s institutional and technical capacity and contributing to its long-term work in radiation safety. The donated equipment will enhance the technical capacity of the Agency’s Training and Press Centre in Buston, Sughd Branch. The Centre already plays an important role in organizing radiation safety training and information campaigns for local populations in areas affected by the uranium legacy. The equipment will strengthen these ongoing activities by providing modern technical means for regular training and educational activities, as well as for raising awareness among local communities about the risks associated with uranium legacy sites and measures to mitigate them. The equipment is particularly important for Sughd region, which is affected by the legacy of former uranium mining and processing activities. Uranium legacy sites may include former mining areas, waste dumps and tailings, which can present environmental and radiation-safety concerns and require continued monitoring, awareness and risk mitigation. Strengthening the Training and Press Centre’s technical capacity will support regular radiation safety training and help local stakeholders and communities better understand the potential risks associated with uranium legacy sites and measures to reduce them. The donation was provided within the framework of the EU-funded project on “Stakeholder Engagement for Uranium Legacy Remediation in Central Asia - Phase III”, implemented by the OSCE and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. By supporting stakeholders and communities to strengthen knowledge, collaborate and take action on environmental challenges, the project reflects the shared EU-OSCE-UNDP commitment to environmental protection and meaningful engagement and aimed to reduce environmental and health risks associated with uranium legacy sites in Central Asia, which remain a source of potential contamination and hazard for communities. https://www.osce.org/chairpersonship/667.body: Media advisory OSCE Chairpersonship conference in Zug to focus on de-escalation in cyberspace Date: 22 September 2026 Place: VIENNA/BERN Source: OSCE Chairpersonship VIENNA/BERN, 22 September 2026 – The Swiss OSCE Chairpersonship will convene its conference on “De-escalation in Cyberspace: Mediation and Preventive Diplomacy” in Zug on 29-30 September 2026. It will bring together participating States, experts, academics and private sector representatives to discuss ways to reduce tensions and prevent the escalation of cyber incidents. The conference is the last of four thematic conferences organized by the Swiss OSCE Chairpersonship this year and will focus on the role of preventive diplomacy and mediation in addressing risks of escalation in cyberspace. Participants will discuss the development and implementation of the OSCE’s cybersecurity confidence-building measures (CBMs), including their role in strengthening transparency, communication and trust among participating States. The participants will also discuss the potential of cyber mediation as an emerging tool for managing tensions and preventing escalation. They will explore practical approaches, challenges and the role of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, in supporting mediation efforts. The discussions will further address the contribution of the private sector, technical communities, academia and civil society to preventing and managing cyber crises. Drawing on Switzerland’s long-standing experience in conflict prevention and mediation, as well as its expertise in cybersecurity and new technologies, the conference underscores the role of cyber diplomacy as an instrument of international peace and security and Switzerland’s commitment to an open, safe and peaceful cyberspace and responsible State behavior. Media representatives are invited to the opening of the conference, which will feature addresses by Swiss Federal Councillor Martin Pfister, Head of the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport and Director of the Swiss National Cyber Security Centre Florian Schütz. OSCE Chairman-in-Office, Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis, will deliver concluding remarks at the end of the event. Media representatives are required to obtain accreditation in advance. Interested journalists are invited to register no later than Friday, 25 September 2026, at 14:00 (CEST) via the following link . The Media Corner provides practical information on the venue, programme, accreditation, photos and useful links. https://uhrp.org/news/we-want-china-out-.body: “We want China out of Tibet”: Tibetans, Uyghurs hold anti-China protests in Washington over Xi’s US visit - Uyghur Human Rights Project Skip to content “We want China out of Tibet”: Tibetans, Uyghurs hold anti-China protests in Washington over Xi’s US visit September 25, 2026 | ANI News Speaking at the protest, Uyghur Human Rights Project (UHRP) Executive Director Omer Kanat drew parallels between the concerns raised by Tibetan and Uyghur communities. “The situation of Tibetans and Uyghurs is identical. As already said, Tibet was never part of China; East Turkistan was never a part of China. East Turkistan was occupied in 1949. Tibet was occupied in 1959,” Kanat said. He alleged that policies of the Chinese government had restricted religious practice, language and cultural life in Tibet and said Uyghurs faced similar restrictions. “In Tibet, the Chinese government imposed severe restrictions on religious practice, on Tibetan language and on cultural life. Tibetan children and [sic] separated from their families, raised without their language, culture or faith. Uyghur children now face the same fate as the boarding school system expands to East Turkistan,” Kanat said. https://uhrp.org/uyghur-reader/the-uyghu.body: The Uyghur Reader: Stories We’re Following (Issue 32) - Uyghur Human Rights Project Skip to content The Uyghur Reader: Stories We’re Following (Issue 32) Issue 32: September 3, 2026 – September 16, 2026 Welcome to the thirty-second issue of the Uyghur Reader, a biweekly content roundup curated by the staff of the Uyghur Human Rights Project. Each issue features carefully selected articles, reports, and publications from media outlets, academic institutions, NGOs, and government sources. While we highlight urgent human rights issues, we also aim to reflect the breadth of the Uyghur experience, including politics, economics, history, and culture. 📌 Ablet Turdi and Erk Altay of Uyghur Rights Monitor examine five digital surveillance platforms that form an integrated system for monitoring and policing Uyghurs and other Turkic peoples in the Uyghur Region. The report finds that authorities combine household registration, biometric verification, mobile phone inspections, government services, and predictive policing to turn everyday activities into intelligence and indicators of suspicion. The authors detail how platforms including iTap and the Integrated Joint Operations Platform (IJOP) aggregate data and classify individuals for police attention, including based on ordinary religious and social behavior. The report also traces the network of state-owned, private, and foreign companies whose technologies support the surveillance system. September 15, “ The Architecture of Digital Mass Surveillance in East Turkestan .” 📌 Anna Isaac and Ben Quinn of The Guardian report that Ray Addison, the top media presenter for Reform UK, a British political party, worked as a correspondent for Chinese state broadcaster CGTN in 2025, fronting a series titled Raymond’s Xinjiang Stories . The videos presented the Uyghur Region’s infrastructure and cotton industry in favorable terms, without addressing forced labor and other abuses against Uyghurs. The authors note that Addison’s work for CGTN contrasts with Reform UK leaders’ public criticism of the Chinese government; the party said it knew of Addison’s previous work before hiring him and defended his media career. September 3, “ Reform’s media presenter worked for Chinese state propaganda channel .” 📌 Asiye Uyghur , writing for Bitter Winter , examines how Chinese education policy in the Uyghur Region has increasingly placed Uyghur children in centralized, state-run boarding schools while expanding Mandarin-centered instruction and political education. Drawing from official policy documents, the article highlights the contradiction between formal recognition of mother-tongue education rights and policies that portray non-Mandarin languages as an obstacle to development and “long-term stability.” It argues that school consolidation, boarding programs, mainland classes, and vocational education have progressively shifted children away from their families, local communities, and linguistic environments while linking education to broader state goals. September 3, “How Beijing Turned Uyghur Childhood Into a State Project.” 📌 Dr. Adrian Zenz , writing in the Journal of Human Trafficking , proposes a new methodology for identifying and measuring state-imposed forced labor (SIFL), arguing that existing International Labour Organization frameworks do not adequately distinguish between the mechanisms governments use to coerce labor and the purposes for which labor is imposed. The article introduces a SIFL Categorization Matrix and a three-pillar assessment framework centered on coercion, structural coercion, and “structurally engineered involuntariness.” Zenz argues that the approach could strengthen comparative research and help regulators move beyond localized workplace audits toward assessments of the broader state systems that produce forced labor risk, with particular relevance for enforcement of the European Union Forced Labor Regulation. May 2026, Architecture of Coercion: Conceptualizing and Measuring State-Imposed Forced Labor Based on ILO Standards . 📖 Keep reading Massimo Introvigne, Bitter Winter , September 14, Anthropic Reveals Massive Chinese Anti-Dissident AI-Generated Slander Justin Wong, The Press , September 14, ICBC handled NZ cash for Chinese tech firm linked to Xinjiang repression Rahima Mahmut, Middle East Monitor , September 10, We must challenge the UAE’s role as a haven for hostile state activity – Middle East Monitor James Moules, Politics Home , September 9, Labour Government Did Not Pursue Legal Advice On Uyghur Genocide Despite Pre-Election Pledge Abdurehim Gheni Uyghur, Union of Catholic Asian News , September 9, A world that commemorates the dead but fails to save the living Amnesty International, September 8, Kazakhstan: Detained activists need urgent medical care Uyghur News Network, September 5, The Uyghur Story Missing From Zhu Rongji’s Obituaries Tahir Imin, Uyghur Times , September 4, First-Generation Uyghur Archaeologist Abduqeyum Khoja Dies at 85 in Urumqi Tweets by UyghurProject

https://montenegro.osce.org/news/mission.body: News News Item OSCE strengthens capacities in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and Serbia through regional forged document training-of-trainers Issued on: 25 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Montenegro Fields of work: Policing From 21 to 25 September, the OSCE Transnational Threats Department, in close co-operation with the OSCE Missions to Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH), Montenegro and, Serbia, held a regional training-of-trainers (ToT) course on detecting forged documents and impostors at border crossing points. Hosted at the Police Cooperation Centre in Trebinje, BiH, the course brought together 18 experienced border police officers and forensic document experts from BiH, Montenegro and Serbia to strengthen their technical expertise and build their capacity as trainers, ensuring the long-term transfer of skills within their national border police services. Delivered by experts from BiH and Serbia, the programme combined theory, hands-on exercises with genuine and forged specimens, peer learning, and participants’ presentations to build their confidence in training their colleagues. Sessions covered practical detection skills, including substrate analysis, security printing techniques, recognition of printing methods and document evaluation under realistic conditions. The regional focus reflects the ongoing threat of document forgery and identity fraud in South-Eastern Europe, where counterfeit and fraudulently obtained travel documents continue to facilitate migrant smuggling, trafficking in human beings and other forms of organized crime. Strengthening frontline officers' ability to detect such fraud is key to disrupting criminal networks and enhancing security and stability across South-Eastern Europe and the wider OSCE area. With 18 participants trained as trainers, the course is designed to multiply its impact, equipping national border police services to extend detection skills to a much wider group of frontline officers. Since 2015, the OSCE Transnational Threats Department has delivered a series of similar ToT courses across the region, helping to standardise detection procedures at border crossings. “I am confident that participants will leave this training with practical, hands-on skills for verifying document authenticity and detecting forgeries and impostors, which they can apply immediately and pass on to colleagues through future courses they deliver themselves,” said Slobodan Krstić, a trainer and retired member of the BiH Border Police. “Bringing together border police from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, and Montenegro also creates a valuable opportunity to exchange experiences and build a regional network of trainers in this field.” The course concluded with the handover of certificates, marking participants' readiness to serve as national trainers and roll out training to frontline officers across the region in 2026-2027, supported by follow-up mentoring for sustained impact. This event is part of a series of activities on the detection of forged travel documents and impostors organized by the OSCE Border Security and Management Unit across the OSCE region since 2015. Since 2015, the OSCE Transnational Threats Department has delivered a series of similar ToT courses across the region, helping to standardise detection procedures at border crossings. “I am confident that participants will leave this training with practical, hands-on skills for verifying document authenticity and detecting forgeries and impostors, which they can apply immediately and pass on to colleagues through future courses they deliver themselves,” said Slobodan Krstić, a trainer and retired member of the BiH Border Police. “Bringing together border police from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, and Montenegro also creates a valuable opportunity to exchange experiences and build a regional network of trainers in this field.” The course concluded with the handover of certificates, marking participants' readiness to serve as national trainers and roll out training to frontline officers across the region in 2026-2027, supported by follow-up mentoring for sustained impact. This event is part of a series of activities on the detection of forged travel documents and impostors organized by the OSCE Border Security and Management Unit across the OSCE region since 2015.

https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/9.body: Listen (3 mins) Save Share UAE bars Iranian airlines as US sanctions squeeze Iran’s aviation sector on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google A flight information board at Imam Khomeini international airport in Tehran, Iran, on September 23, 2026 [Vahid Salemi/AP Photo] By Al Jazeera Staff , AFP and Reuters Published On 25 Sep 2026 25 Sep 2026 The United Arab Emirates has halted flights operated by Iranian airlines, joining several other countries in adopting United States sanctions aimed at pressuring Tehran’s aviation sector. On Thursday, a statement carried by the Emirati WAM news agency said, “The General Civil Aviation Authority announced the suspension of all flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the UAE.” It said the decision was “based on the US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines preventing them from using airports around the world ”. The UAE has joined Oman, Iraq, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkmenistan in restricting or suspending access for Iranian airlines amid the new US sanctions threat. Dubai, the UAE’s commercial hub, is a major destination for Iranian carriers, with multiple daily flights, a large Iranian community and close business links. An Iran Airtour flight from Tehran to Dubai was cancelled shortly before its scheduled departure on Thursday morning, after tickets had already been issued, according to the AFP news agency. The UAE, which was repeatedly hit by Iranian missiles and drones throughout the US-Israel war on Iran, suspended trade and financial exchanges with Iran last month. On Wednesday, the UAE’s central bank blocked transactions involving Iran’s Bank Melli, claiming the financial institution had violated rules on money laundering, terrorism and arms proliferation. The US Treasury announced sweeping sanctions on Iran’s aviation sector earlier this month, targeting 27 airlines and dozens of companies that support them. The measures aim to cut off Iran’s air links entirely, warning that any airport or company still servicing Iranian carriers risks being cut off from the US dollar system. Advertisement Iran’s Civil Aviation Organization spokesman Majid Akhavan said: “Diplomatic and aviation talks are under way to remove the restrictions and restore flights” to the UAE. Akhavan added that Turkmenistan also turned back a flight from Tehran to Dushanbe on Thursday. “Turkmenistan’s refusal to allow the Iranian aircraft to pass through its airspace meant the flight could not continue on its route and had to return,” Akhavan told the Iranian IRNA news agency. Several smaller Iranian airlines continue flying to China and Armenia, both of which have resisted US pressure, while routes to Turkiye remain open for some carriers.

https://uhrp.org/news/when-xi-visits-was.body: When Xi Visits Washington, Trump Must Raise China’s ‘Ethnic Unity’ Law - Uyghur Human Rights Project Skip to content When Xi Visits Washington, Trump Must Raise China’s ‘Ethnic Unity’ Law September 22, 2026 | The Diplomat | Omer Kanat When Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington on September 24, the agenda will be crowded: trade, technology, fentanyl, Taiwan, and global security. But there is another issue that the United States cannot afford to leave out: China’s newly adopted Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress. U.S. President Donald Trump should raise a question that goes to the heart of American sovereignty: Why are Uyghur Americans being forced to choose between exercising their freedoms here and protecting their relatives from retaliation in China? The Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress was passed by China’s National People’s Congress in March and took effect July 1. Beijing presents it as a measure to promote harmony among China’s ethnic groups. Uyghurs, Tibetans, Southern Mongolians, and others know better. The law does not protect unity; it codifies the forced assimilation campaigns our communities have long experienced. Since 2017, the Chinese government has waged a systematic campaign to extinguish Uyghur national identity, religion, and cultural life. With the ethnic unity law, Beijing has codified and expanded this assault. Americans must pay particular attention to the law’s reach beyond China’s borders. Article 63 of the law says organizations and individuals outside China can be held legally responsible for actions deemed to “undermine ethnic unity and progress or create ethnic division.” China’s vice justice minister openly defended this overseas provision as “legitimate, lawful, necessary, and feasible.” Article 10 asserts that foreign entities “using excuses such as ethnicity, religion, or human rights to insult and disparage, contain and suppress, or infiltrate and undermine the PRC are to be resolutely opposed.” That is an unmistakable message to Uyghurs, Tibetans, Hong Kongers, and other communities: Beijing claims the right to police our identities even outside its borders. But it is also a threat to all Americans, even those without family ties in China. Any person who expresses a view China deems as contrary to ethnic unity can be targeted under the new law. These risks are not hypothetical. As I wrote last month, Uyghurs abroad already feel its impact. Since the law went into effect, families have stopped sending their children to Uyghur language schools out of fear of retaliation by Chinese authorities. People who live thousands of miles from China are asking whether a speech, a social media post, a cultural event, or even a private act of faith could put family members back home in danger. This is how transnational repression works. The Chinese government does not need to arrest every Uyghur activist living in the United States or Europe. It only needs to create an atmosphere of fear. It only needs people to believe that what they do abroad may have consequences for themselves or their loved ones. That is why this law is not only a human rights issue, it is an immediate challenge to U.S. sovereignty. Other governments have spoken out. Australia reportedly raised concerns with Beijing. Members of the European Parliament called for the law’s repeal. U.N. experts warned that it risks entrenching forced assimilation and expanding transnational repression. But the United States, which formally recognized China’s treatment of Uyghurs as genocide and is home to several prominent Uyghur civil society organizations, has not clearly condemned the law. Trump should raise the ethnic unity law directly with Xi and make clear that attempts to enforce it against people in the United States will not be tolerated. No foreign government has the right to determine what people living in America or in any democratic societies say, believe, teach their children, or advocate for. Washington should say clearly that China’s “ethnic unity” law stops at America’s borders. Read the op-ed in The Diplomat : https://thediplomat.com/2026/09/when-xi-visits-washington-trump-must-raise-chinas-ethnic-unity-law/ Tweets by UyghurProject

https://hrf.org/latest/venezuela-digital.body: @HRF View post HRF condemns Delcy Rodríguez’s regime for continuing to weaponize state censorship and political repression in Venezuela. The regime continues to block more than 200 digital domains, including 65 independent news outlets. As local NGO @vesinfiltro noted, ending this blackout requires no legal reforms — only the political will to order internet service providers to lift the blocks immediately. Digital censorship is just one layer of a continued, systematic pattern of repression and control. @CNPcaracas registered 134 attacks against journalists and media outlets between January and July, including 23 arbitrary detentions, 15 deportations of foreign correspondents, and 4 station shutdowns. Furthermore, state security forces under minister Diosdado Cabello have routinely harassed and intimidated reporters to prevent them from documenting critical events, including the aftermath of the earthquakes. Despite promises of reform, the regime’s repressive apparatus remains fully intact and operational. UN High Commissioner Volker Türk ( @UNHumanRights ) expressed concern that human rights violations and reports of torture in detention centers persist. Meanwhile, @ForoPenal confirmed that at least 328 political prisoners remain arbitrarily detained in Venezuela, enduring severe conditions even as official channels routinely inflate release numbers. While HRF welcomes the release of political prisoners, true freedom cannot be conditional. Releasing individuals under heavy judicial restrictions, travel bans, and ongoing court presentations — only to re-arrest others through a continuous “revolving door” mechanism — is a tactic to silence dissent. Democracies, and the United States in particular, must not be deceived by partial releases: They must demand an immediate end to censorship, the dismantling of the repressive state apparatus, and the unconditional release of all political prisoners. https://www.fidh.org/en/en/region/europe.body: 18/09/2026 Press release Turkey LGBTQI+ rights KEMAL ASLAN / AFP In Turkey, LGBTI+ associations and venues frequented by the community were hit by a wave of police raids and arrests. These operations are part of an ongoing campaign from the authorities, with explicitly discriminatory aims and justifications, in contradiction with international law. 18 September, 2026. In Turkey since this past weekend, the authorities have launched waves of police raids targeting the LGBTI+ community, amid a vast campaign dubbed " Ailem Güvende " (in english " my family is safe "). At least 116 people have been detained as part of these operations, 44 of them LGBTI+ rights defenders and at least 82 have since been remanded in pre-trial detention. The majority of those arrested are trans women, charged with a combination of prostitution, drug and obscenity offences as well as violations of the Law on Associations. At least 125 additional people were detained across Ankara, Istanbul and Izmir following protests in support of the initial victims of the crackdown. Solidarity with LGBTI+ communities has also been censored through restrictions on the social media accounts of journalists and activists. The International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), and its member organisation in Turkey, İnsan Hakları Derneği (IHD), denounce in the strongest terms these arrests and demand the immediate dropping of all prosecutions based on discriminatory accusations. They urge international actors to react strongly to Turkey’s broader anti LGBTI+ turn and its infringement of international human rights law, including freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly (United Nations, Council of Europe), as well as its political commitments (European Union-EU accession) and economic commitments (Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development-OECD standards and policies). " Faced with these unacceptable violations, and with no prospect of any backing down nor reparations from the authorities, the EU must firmly acknowledge Turkey’s incompatibility with the values of the Union and therefore place an indefinite hold on its accession process by immediately stopping the pre-accession funding, " commented Alexis Deswaef, FIDH President . Turkey has seen a sustained erosion of freedoms of expression, association, and peaceful assembly in recent years , with LGBTI+ people and organisations among the primary targets . " Obscenity " and " child protection " laws have been weaponized to effectively criminalise LGBTI+ people’s existence. Pressures on civil society are rampant, with surveillance, police and judicial harassment, political banning and dissolutions enacted on any opposition, real or perceived. The LGBTI+ community has become a regular fixation for Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, who recently pronounced the next ten years as the " Decade of Family and Population ". No concept of " family values " should be used as a tool to justify an ever increasingly authoritarian and conservative power in Turkey. FIDH and IHD urge Turkish authorities to immediately release all individuals detained in the framework of this operation and to put an end to the criminalisation of LGBTI+ civil society. They call on international actors, in particular the European Union, the Council of Europe and United Nations mechanisms, to firmly condemn the raids and detentions carried out by Turkish authorities. 22/09/2026 Press release France en fa fr Syria National courts RICCARDO MILANI / HANS LUCAS / HANS LUCAS VIA AFP Following the conviction of Sabri Essid for genocide and crimes against humanity, the Paris Criminal Court has issued an important ruling on the civil claims, formally recognising the harm suffered by the civil parties and awarding them damages. This financial reparation will unfortunately remain very symbolic. Paris, 22 September 2026. Six months after the historic conviction of French Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) fighter Sabri Essid (alias Abou Dojanah al-Faransi), the Paris Criminal Court has issued its decision on the civil claims, providing judicial recognition of the lifelong and multifaceted harm suffered by the survivors of the Yazidi genocide. On 20 March 2026, Sabri Essid was sentenced in absentia to life imprisonment for genocide, crimes against humanity and complicity in these crimes, committed in Syria between August 2014 and throughout 2016 against Yazidi women and children. This marked the first conviction of a French national for genocide, as well as the first time that a French court addressed the atrocities committed by ISIS against the Yazidi community. In its decision on the civil claims, the Court formally recognised the extent of the harm inflicted by Sabri Essid on the three Yazidi women and their eight children, including the damage arising from the fear of impending death (prejudice d’angoisse de mort imminente), the loss of affection (prejudice d’affection) and the moral damage (préjudice moral), and granted them financial awards. The Court also acknowledged the moral damage suffered by the Yazidi associations that joined the proceedings as civil parties – Kinyat, the Free Yezidi Foundation (FYF) and Yazda – as well as by the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) and the Ligue des droits de l’Homme/droits humains (LDH) and awarded them one symbolic euro. In practice, these financial awards will unfortunately remain largely symbolic. As Sabri Essid has never been located, the victims cannot claim compensation from him. Additionally, under the current French legal framework, foreign victims of international crimes committed abroad are not eligible for compensation from the Commission d’indemnisation des victimes d’infractions (CIVI). " There can be no meaningful justice without effective reparation. Although this is an important decision, it will remain symbolic as French law does not allow foreign victims to have equal access to compensation mechanisms and to effectively benefit from reparations awarded by the courts, in cases where the accused is not present or solvent, " declared the five civil party associations . https://adcmemorial.org/en/news/followin.body: Facebook Twitter Вконтакте On October 14, 2026, Anti-Discrimination Centre Memorial Brussels organises a side event during the annual Warsaw Human Dimension Conference of the OSCE (Warsaw, Sofitel Victoria Hotel, Saski room, 16:00–17:00 CET). Anti-Discrimination Centre Memorial (Brussels) proposes to integrate the human rights approach into the ongoing discussion among many indigenous activists on the idea of overcoming Russian colonial oppression, guaranteeing the cultural, economic, environmental and political rights of each group. While there are sound voices of the peoples of the Caucasus, the Urals and Siberia insisting on the future as independent national republics based on the cultural and political heritage of the local peoples, there are also concerns about the rights of other groups living on the same territories – such as small-numbered Indigenous peoples and other minorities. Most anti-colonial activists agree that the future political models should be democratic and inclusive. However, the question is how to ensure non-discrimination and equity, how to protect the rights of those who can’t form an independent state, but need their rights to be realised within those future new political subjects? Another burning question would be – how to solve the existing problem of Russian domination (language, political and economic resources, ideas of the past and historical heritage)? What examples of the European historical past should be considered or could serve as a warning against too radical (even violent in some cases) approach? The 20th century showed many waves of politically dominated relocation of ethnic groups: Soviet repressions against peoples and later their efforts to get back to their native territories; German attempts to replace the population of the occupied lands, that ended with the exile in 1945 of millions of Germans from some parts of Central Europe; among other examples one can think of Polish and Ukrainian (Soviet) treaty of 1944 and the 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey. Maybe thinking of the relevant cases of the past century, trying to avoid the mistakes and prevent the crimes could help to plan a non-discriminating and inclusive future, and bring the idea of human rights protection as the most necessary element to these actual discussions. These issues will be discussed by representatives of the Indigenous rights movement with human rights experts at the side event of ADC Memorial Brussels. Speakers: Ruslan Valiev , Aspects of Bashkortostan Maria Ochir-Goryaeva , historian, decolonial activist from the Republic of Kalmykia Tavlan Salpagarov , Indigenous Peoples Global Unity (via Zoom) Viacheslav Shadrin , expert on the Indigenous peoples’ rights, representative of Yukaghir Indigenous people (via Zoom) Natalia Sineaeva-Pankowska , “Never Again” Association Co-moderators: Stephania Kulaeva (ADC Memorial Brussels) and Ruslan Valiev (Aspects of Bashkortostan) Date: 14 October 2026, 16:00-17:00 CET Location: Warsaw, hotel Sofitel Victoria, room Saski Languages: The event will be held in Russian and English, with simultaneous interpretation. Refreshments and beverages will be provided. The side event will be organized as part of the project “Indigenous Peoples’ Rights for a Democratic Future”, which is being implemented by INFOE (Institut für Ökologie und Aktions-Ethnologie e.V.), ICIPR (International Committee of Indigenous Peoples of Russia), the Never Again Association and the ADC Memorial, with the support of the German Federal Foreign Office. https://adcmemorial.org/en/news/witnesse.body: Facebook Twitter Вконтакте Elie Wiesel , a survivor of Auschwitz and Buchenwald and the author of the well-known autobiographical novel Night, wrote that “only those who experienced Auschwitz know what it was; the rest will never know.” As Wiesel saw it, “the witness knew then, as he knows now,” that his experience could not be conveyed or fully comprehended by those who had not been in a concentration camp and had not endured torture and humiliation. The author of the testimony asks: “Others will not know, but will they be able to understand?” And yet, despite his doubts, Wiesel “simply could not remain silent.” Reflecting on the destruction of European Jewry by the German Nazis, Wiesel concludes that over the years not only the actions but also the aims of the antisemites changed: if at the beginning of their rule the Nazis set themselves the task of “building a society without Jews,” towards the end they wanted “to leave behind a world in which Jews seemed never to have existed at all.” Violence against people — Jewish men, women and children — was accompanied by the destruction of the very memory of this people, their culture, language and religion. For many witnesses, the struggle against the destruction of memory became the purpose of their lives, an act of resistance. Contemporary antifascists often repeat that “to remember means to resist,” holding events in memory of comrades killed by neo-Nazis. “Memory Is Resistance” is the slogan on the website of members of Memorial who study the history of political repression in the USSR and preserve testimonies of the horrors of the Soviet past. Memory matters to everyone: both to those who refuse to let themselves or others forget the crimes of the past and the suffering of the victims, and to those who take pride in that past. It is not simply a matter of knowing something — Wiesel was right about that — achieving understanding is much more difficult. We can see how declared aims and ideological attitudes continue to change in our own time. From “Holocaust denial” — until quite recently, apologists for German nationalism claimed that Jews had not been exterminated and had themselves invented both the camps and the crematoria in order to slander innocent Germans (there were even claims that Jews themselves had organised the mass murder of Jews to spite the Aryans) — to contemporary proposals by Alternative for Germany not to teach about Hitlerism in schools and instead devote more attention to Bismarck. Germany’s far-right politicians are now closer to the cynical attitude: “Here’s your beer, here’s your ham, and what happened yesterday is in the past” (the ever-relevant words of a song by Yuliy Kim). No one is saying that it did not happen: it did. The only question is how to regard it, how to understand it. The militarist and nationalist Bismarck is, for the AfD, something good, something to take pride in, while schoolchildren need not be told about certain costs of twentieth-century history: enough already, so much has been said about it. The lavish funeral held in Belgrade with military honours for Ratko Mladić, convicted by the Hague Tribunal of crimes against humanity, is a striking manifestation of the contemporary conflict over memory: for some, the victims and witnesses of crimes matter; for others, what matters is the glorification of war criminals. Everyone wants to remember — but they remember different things and understand the past differently. Those who are erecting ever more monuments to Stalin in the Russian Federation obviously want to remind people of him, often making no attempt to conceal the fact that Stalinism was terror. They simply like terror and want to put it back on a pedestal. And they are prepared to remember the Gulag as well — not to deny its existence, but to explain it in their own way, interpreting it within the framework of the “inadmissibility of distorting the history of the USSR.” Thus, for example, one can hold an academic conference in a former Soviet camp, highlighting “examples of the extraordinary courage and patriotism of our compatriots, whose military and labour achievements have more than once become a central theme of academic conferences organised for ten years by the Perm-36 Museum-Reserve.” But telling the history of the Stalinist era as it was seen by those who survived despite the terror, those who neither forgot nor forgave, is treated as extremism. This is why Memorial was banned and the Gulag History Museum in Moscow was closed. It is not memory that is forbidden — it is understanding that is forbidden, precisely what Elie Wiesel and many others sought to achieve through their testimonies. The struggle to foster an understanding that terror and war crimes are unacceptable does not end even when a verdict has been handed down by the Hague (or Nuremberg) Tribunal. Constant efforts are required not only to prevent people from forgetting, but also to show history — including the most recent history — through the eyes of victims of violence, those who suffered, and surviving witnesses. To show their truth rather than the perpetrator’s version: the perpetrator who does not even conceal what he is doing — who may even take pride in it — but who always has an explanation of his own, most often that he was forced to “strike first,” to assert his right to dominance, and so on. The perpetrators themselves are also eager to preserve the memory of violence — in military monuments, bas-reliefs and installations. The voices of those who suffered can be heard in their memories, accounts and testimonies, which must be collected and published, as is being done today by the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group’s “Voices of War” project and in human rights reports , which bring together the tragic experiences of Ukrainian women and men who have suffered as a result of Russia’s military aggression. Stephania KULAEVA First published on the Radio Svoboda blog Facebook Twitter Вконтакте

Бұған ресми сот істері дәлел. Заңсыз темекі Қазақстанға қайдан әкелініп жатыр? Миллиондаған қорап темекі тәркіленіп жатса да, неге базарларда заңсыз өнім ашық сатылып жатыр? Азаттық кемі төрт базарға барып көрді. Онда 20 тал темекіден тұратын бір қорап 450-500 теңгеден сатылып жатыр. Сыртында ешқандай акциз маркасы жоқ. Мұндай өнім – заңға қайшы. Қазақстанда темекіге қойылған шекті баға бар. Биыл 1 тамыздан бастап Қаржы министрлігі бекіткен 20 тал темекінің ең төмен бағасы – 1060 теңге. Яғни, дүкенде заңды түрде сатылатын бір қорап темекі құны осыдан арзан болмауға тиіс. Алматыда көргеніміз бір базар не қалаға ғана тән жағдай емес. Қазақстанның басқа өңірлеріндегі базарлардан да заңсыз айналымдағы темекі оңай табылады. Бұған блогер Кирилл Павловтың көзі жеткен. Ол Шымкент, Тараз, Ақтөбе, Қарағанды, Петропавл, Көкшетау сияқты тағы басқа ірі қалалардың орталық базарларын аралаған. Темекінің заңсыз айналымда екенін арзан бағасына және штрих кодына қарап білуге болады. Ол үшін Egov mobile қосымшасына кіріп, сондағы Naqty onim деген қызмет арқылы тексеруге мүмкіндік бар. Кез келген темекіде штрих код болады. Сол кодты сканерлейтін болсаңыз қолыңыздағы темекі туралы барлық ақпарат – өнімнің шыққан жері, тауар коды, бәрі шығады. Ал сыртындағы штрих код арқылы тексерген кезде ешқандай ақпарат шықпаса, онда бұл күмәнді өнім, демек, нарықта заңсыз сатылып жатыр деген сөз. Азаттық сөйлескен саудагерлер тауарды қайдан әкелінгенін нақты білмейміз дейді. Ешбірі видеоға не аудиотаспаға сұхбат беруге келіспеді. Тек ауызекі әңгімеде ғана кейбір сұраққа жауап берді. Кейбірі оның қайдан әкеленетінін білмейтінін айтады. Оларға делдалдар әкеліп, көтерме бағамен сатады. Мысалы, олар бір қорап темекіні базарда 500 теңгеге сатып тұрса, "делдалдан 250-300 теңгеден аламыз" дейді. Ал тағы бір саудагердің айтуынша, тауар базардың артқы жағына жүк көлігімен жеткізіледі, сол жерден блогын 3300–4000 теңгеге сатып алады. Оны өздері 5000-5500 теңгеге сатады. Салыстыру үшін айтайық, Алматы базарларында заңды өнім сатып тұрған дүкендерде ең арзан темекінің бір блогы 11 мың теңге тұрады. ҚЫРҒЫЗСТАН АРҚЫЛЫ ЖЕТЕТІН КҮМӘНДІ ӨНІМ Көтерме бағамен сауда жасайтындар тауар Қырғызстан жақтан келетінін айтты. Заңсыз айналымдағы темекі нарығын зерттеп жүрген блогер Кирилл Павловтың сөзінше, қазір Қазақстанның оңтүстік өңірлерінде заңсыз сатылып жатқан темекі өнімдері негізінен Қырғызстан шекарасы арқылы өтіп келеді. – Мендегі ақпарат бойынша, Қырғызстан – бұл өнімді ірі көлемде көтерме сататын тарап қана. Ең танымал сауда маркасы – Oris. Оған қатысты "Біріккен Араб Әмірліктерінен келеді" деген аңыз бар, бірақ бұл шындыққа жанаспайды. Біздің Жамбыл облысының шекарасында бауырлас елмен арадағы өткізу бекеттерінде ұсталған тауарларға қатысты жағдайларды көріп жүрміз. Онда әлсін-әлсін осы өнім қораптардың арасынан немесе жасырын орындардан табылып жатады. Біздегі мәлімет бойынша, бұл өнім бізге дәл Қырғызстанмен шекара арқылы заңсыз жолмен өтіп келеді. Мұны талдау деректері де растайды. Көтерме сауда бойынша ұсыныстардың барлығы негізінен Қордай, Қарасу сияқты шекараға жақын елді мекендерде шоғырланған. Ал нарықтағы ең үлкен үлес, қалай болғанда да оңтүстік өңірлерге тиесілі: Алматы қаласы, Алматы облысы, Жетісу, Жамбыл және Түркістан облыстары, – дейді агросарапшы, блогер Кирилл Павлов. Контрабандалық жолмен тасымалданған темекі өнімдері (көрнекі сурет) Кейінгі уақыттағы Қырғызстандағы қылмыстық істер де бұл бағытта заңсыз тасымал барын көрсетеді. Былтыр Қырғызстанның Ұлттық қауіпсіздік жөніндегі мемлекеттік комитеті (ҰҚМК) бірнеше жылдан бері заңсыз әрекетпен айналысқан трансұлттық топты анықтады. Қырғыз билігінің мәліметінше, осы топ өткізген темекілер кейін Қазақстан аумағында кеден төлемінсіз сатылған. Ал биыл 16 мамырда Қырғызстанның ҰҚМК шетелде өндірілген темекі өнімдерін контрабандалық жолмен тасымалдаған топты ұстады. Іске қатысы бар адамдардың арасында Шекара қызметінің өкілдері болған. Базарларда көзге түскен Oris, Zumerret маркалы темекілердің қаптамасында "Біріккен Араб Әмірліктерінде жасалған" деген жазу бар. Ашық ақпаратқа қарағанда, аталған темекі маркаларының зауыттары Дубайда орналасқан. Алайда нақты Қырғызстан шекарасы арқылы өткен бұл темекілер Дубайда емес, басқа елде астыртын цехта жасалады деген ақпарат бар. Бұған қазақстандық қауымдастық жүргізген зерттеу жанама дәлел. Олар елдің Қырғызстанмен шекаралас аймағында тәркіленген темекінің көшірме өнім екенін анықтаған. Зерттеуді Қазақстандағы Адам денсаулығына қауіпті факторларының зиянын азайту жөніндегі ұлттық "Денсаулық" қауымдастығының тапсырысымен "Бүкілресейлік темекі өнімдерін ғылыми-зерттеу институты жүргізген. Олар Oris, Zumerret маркалы темекілерден сынама алып, физика-химиялық сараптама жасаған. Сынамаға берілген темекі үлгілері "заңсыз өндірілген, фальсификат өнім" деп танылған. Зертхана қорытындысына сәйкес, бұл темекілер Кеден одағының техникалық регламентінің оннан астам міндетті талабын бұзған. Oris үлгісінің құрамында хлордың мөлшері 1,5% екені анықталды, яғни қалыпты мөлшерден екі еседей көп. Бұл көрсеткіш темекінің сапасыз, химиялық жолмен өңделген арзан шикізаттан және астыртын цехтарда жасалғанының басты дәлелі. Заңды өндірілген Oris-те бұл көрсеткіш – 0,7%. Халықаралық стандарт бойынша, жалпы темекідегі хлор мөлшері 1%-дан аспағаны жөн. Ал Zumerret темекісінде сүзгінің желдету саңылауы жабық екені анықталды. Тексерілген үлгілердегі желдету көрсеткіші 4%-дан 34%-ға дейін болған. Ол темекінің зиян заттарды ұстап қалу деңгейі төмен дегенді білдіреді. Қаржы мониторинг агенттігі тәркіленген темекі өнімдері негізінен қай елде өндірілетінін айта алмады. Азаттыққа берген жауабында "өндіруші елдер қылмыстық тергеп-тексеру шеңберінде, сот сараптамаларын тағайындау арқылы анықталады" деп қысқа қайырған. Oris маркалы темекінің бірнеше түрі бар. Қаржы мониторинг агенттігінің дерегінше, Oris-тің бүгінге кейін кемі алты түрі тәркіленген. Олардың қаптамасында "Біріккен Араб Әмірліктерінде жасалған. Сауда маркасының Германиядағы иесімен келісім негізінде шығарылған" деп жазылған. Қаржы мониторингі агенттігі тәркілеген темекі маркаларының географиясы кең. Бейсенбіде теңізден құтқарылған үш әскери қызметкердің біреуі қазір ауруханада жатыр, дәрігерлер оның өміріне қауіп жоқ дейді. Қазақстан президенті Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаев Каспий теңізіндегі әскери оқу-жаттығу кезінде қаза тапқан әскери қызметшілердің отбасына көңіл айтып, 25 қыркүйекті Каспийде қаза тапқан жауынгерлерді аза тұту күні деп жариялады. Қайғылы оқиғаның жай-жапсарын тексеріп, қаза тапқан жауынгерлердің отбасына жәрдемдесу үшін премьер-министрдің орынбасары Қанат Бозымбаев жетекшілік ететін үкімет комиссиясы құрылды . Жұма күні Алматыда Тоқаев қатысқан Қазақстан-Қытай форумына жиналған жұрт марқұм сарбаздарды бір минут үнсіз еске алды деп хабарлады мемлекеттік басылымдар. Қайғылы оқиғаға байланысты экс-президент Нұрсұлтан Назарбаев та мәлімдеме жасап, марқұмдардың туған-туыстарына көңіл айтты. 25 қыркүйекте Бас прокуратура Маңғыстау облысында оқу-жаттығу кезінде әскери қызметкерлердің қаза табуына байланысты қозғалған іс бойынша күдіктілер анықталып, тергеу жүріп жатқанын мәлімдеді. Каспий теңізіндегі "Хазар қорғаны-2026" оқу-жаттығу жиыны. 21 қыркүйек, 2026 жыл. Көп адамның өліміне себеп болған оқиғаға байланысты Қылмыстық кодекстің "Қызметке салғырт қарау" және "Кеме жүргізу қағидаларын бұзу" баптары бойынша қылмыстық іс қозғалып, ведомствоаралық жедел-тергеу тобы құрылған. "Қызметке салғырт қарады деп күдік келтірілген, сондай-ақ метеорологиялық жағдайларды ескере отырып, жеке құрамның қауіпсіздігін қамтамасыз ету үшін тиісті бақылау мен қажетті шаралардың қабылдануын қамтамасыз етпеген, құтқару жұмыстарын тиісінше ұйымдастырмаған, соның салдарынан адамдардың қаза болуына әкеп соққан лауазымды тұлғалар анықталды. Тергеу барлық күдіктінің әрекеттеріне толық құқықтық баға беріп, оларға қатысты процестік шаралар қабылдайды" делінген Бас прокуратура таратқан ақпаратта. Жұма күні түске қарай ішкі істер министрлігі сарбаздар қазасына байланысты елдің әскери-теңіз күштері қолбасшысының бірінші орынбасары – штаб бастығы, екі әскери бөлім командирі, теңіз жаяу әскері ротасының және "Қайсар" қатерінің командирлері – барлығы бес адам ұсталғанын хабарлады . "Қайсар" қандай катер? "Қайсар" катері (борт нөмері 102). "Қайсар" катеріне 17-19 адам сияды. Ресейдегі "Рыбинская верфь" зауытында жасалған. Қазақстан теңіз әскерінің Ақтаудағы бөлімшесінде 2023 жылдан бері бар. "Қайсар" жоғары жылдамдықпен жүретін десанттық броньдалған катер. 80 км/сағ жылдамдыққа дейін барады.16-18 метр болатын катерді жағалауды қадағалауға, диверсиялық операцияларға, теңіз шекарасын бұзғандар мен табиғатқа зиян келтіргендерді ұстауға, десанттарды түсіруге және әскерилерді тасымалдауға қолданылады. Прокуратура қайғылы оқиғаға байланысты 30-дан астам әскери қызметкерден жауап алынып, 12 сараптама тағайындалғанын хабарлады. Бұған дейін Қазақстанның қорғаныс министрлігі 22 қыркүйекте Каспий теңізінің қазақстандық бөлігінде "Хазар қорғаны-2026" оқу-жаттығуы басталғанын, 500-ден аса әскери қызметші, әскери кеме экипаждары, жағалау бөлімшелері, ҰҚК шекара қызметінің жағалау күзеті, әуе қорғанысы күштері қатысып жатқан жаттығуларға әскери-теңіз күштерінің бас қолбасшысы, бірінші дәрежелі капитан Қанат Ниязбеков басшылық ететінін хабарлаған.Ақпарат құралдарының жазуынша, төтенше оқиға болған бейсенбі күні теңізде толқын күшейіп, жағалау маңында қатты жел тұрған. Теңізде хабар-ошарсыз кеткен адамдарды іздеу-құтқару жұмыстарына ауа райының қолайсыздығы кедергі келтірген . "ЖҮЙЕЛІ ТҮРДЕ ҚАЙТАЛАНАТЫН ҚАСІРЕТ" Жергілікті медиа мен блогерлер қаза тапқан жауынгерлердің көбі – әскер қатарына Маңғыстау облысынан шақырылған азаматтар деп хабарлады. Кейбірінің әскери қызмет борышын өтеуді аяқтауына санаулы күн қалған. Кейбірінің тойы да белгіленіп қойған деп жазды басылымдар. Қоғамда әскери басшылық пен билік органдарының қайғылы оқиға кезіндегі іс-әрекетіне сын айтып, наразы пікір білдіріп жатқандар аз емес. Олар ауа райын болжау қызметінің алдын ала ескертуіне қарамастан, қатты жел мен толқын тұрған күні бес қаруын түгел асынған жауынгерлерге теңізге түсуді бұйырған деп әскери басшылықты кінәлап жатыр. "Өкінішке қарай, мұндай қасірет бір рет қана болған жайт емес, жүйелі түрде қайталанатын болды" деді Азаттыққа пікір білдірген адамдардың бірі: Embed Бөлісіңіз «Қорғаныс министрі жауап беруі керек». Ақжол міндетті әскери борышын өтеуді биыл күзде аяқтап, қазан айының басында үйіне оралуы керек болған. Желіде кейбір адамдар президент Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаевты қаралы хабарды халыққа өзі айтпай, қарамағындағылардың біріне тапсырғаны үшін сынға алды. "Қатты кетсем ғафу өтінемін, бірақ неге сарбаздар қазасы мен аза тұту туралы президент емес, Бозымбаев хабарлайды? Неліктен адамдармен амандасуды үйрету, таза Қазақстан, заңдылық пен тәртіп, граффити жазу жайлы президент айтады да, көңіл айтуға келгенде бұған еш қатысы жоқ шенеунік шыға келеді? Құрметті мемлекет басшысы өз жоғарғы қолбасшылығы астында болып жатқан сұмдыққа назар аударуы үшін неше сарбаз өлуі керек?"деп жазды журналист, блогер Денис Кривошеев Facebook-парақшасына. Енді біреулер қорғаныс министрі мен жақында жаңадан тағайындалған вице-президент неге қара жамылған ата-аналарға барып, басу айтуға жарамаған деп сұрақ қойған. "Қорғаныс министрлігін түбегейлі реформалау қажет" деп жазды желі қолданушы Zhandos Iskakov . "Қаза бізге аяқ астынан келген жоқ. Бұл үнемі болатын жайт. Өйткені 11 жыл бұрын сарбаздар дәл осылай суға батып кеткенде ешкім ешқандай қорытынды жасаған жоқ. Өйткені әскери басшылық, 11 жыл бұрынғыдай, ауа райы болжамын елемеген" деп жазды журналист Динара Егеубаева. Қазақстан халқына шет мемлекеттер басшылары мен халықаралық ұйым өкілдері де көңіл айтып жатыр. Қорғаныс министрлігі қаза тапқан жауынгерлердің отбасына материалдық және психологиялық көмек көрсетіледі деп мәлімдеді. Елдегі бірнеше кәсіпкер марқұм болғандардың жақындарына көмек ретінде ақша аударып жатыр деп жазды жергілікті басылымдар. Қазақстандық боксшы Абылайхан Жүсіпов украиналық "Миротворец" сайтының базасына енгізілді. Бұл база Жүсіпов Геннадий Головкинді қолдады дейді. Жүсіпов бұған дейін "Халықаралық спорт ұйымының шешімін Головкиннің шешімі деп қарауға болмайды. Ресей спортшылардың туымен және әнұранымен жарысқа қатысу шешімі халықаралық ұйымның құзырында және Халықаралық олимпиада комитетінің ұсынысын ескеріліп қабылданады... Спорт адамдарды біріктіріп, достық пен сыйластықты насихаттауы керек, саяси құрал болмауы тиіс" деп жазған еді. "Миртворец" Жүсіповтің бұл жазбасын "Ресей нарративін қолдау" деп есептейді. Бұған дейін Қазақстан Ұлттық олимпиада комитетінің басшысы Геннадий Головкин де украиналық "Миротворец" сайтының базасына енгізілген . Бұған Головкин басқаратын World Boxing ұйымының ресейлік боксшыларға халықаралық жарыстарға Ресей туымен қатысуға рұқсат бергені себеп болған. "Миротворец" базасындағы жазбада Головкинге қатысты "Ресейдің Украинаға қарсы басқыншылығын және украин азаматтарын өлтіруін қолдады" деген анықтама берілген. Головкин де, Жүсіпов те "Миротворец" тізіміне енгені жайлы ешқандай пікір білдірген жоқ. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Геннадий Головкин украиналық "Миротворец" тізіміне енгізілді Тамыз айының басында халықаралық World Boxing федерациясы Ресей спортшыларына бұрын енгізілген барлық шектеулерді алып тастады. Енді Ресей боксшылары барлық жас санатында халықаралық турнирлерге ұлттық рәміздерімен қатыса алады. World Boxing 2028 жылғы Олимпиада ойындарында бокс жарысын ұйымдастырады. Ұйым мәлімдемесінде "атқарушы комитет ресейлік спортшылардың өзге ұлттық федерациялар өкілдерімен тең жағдайда жарысқа қатысатынын мойындады, алайда Ресей делегацияларының шаралар кезіндегі іс-әрекеті мен допингке қарсы талаптардың сақталуын қатаң бақылауда ұстайтын болады" делінген . Ресейдің спорт министрі әрі Ресей Олимпиада комитетінің басшысы Михаил Дегтярев әлеуметтік желіде бұл шешім қабылданғанға дейін Ташкентте Геннадий Головкинмен кездескенін жазды. Оның айтуынша, кездесуде екеуі ресейлік спортшыларды халықаралық аренаға қайтару мәселесін талқылаған. Биыл наурызда World Boxing ұйымының атқару кеңесі Ресей бокс федерациясын ұйымға мүше етіп қабылдауды мақұлдаған . Беларусь бокс федерациясына қатысты да осындай шешім қабылданды. "Миротворец" – 2014 жылдан бері жұмыс істейтін украиналық мемлекеттік емес ұйым. Сайт авторлары "Украинаның қауіпсіздігіне қарсы әрекеттерге қатысы бар" деп есептейтін адамдар жайлы, соғысты қолдайтындар туралы мәліметтер жариялап, тізімдеріне енгізеді. Сайттың ресми мәртебесі жоқ, алайда ол Украинаның құқық қорғау органдарының назарына ілінген тұлғалар жайлы ақпарат алмасатынымен де белгілі. Бұған дейін "Миротворец" базасына Қазақстанның бұрынғы парламенті мәжілісінің депутаты Айдос Сарым да енгізілген . Сайттағы ақпаратта Сарымның "Украинаны қолдаған Қазақстан азаматтарын қылмыстық жауапқа тартуға бағытталған әрекетті жария түрде насихаттағаны" және "Ресей пропагандасының нарративін" таратқаны жазылған . Сарымның өзі мұны "күлкілі жайт" деп атаған.
