https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1005316/%.body: سریال مهیج و پساآخرالزمانی هشتقسمتی «شهر خون» با انتشار یکجای تمام قسمتها، به پربینندهترین مجموعه تلویزیونی پلتفرم دیزنیپلاس در سطح جهانی تبدیل شد. پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات فرارو- در تداوم استقبال گسترده مخاطبان از ژانر پادآرمانشهری در سرویسهای آنلاین، پلتفرم پخش فیلم و سریال دیزنیپلاس با عرضه یک سریال جدید آلمانی، موفق به ثبت رکوردی جهانی در جدول پربینندهترین آثار نمایشی شد. به گزارش فرارو به نقل از اسکرین رنت، جدیدترین پدیده شبکه پخش آنلاین دیزنیپلاس موفق شده است هیجان و رونقی چشمگیر به فهرست آثار موفق سبک پادآرمانشهری در جهان ببخشد. عناوین ماوراءطبیعی، علمی-تخیلی و روایات پسا-رستاخیزی سالهاست که در سرویسهای مختلف پخش محتوا عملکردی درخشان از خود به جای میگذارند. پیش از این، شبکه اچبیاو مکس با اقتباس تلویزیونی بازی ویدئویی «آخرین بازمانده از ما» با هنرنمایی پدرو پاسکال به موفقیت بزرگی رسید. در سال ۲۰۲۶ نیز اپل تیوی پلاس با پخش فصل سوم سریال محبوب «سیلو» نشان داد کشش دراماتیک دنیاهای تاریک آینده همچنان گیرا و پرتنش است. علاوه بر این، عناوینی چون «فالاوت» از آمازون پرایم ویدیو و آثار پلتفرمهای هولو و دیزنیپلاس گواه جذابیت بیپایان این فضا هستند. در میان موفقیتهای متأخر ژانر، عناوینی نظیر اسپینآف «سرگذشت ندیمه» با نام «وصایا» و تریلر علمیتخیلی «پارادایز» توجه منتقدان را جلب کردهاند. در حالی که صنعت سرگرمی در سال ۲۰۲۶ منتظر اکران پروژههای شاخصی همچون سریال «بلید رانر ۲۰۹۹» است، دیزنیپلاس اکنون با معرفی مینیسریال اختصاصی و دلهرهآور «شهر خون» توانسته در رأس جدولهای بینالمللی قرار گیرد؛ موفقیتی که با انتشار همزمان تمام قسمتها تقویت شد. سریال آلمانی «شهر خون» در حال حاضر عنوان پربینندهترین اثر تلویزیونی دیزنیپلاس در جهان را به نام خود ثبت کرده است. این مجموعه هشتقسمتی در ۲۵ شهریور بهطور همزمان بر روی پلتفرمهای دیزنیپلاس و هولو بارگذاری شد تا علاقهمندان به تماشای ماراتنگونه دسترسی کاملی به داستان داشته باشند. وبسایت اسپیناف با دادن امتیاز ۳ از ۵ از تعلیق معمایی داستان تمجید کرده، در حالی که هیون آو هارور با اعطای امتیاز ۲ از ۵ از خردهروایتهای پراکنده آن انتقاد کرده است. با این همه، استقبال عمومی بسیار چشمگیر است. این اثر فراتر از رقبایی همچون سریال جنایی «خشمگین»، مجموعه مارولی «لوکی» و کمدی ورزشی «چد پاورز» قرار دارد. داستان «شهر خون» در جغرافیایی رقم میخورد که بحران ویرانگر دگرگونیهای اقلیمی نظم پیشین زمین را به هم ریخته است. سرزمینی سوزان که حرارت خفقانآور و جنایت گسترده بر آن سایه افکنده است. محور قصه بر سرنوشت دو خواهر متمرکز است که در سنین کودکی از یکدیگر جدا افتادهاند. یکی از آنها به نام «بئا» درون گنبدی مجلل و مجهز به سامانههای خنککننده در جمع طبقه اشراف بزرگ شده، در حالی که «فیبی» مجبور بوده برای بقا در خیابانهای بیرحم و دودگرفته برلین مبارزه کند. پیوند دوباره این دو خواهر با کشف رازی شوم گره میخورد: مدیریت پنهان کارتلهای تبهکاری شهر به دست خونآشامها اداره میشود؛ پیرنگی دلهرهآور که به نظر میرسد این موفقیت جهانی را تداوم خواهد بخشید. تبلیغات جزئیات سریال پساآخرالزمانی «شهر خون» کارگردان «مرد عنکبوتی» سراغ «جنگ ستارگان» رفت پشت پرده حاشیه «تهران پاریس تهران/ پل» امیر جعفری هم بعد از همسرش تغییر کرد؛ تغییر چشمگیر بازیگر سینما بیشتر بدانید: سریال مینی سریال تبلیغات نقد و بررسی سریال «گروگان آمریکایی» 'American Hostage' نقد و بررسی سریال آلمانی «ناآشنا» 'Unfamiliar' چرا مخاطب دیگر حوصله سریال ۳۰ قسمتی ندارد؟

https://www.amnesty.org/ru/latest/news/2.body: В опубликованном сегодня совместном заявлении группа из 21 организации гражданского общества, включая Amnesty International, призывает продлить мандат Миссии ООН по установлению фактов в Венесуэле (FFM) и отвечает на ключевые вопросы об этом специальном механизме ООН: что представляет собой FFM и почему её мандат необходимо сохранить по меньшей мере до 2028 года; как её работа дополняет деятельность Управления ООН по правам человека и международных механизмов правосудия; и, что особенно важно, какой вклад Миссия может внести в будущее Венесуэлы. Заявление последовало за интерактивным диалогом, состоявшимся 18 сентября 2026 года в Женеве в рамках продолжающейся 63-й сессии Совета ООН по правам человека (СПЧ), на котором FFM представила свои последние выводы. Несколько организаций гражданского общества выступили с устными заявлениями, призвав Совет продлить мандат Миссии ещё на два года. FFM пришла к выводу , что в Венесуэле продолжаются грубые нарушения прав человека и совершаются преступления по международному праву, при этом сохраняется безнаказанность. Миссия также обратила внимание на роль вооружённых групп гражданских лиц в проводимой правительством политике репрессий и других нарушениях прав человека. Эти выводы опираются на значительный массив материалов, опубликованных с 2020 года. В своих докладах FFM описала роль ряда предполагаемых исполнителей среднего и высокого уровня, цепочки командования в разведывательных службах и силах безопасности, а также государственную политику в отношении гражданского населения, которое может считаться инакомыслящим, — политику, способную составлять преступления против человечности, включая преследование по политическим мотивам. FFM пришла к выводу, что в Венесуэле продолжаются грубые нарушения прав человека и совершаются преступления по международному праву, при этом сохраняется безнаказанность. Миссия также обратила внимание на роль вооружённых групп гражданских лиц в проводимой правительством политике репрессий и других нарушениях прав человека. Дополнительная информация Независимая международная миссия ООН по установлению фактов в Венесуэле — это специальный механизм, созданный ООН в 2019 году для наблюдения за ситуацией и расследования грубых нарушений прав человека в Венесуэле. Значимость её работы получила широкое признание, и ввиду сохраняющейся актуальности её мандат продлевался на два года в 2020 , 2022 и 2024 годах . Ожидается, что резолюция о продлении мандата будет вынесена на голосование в последние дни 63-й сессии Совета ООН по правам человека — с 5 по 7 октября. Как и в случае с предыдущими резолюциями о продлении мандата FFM, ведущую роль в этом процессе продолжают играть государства Америки. С 2024 года эту инициативу возглавляют Аргентина, Канада, Чили, Эквадор, Гватемала, Парагвай и Уругвай.

https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1005309/%.body: کمبود ویتامین فولات یا همان ویتامین ب ۹ با ایجاد نوعی کمخونی شدید میتواند به خستگی مزمن، سردرد و افت تواناییهای حافظه منجر شود. پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات فرارو- این روزها خستگی مفرط، سردردهای آزاردهنده و فراموشیهای مقطعی به بخشی عادی از زیست روزمره بسیاری از شهروندان تبدیل شده است، اما پژوهشهای نوین پزشکی بر نقش محوری یک ریزمغذی حیاتی انگشت گذاشتهاند که کمبود آن میتواند هشداری برای بروز اختلالات عمیقتر عصبی و خونی باشد. به گزارش فرارو به نقل از هافپست، برای بخش قابل توجهی از مردم، احساس خستگی مداوم، کمبود شدید انرژی روزانه یا تحمل سردردهای پیدرپی به اندازهای تکرار میشود که گویی به بخشی جداییناپذیر و روزمره از زندگی آنها بدل شده است. با این حال، کارشناسان حوزه سلامت و متخصصان بالینی یک هشدار همگانی را مطرح میکنند: این علائم هرگز هنجار نیستند و هیچ فردی نباید خود را به همزیستی مسالمتآمیز با آنها وادار کند. در فیزیولوژی بدن انسان، خستگی مفرط و سردرد در واقع زبان ارتباطی ارگانها هستند تا اعلام کنند بخشی از چرخههای حیاتی دچار اختلال شده است یا نیازی اساسی در بدن بیپاسخ مانده است. این نیاز ممکن است استراحت ناکافی، عدم نوشیدن آب به میزان لازم یا ناتوانی در تأمین پایهایترین احتیاجات تغذیهای باشد. در این میان، یک ریزمغذی اساسی وجود دارد که کمبود آن اغلب از چشم افراد و حتی برخی درمانگران پنهان میماند، اما نادیده گرفتن آن میتواند به خستگی شدید، سردردهای مزمن و تضعیف عملکردهای شناختی مغز و حافظه منتهی شود: این ماده حیاتی چیزی جز «فولات» (ویتامین B9) نیست. کمبود فولات؛ کاتالیزور کمخونی و سلسلهای از مشکلات جسمانی شناسایی دقیق و ریشهیابی خستگی مداوم همواره کار سادهای نیست. در گام نخست، شاید اذهان عمومی به سمت مقصران سنتی و نامآشناتری نظیر کمبود آهن یا مصرف ناکافی پروتئین معطوف شود. اما فاکتوری که غالباً نادیده گرفته میشود، میزان ذخایر فولات در خون است. دکتر ندا هندیه، متخصص مغز و اعصاب و مدیر ارشد پزشکی مرکز سردرد و میگرن «هیوِن»، تأکید میکند احساس فرسودگی و خستگی بارزترین نشانه اولیه در افراد مبتلا به کمبود فولات است. او تشریح میکند: «فولات نقشی غیرقابل انکار و محوری در فرایند ساخت گلبولهای قرمز سالم و بالغ در مغز استخوان ایفا میکند. بدون وجود مقادیر کافی از این ویتامین، بدن دچار کمخونی میشود. بر همین اساس، مبتلایان معمولاً احساس مداوم رخوت، خستگی، ضعف عضلانی و تنگی نفس را در طول فعالیتهای معمول خود گزارش میکنند.» این متخصص مغز و اعصاب میافزاید عوارض ناشی از عدم دریافت یا جذب ناکافی فولات به صورت تدریجی شکل میگیرند و در گذر زمان میتوانند پیامدهایی جدی همچون سردرد و افت توانمندیهای شناختی به بار آورند. اگرچه کمبود فولات لزوماً نخستین علت مستقیم میگرن یا سردردهای موضعی تلقی نمیشود، اما کمبود قابلتوجه و طولانیمدت آن قادر است نوعی کمخونی ساختاری به نام کمخونی مگالوبلاستیک ایجاد کند که در پی آن، سردرد به یک علامت شایع ثانویه تبدیل خواهد شد. اثرات مخرب کمبود فولات در درازمدت متوجه سلامت مغز و بهویژه ساختار ظریف حافظه نیز میشود. پژوهشها نشان میدهند افت سطح فولات سرم با تسریع افت عملکردهای شناختی پیوند مستقیم داشته و یک نشانگر زیستی مهم برای پیشبینی کاهش توان ذهنی در میان سالمندان به شمار میرود. در همین چارچوب، دکتر شوانگ جوشی، استادیار رشته نورولوژی در دانشگاه ماساچوست، خاطرنشان میسازد که درصد فراوانی از مبتلایان به فقر فولات همزمان با افت سطح ویتامین ب ۱۲ نیز دستبهگریبان هستند؛ ویتامینی که بر اساس یافتههای پژوهشی ارتباطی بنیادین و اثباتشده با ضعف حافظه و زوال شناختی دارد. دکتر هندیه نیز با تأکید بر اینکه کارکرد عادی مغز کاملاً متکی به حضور فولات است، میگوید: «موضوع حافظه سازوکاری پیچیده و چندبعدی دارد؛ دلایل بیشماری میتوانند عملکرد حافظه را مخدوش کنند که کمبود فولات تنها یکی از این قطعات پازل به شمار میآید و نباید در بررسیهای بالینی از آن غفلت ورزید.» چه گروههایی در معرض بالاترین ریسک کمبود فولات قرار دارند؟ نکته اطمینانبخش این است که از نگاه هر دو متخصص مغز و اعصاب، وقوع فقر حاد فولات در جوامع مدرن پدیدهای نسبتاً نادر محسوب میشود. دکتر جوشی توضیح میدهد: «امروزه در بسیاری از کشورها به دلیل غنیسازی گسترده مواد غذایی، بهویژه آرد و فرآوردههای غلات با اسید فولیک، ابتلای افراد به کمبود واقعی این ویتامین چندان شایع نیست.» فولات طبیعی در طیف گسترده و متعددی از اقلام غذایی در دسترس است؛ از سبزیجات برگسبز تیره، میوهها، مغزها و دانههای روغنی گرفته تا حبوبات، غذاهای دریایی، تخممرغ، فرآوردههای لبنی، گوشت قرمز، مرغ و دانههای سبوسدار. به همین دلیل، چنانچه شخصی با کمبود این ویتامین مواجه گردد، بهاحتمال بسیار قوی نشاندهنده سوءتغذیه کلی و فقر در دریافت سایر ریزمغذیهای بنیادین نیز خواهد بود. کسانی که از بیماریهای سوءجذب دستگاه گوارش نظیر بیماری سلیاک یا بیماریهای التهابی روده رنج میبرند، مستعد افت شدید این ماده هستند. در کنار این موارد، به گفته گیلو، زنان در دوران بارداری نیز به علت نیاز مبرم به سنتز دیانای جنینی و تقسیمات سریع سلولی، در معرض خطر بیشتری قرار دارند و نیازمند دریافت مضاعف هستند. راهکارهای ساده و علمی برای تأمین فولات کافی بر پایه رهنمودهای مؤسسه ملی سلامت آمریکا، میزان توصیه شده روزانه فولات برای افراد بزرگسال غیرباردار، ۴۰۰ میکروگرم از «معادلهای فولات غذایی» است. اگرچه اکثر مردم از طریق سبد غذایی خود مقادیر لازم را به دست میآورند، اما هرگاه علائم هشداردهندهای مانند خستگی مزمن، سردرد و مه مغزی پدیدار شد، سنجش سطح سرمی فولات از طریق یک آزمایش خون ساده، گامی راهگشا و اولیه در روند تشخیص پزشکی به شمار میرود. امی براونستین، متخصص تغذیه، رمز اصلی تندرستی را تنوع در رژیم غذایی میداند. بهترین و متمرکزترین منابع طبیعی فولات شامل لوبیا چشمبلبلی، اسفناج بخارپز و غلات صبحانه غنیشده هستند. وی اضافه کردن تنها یک وعده روزانه از مواد غنی از فولات را برای رفع کامل احتیاجات بدن کارآمد قلمداد میکند. براونستین تأکید میکند زنان باردار یا زنانی که قصد بارداری دارند، عمدهترین گروهی هستند که باید تحت نظر پزشک از مکملهای دارویی استفاده نمایند؛ زیرا این ماده بهخصوص در هفتههای نخست حاملگی برای تکامل بدون نقص لوله عصبی و نخاع جنین نقشی حیاتی و غیرقابل چشمپوشی ایفا میکند. در پایان، متخصصان متذکر میشوند دریافت بیش از حد فولات از طریق منابع غذایی طبیعی به ندرت روی میدهد و عموماً بیخطر است، اما در صورت استفاده از مکملها و قرصهای ویتامینی، مجموع دوز دریافتی روزانه نباید از سقف مجاز ۱۰۰۰ میکروگرم تجاوز نماید. اگرچه کمبود فولات در جوامع امروزی وضعیتی فراگیر نیست، اما بیتوجهی به آن میتواند موجی از عوارض عصبی و فیزیولوژیک برانگیزد؛ از این رو مراجعه به پزشک در مواجهه با خستگی و افت تمرکز، نخستین گام منطقی در مسیر بازیابی نشاط، انرژی پایدار و وضوح ذهنی است. تبلیغات آیا چای میتواند نیاز روزانه بدن به آب را تأمین کند؟ پارادوکس شادی و اندوه؛ چرا پشت تحولات مثبت، سوگی پنهان نهفته است؟ این ۶ عادات قدیمی نظافت را کنار بگذارید مرز باریک محبت و دخالت؛ رفتارهای مخرب تربیتی پدربزرگها و مادربزرگها بیشتر بدانید: خستگی مزمن فولات ویتامین ب تبلیغات مهمترین علائم کمبود اسید فولیک از زبان پزشکان کمبود کدام ویتامینها موجب کاهش انگیزه میشوند؟ سندرم خستگی مفرط؛ چگونه خلأهای هفتگانه انرژی خود را پر کنیم؟

https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1005448/%.body: رقابت آمریکا و چین با وجود اختلافات راهبردی، به دلیل وابستگی اقتصادی و فناورانه دو کشور همچنان با همکاریهای ناخواسته همراه است. استفاده از مدل چینی برای تحلیل یک حمله سایبری به فناوری آمریکایی، نقش کاهش تقاضای نفت چین در کنترل قیمت انرژی و وابستگی دارویی آمریکا، نشان میدهد جدایی کامل پرهزینه است. پ ، پـ فرارو– فرید زکریا، ستون نویس روزنامه واشنگتن پست و مجری شبکه سی ان ان به گزارش فرارو به نقل از نشریه فارن پالیسی، همزمان با تلاش دونالد ترامپ و شی جینپینگ برای مدیریت رقابت فزاینده میان آمریکا و چین، یک واقعیت کمتر دیدهشده نشان میدهد که وابستگی متقابل دو کشور هنوز آنقدر عمیق است که حتی در اوج رقابت راههایی برای همکاری ایجاد میکند. نشست اخیر ترامپ و شی نشان داد که رهبران آمریکا و چین، با وجود افزایش رقابت راهبردی، همچنان به دنبال حوزههایی برای همکاری هستند. یکی از نمونههای کمتر مورد توجه، همکاری غیرمستقیم فناوریهای آمریکایی و چینی در جریان یک حمله سایبری اخیر بود؛ رویدادی که نشان میدهد وابستگی متقابل دو اقتصاد بزرگ جهان صرفاً یک مسئله تجاری نیست و در حوزههای حساس فناوری و امنیت نیز خود را نشان میدهد. هوش مصنوعی؛ یک آمریکایی حمله کرد، یک چینی به تحقیق کمک کرد در ماه ژوئیه، حملهای به «هاگینگ فیس»، یکی از پلتفرمهای مهم آمریکایی هوش مصنوعی، خبرساز شد. این شرکت برای بررسی حادثه تلاش کرد از مدلهای هوش مصنوعی برای تحلیل حمله و واکنش به آن استفاده کند، اما مدلهای پیشرفته آمریکایی به دلیل سازوکارهای ایمنی خود از کمک خودداری کردند؛ زیرا نتوانستند میان بررسی یک حمله سایبری و اجرای حمله تمایز کافی قائل شوند. در نهایت، هاگینگ فیس برای تحلیل حادثه به یک مدل چینی به نام «جیالام-۵.۲» روی آورد که توسط شرکت چینی «زد.ایآی» توسعه یافته بود. بنابراین، در نمونهای قابل توجه، یک فناوری آمریکایی هدف حمله قرار گرفت و برای فهمیدن نحوه وقوع آن، از فناوری چینی استفاده شد. چین چگونه به کنترل قیمت نفت در آمریکا کمک کرد؟ نمونه دوم به بازار انرژی مربوط میشود. آمریکا درگیر جنگ با ایران، یکی از تولیدکنندگان بزرگ نفت جهان شده است؛ در حالی که پیشبینیهایی درباره افزایش شدید قیمت نفت در صورت طولانی شدن جنگ مطرح شده بود و برخی کارشناسان حتی قیمت ۱۵۰ دلار برای هر بشکه را محتمل میدانستند. با این حال، چنین جهشی رخ نداد و یکی از مهمترین عوامل، کاهش چشمگیر واردات نفت چین عنوان شده است. چین بنا بر این گزارش حدود چهار میلیون بشکه در روز از واردات نفت خود کاسته است. این اقدام که با انگیزههای خود چین انجام شده، به کاهش فشار بر بازار جهانی نفت کمک کرده و در نتیجه، قیمت بنزین در آمریکا نیز پایینتر از سطحی قرار گرفته که در صورت نبود این کاهش تقاضا ممکن بود تجربه شود. چرا رابطه آمریکا و چین شبیه جنگ سرد نیست؟ با استناد به کتاب جدید «قفل داروین» نوشته جاشوا کوپر رامو، مفهوم تکامل برای توضیح روابط آمریکا و چین به کار گرفته میشود. داروین در بررسی نظریه تکامل دریافت که منطق رقابت صرف نمیتواند پدیدههایی مانند فداکاری یا همکاری را توضیح دهد. در محیطهای سخت، گونهها گاهی به همکاری متقابل روی میآورند، زیرا چنین همکاریای برای بقا ضروری است. این منطق را میتوان تا حدی درباره آمریکا و چین نیز به کار برد. دو کشور طی چهار دهه در یک اکوسیستم اقتصادی و فناورانه مشترک رشد کردهاند و زنجیرههای تأمین، سرمایه، پژوهش، تولید و بازارهای آنها در هم تنیده شده است. به همین دلیل، مقایسه روابط کنونی واشنگتن و پکن با جنگ سرد آمریکا و شوروی چندان دقیق نیست. آمریکا و اتحاد شوروی از نظر اقتصادی و فناورانه ارتباط محدودی داشتند، اما آمریکا و چین امروز بهشدت به یکدیگر وابستهاند و قطع کامل این روابط هزینه سنگینی برای هر دو کشور و اقتصاد جهانی خواهد داشت. وابستگی دارویی؛ نمونهای از آسیبپذیری مشترک حوزه دارو یکی از روشنترین نمونههای این وابستگی است. طبق دادههای ارائهشده در گزارش، حدود ۴۱ درصد از مواد اولیه کلیدی مورد استفاده در داروهای مورد تأیید آمریکا، تنها از چین تأمین میشوند. این وابستگی در حوزههایی مانند آنتیبیوتیکها و مواد اولیه داروهای کاهشدهنده کلسترول، ضدافسردگی و داروهای فشار خون بیشتر است. دادههای سازمان غذا و داروی آمریکا نیز نشان میدهد که سهم تولیدکنندگان داخلی تأمینکننده مواد اولیه دارویی برای بازار آمریکا حدود ۹ درصد است، در حالی که این رقم برای چین ۲۲ درصد و برای هند ۴۴ درصد گزارش شده است. وابستگی مدیریتشده این واقعیت به معنای کنار گذاشتن رقابت نیست. آمریکا همچنان درباره وابستگی به چین در حوزه مواد حیاتی نگران است و چین نیز نسبت به وابستگی خود به فناوری آمریکایی بهویژه تراشههای مورد استفاده در توسعه هوش مصنوعی نگرانی دارد . راهحل پیشنهادی، نه وابستگی مطلق و نه جدایی کامل، بلکه نوعی «وابستگی مدیریتشده» است: شناسایی نقاط آسیبپذیر، ایجاد منابع جایگزین در حوزههای حساس و حفظ روابط اقتصادی در بخشهایی که خطر امنیتی جدی ایجاد نمیکنند. بر اساس این دیدگاه، آمریکا و چین احتمالاً همچنان رقبای جدی در فناوری، نظامیگری و سیاست جهانی باقی خواهند ماند، اما تلاش برای تضعیف کامل یکدیگر میتواند پیامدهایی متقابل داشته باشد. مسئله اصلی این است که رقابت در یک حوزه به بحرانی فراگیر در کل رابطه تبدیل نشود . در نهایت، تجربه سه دهه گذشته نشان داده است که تصور اینکه تجارت میتواند ژئوپلیتیک را از میان ببرد، اشتباه بوده است. اما تصور معکوس یعنی اینکه ژئوپلیتیک میتواند بهسادگی واقعیت اقتصاد جهانی و پیوندهای میان آمریکا و چین را از بین ببرد، میتواند به همان اندازه پرهزینه باشد. نویسنده : فرید زکریا سئول زیر فشار ترامپ برای اعزام نیروی دریایی به تنگه هرمز رابطه «قفل داروین» جایگزین «جنگ سرد» چرا «هواپیمای روز قیامت» آمریکا به پرواز درآمد؟ چرا اروپا از تهدید ترامپ نگران است؟ بیشتر بدانید: چین هوش مصنوعی دونالد ترامپ شی جین پینگ آیا آمریکا و چین میتوانند از «دام توسیدید» فرار کنند؟ آمریکا سردرگم؛ چین در مسیر شتاب خروجی دیدار ترامپ و شی چه بود؟

https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/09/25/from.body: Business Companies News News From Gorno-Badakhshan to Italy: the story of Tajik white stone and a Chinese entrepreneur This is a case where a natural material from Tajikistan can compete not only on price or origin, but on quality, appearance and character. Partnership post 25.09.2026 15:15 Telegram Facebook WhatsApp Copy URL White stone from the high-altitude Poyi Mazor deposit in Vanj district of the Gorno BAdakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) is being presented in Italy for the first time at the international Marmomac exhibition . What only a few years ago was known mainly to specialists and designers in China is today making its debut at one of the world’s leading platforms for the natural stone industry. And behind this event stands not only Tajikistan’s unique resource, but also the people who believed in its potential and managed to take it far beyond the country’s borders. Sometimes a long journey begins with a single stone In Tajikistan’s case — with a white stone high in the Pamir mountains, amid a harsh climate, snow and virtually inaccessible deposits. Today this material is being presented in Italy for the first time at Marmomac — one of the most renowned and authoritative international exhibitions of natural stone. It is the most important exhibition for the entire stone production chain. Here visitors can see finished products, equipment, tools and technologies used in the extraction and processing of natural stone. From 22 to 25 September, the exhibition in Verona will mark its 60th anniversary in the natural stone sector. For Tajikistan, this event carries special significance. As an international platform, the product is seen by professionals from across the global industry — architects, designers, manufacturers, processors and companies working with natural stone worldwide. And most importantly — Tajikistan genuinely has something to show. Poymazar marble, for instance, cannot be assessed merely as a building material. Its principal advantage lies in its light, almost luminous surface: a soft natural pattern and fine white veins create an effect of fluidity. Its texture is compared to jade — a dense, noble and visually luxurious material. But behind the beauty lie serious technical characteristics as well. The water absorption of the white stone is just 0.01%. It has high resistance to abrasion, along with density and strength, which allow it to be used not only as a decorative element but also in complex architectural and interior projects. It is precisely the combination of aesthetics and physical properties that makes this stone particularly attractive for the premium segment. This is a case where a natural material from Tajikistan is capable of competing not only on price or origin. It can compete on quality, appearance and character. From Poymazar to design projects The white stone of Poymazar was discovered around eight years ago. But the journey from the discovery of the deposit to entering the international market proved to be far from straightforward. Poymazar is situated high in the mountains. In winter, the deposit becomes virtually inaccessible. Snow arrives as early as December, and full-scale operations can only resume at the end of April or in May. In practice, conventional extraction is possible for only around six months of the year. The altitude, climate, complex logistics and terrain features long constrained the pace of development. But this is precisely where another part of the story begins — the entrepreneurial one. Chen Yanli, owner of the Chinese company PFM Co., Ltd, began working in Tajikistan through her involvement in one of a local company’s construction projects. At the time, her team was handling façade work on the project. Following that collaboration, PFM was increasingly brought in for other construction projects in the country, including work on residential buildings. Participation in several projects involving marble gradually led Chen Yanli to the idea of developing this area at the level of raw material extraction. According to her, one of the key factors was the high cost of marble. The company therefore began exploring the possibility of developing local deposits. In 2017, PFM began working with one of the limestone quarries, and in 2019 started studying white marble and the prospects for its extraction. From 2023, the company began supplying white marble from Tajikistan to the Chinese market. The stone became more than just a raw material Chen Yanli saw in it an international product — a material that could appeal to architects, designers and developers far beyond Central Asia. The joint work of Chinese company PFM and Tajik company MARMAR STONE gradually transformed the deposit from a challenging high-altitude site into a project with international prospects: extraction, technology, logistics, processing, market development, presenting the material to designers and the continuous development of the product itself. In 2026, a new phase began — tunnel extraction. This technology makes it possible to extract significantly larger stone blocks, thereby expanding the possibilities for their use in large architectural spaces. For premium natural stone, block size is of fundamental importance. The larger the format, the more effectively the material’s natural pattern can be showcased — in hotel lobbies, private villas, residential complexes, large wall panels, entrance halls and other prestigious interiors. Before Italy, the material already had an international history. It entered the Chinese market in 2023. Over three years, the Tajik white stone gained recognition among designers and began to be used in hotel projects, premium apartments, residential complexes and private villas. In other words, it passed a practical market test. Designers saw it, chose it for real projects and began using it in spaces where the quality and appearance of materials are held to particularly high standards. And it was precisely the interest of the Chinese design community that became one of the arguments for the next step: if the stone had already proved its appeal in China — why not show it to Europe? And now it is presented at Marmomac Italy is one of the countries associated worldwide with a culture of marble, architecture and working with natural stone. Here, natural stone is not merely a building material but part of a centuries-old culture. And it is here that stone from Tajikistan has arrived for the first time. At the exhibition, visitors can see the very material that was recently being extracted high in the Pamirs. Now it stands among stones from countries long known to the global industry. ‹ › For MARMAR STONE and PFM, this is an important international milestone. And for Tajikistan — an opportunity to present itself from an entirely different angle. Not only as a country of high mountains, but as a country whose mountains contain truly valuable natural materials. Around 93% of Tajikistan’s territory is covered by mountains. If in the past this figure was most often cited in discussions of geography or tourism, today it is acquiring a different meaning as well. In recent years, new natural stone deposits capable of attracting international market interest have been discovered and developed in the country. And the white stone of Poymazar may prove to be one of the most striking examples of this potential. Today, Marmar Stone and PFM are working to develop a fully-fledged international product. This covers extraction technology, block quality, processing, design, presentation and promotion. The companies are constantly looking for new ways to showcase the material so that its natural structure is revealed to maximum effect. Perhaps the main outcome of this story is not even that one Tajik stone appeared at an international exhibition. https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/09/26/a-ta.body: Law-order News Russia Tajik national sentenced to 20 years in prison in Russia over 2008 murder of skinhead Saidjona Rajabov was detained 17 years after the incident and extradited to Russia. asia+ 26.09.2026 15:15 Telegram Facebook WhatsApp Copy URL A court in Moscow Oblast has sentenced 43-year-old Tajik national Sayedjon Rajabov to 20 years in prison for a 2008 murder and attempted murder, according to the Fergana news agency. The Kolomna City Court found Rajabov guilty of murder and attempted murder of two or more people. He denied the charges. The incident occurred in March 2008 at Golutvin railway station in Moscow Oblast. According to the Moscow Interregional Transport Prosecutor’s Office, Rajabov stabbed three young people during a confrontation. One victim died at the scene, while two others were hospitalized. Rajabov subsequently left Russia and was placed on an international wanted list. Seventeen years later, he was detained in Tajikistan and extradited to Russia. The court sentenced him to 20 years in a high-security penal colony. The number of victims reported by different sources varies. The prosecutor’s office said one person was killed and two were hospitalized. However, archived Russian media reports said that two of the injured victims later died in hospital. According to media reports at the time, the confrontation took place during so-called “cleansing” raids on suburban trains around Moscow by young people with nationalist views. At Golutvin station, they reportedly attacked two Tajik nationals, and Rajabov intervened on their behalf. The case has also been linked in media reports to xenophobic violence against migrants from Central Asia. According to the Sova Center, 161 attacks that it classified as ethnically motivated violence were recorded in Russia in 2025. The victims included people from Central Asia and the Caucasus. https://thediplomat.com/2026/09/at-unga-.body: Credit: UN Photo Subscribe for ads-free reading Amid his 20-minute remarks before the United Nations General Assembly this week, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov took time to complain about sanctions and thank U.S. President Donald Trump for ceasing support to NGOs. “...[T]oday sanctions are, in some cases, used by individual countries as an instrument of interference in the internal affairs of sovereign states,” Japarov said. “The negative consequences of unjustified unilateral sanctions also affect small countries such as ours, which are at the stage of formation and development, and this raises concern among other small states as well.” Japarov went on to claim that “some major states, in pursuit of their own interests, put pressure on smaller countries such as Kyrgyzstan, attempting to force them to bargain over certain matters and issuing ultimatums.” At no point did Japarov lay out specifically what countries he believes are pressuring Kyrgyzstan, and to what end. Then, in the middle of his commentary about sanctions, Japarov pivoted to lauding the U.S. president – although the Trump administration has maintained the prior administration’s sanctions on various Kyrgyz entities. “In this context, I would like to take this opportunity to note the decision made by the President of the United States His Excellency Mr. Donald Trump after taking office to halt funding of non-governmental organizations around the world,” Japarov said. “As a result, interference by NGOs in the internal affairs and policies of developing states has practically ceased.” For Japarov, the two issues are inextricably linked. Last year at UNGA , he stated that “sanctions imposed on Kyrgyzstan are based on false information spread by certain non-governmental organizations and malicious citizens.” Japarov has not specified which NGOs or “malicious citizens” have provided this “false information” that supposedly landed Kyrgyz business and banks on sanctions lists. In April, Kyrgyzstan’s Bakai Bank won a case in a Belgian commercial court against the Open Dialogue Foundation (ODF) for its publication of reports alleging that the bank was involved in the circumvention of sanctions against Russia. Note that the bank had not been sanctioned. The court classified the NGO as a “commercial enterprise,” opening it to liability as if it were a market competitor. As the World Liberty Congress , a global alliance of pro-democracy leaders, said in a statement: “The court required published information to meet a commercial verification standard designed for disputes between market operators, a test that is structurally impossible for any organization working in an authoritarian jurisdiction where access to primary banking records is unavailable.” Meanwhile, also in April 2026 , the EU aimed its “anti-circumvention tool” at Kyrgyzstan, the first country so targeted. In the subsequent months, Kyrgyz authorities pantomimed taking action. In June 2026, two state-owned banks claimed to have ended partnerships with more than 130 clients due to sanctions risks. In August , another round of cut connections was announced. However, Kyrgyz authorities have never specified which companies were affected, making it all but impossible to confirm whether companies that present actual sanctions risks have been cut loose. According to RFE/RL’s Kyrgyz Service, Azattyk , as of June 2026, 31 companies from Kyrgyzstan were under Western sanctions, including five banks. While three Tajik banks were removed from the EU sanctions list in May, the Kyrgyz banks – such as Keremet Bank , Kapital Bank, Eurasian Savings Bank , and EcoIslamicBank – remain designated by the EU, the U.K., and/or the U.S. After thanking Trump “for ending the funding of NGOs,” Japarov continued discussing sanctions, arguing that the decision to impose sanctions should “be taken in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and exclusively within the mandate of the Security Council.” Kyrgyzstan this year won a non-permanent seat on the U.N. Security Council . Japarov went on to speak of the U.N. in terms that seem divorced from the body’s current hamstrung reality. “Every decision of the United Nations should be implemented without delay. If a state fails to implement such decision and other countries cease cooperation with it, the effectiveness of sanctions will increase,” he argued. The permanent members of the UNSC – China, Russia, France, the U.K., and the U.S. – stand on diametrically opposed ends of the global order and this has effectively neutered its possible decisiveness – whether on sanctions or anything else. For example, in September 2022, Russia vetoed a Security Council resolution condemning Moscow’s attempted annexation of parts of Ukraine. The U.S. has repeatedly blocked resolutions targeting Israel . China joined Russia earlier this month to veto an effort to extend the mandate of independent experts monitoring sanctions on Iran. Suggesting that the UNSC become the central clearinghouse for all sanctions is effectively a call for there to be no sanctions, ever. Already have an account? Log in . Then, in the middle of his commentary about sanctions, Japarov pivoted to lauding the U.S. president – although the Trump administration has maintained the prior administration’s sanctions on various Kyrgyz entities. “In this context, I would like to take this opportunity to note the decision made by the President of the United States His Excellency Mr. Donald Trump after taking office to halt funding of non-governmental organizations around the world,” Japarov said. “As a result, interference by NGOs in the internal affairs and policies of developing states has practically ceased.” For Japarov, the two issues are inextricably linked. Last year at UNGA , he stated that “sanctions imposed on Kyrgyzstan are based on false information spread by certain non-governmental organizations and malicious citizens.” Japarov has not specified which NGOs or “malicious citizens” have provided this “false information” that supposedly landed Kyrgyz business and banks on sanctions lists. https://kaktus.media/doc/554036_reuters:.body: kaktus.media Reuters: Россия в августе увеличила поставки дизтоплива в Кыргызстан более чем в 16 раз Политика 340 27 сентября 2026 15:59 Kaktus Все самое интересное в Telegram Россия резко нарастила экспорт дизельного топлива в Кыргызстан в августе 2026 года. Поставки превысили 72 тыс. тонн против 4,4 тыс. тонн в июле, сообщает Reuters со ссылкой на трейдеров. Таким образом, за месяц объем поставок российского дизтоплива в Кыргызстан вырос более чем в 16 раз. Рост произошел на фоне увеличения производства дизеля в России. При этом Москва продолжала ограничивать экспорт топлива на большинство зарубежных рынков из-за роста внутренних цен и дефицита, возникшего в том числе после атак украинских беспилотников на нефтеперерабатывающие заводы. Для ряда стран, включая бывшие советские республики и Монголию, поставки по межправительственным соглашениям разрешены. В целом экспорт российского дизельного топлива в Казахстан, Кыргызстан, Монголию и Таджикистан в августе более чем удвоился по сравнению с июлем и превысил 370 тыс. тонн. По теме: Кыргызстан обсудил с китайскими нефтегазовыми корпорациями строительство НПЗ Больше всего топлива получила Монголия - около 215 тыс. тонн против 124 тыс. тонн месяцем ранее. Поставки в Таджикистан выросли с 16 тыс. до более чем 56 тыс. тонн. Казахстан, который в июле не импортировал российское дизтопливо, в августе получил около 28 тыс. тонн. По словам трейдеров, производство дизельного топлива в России восстановилось примерно до 170 тыс. тонн в сутки, однако этого пока недостаточно для полноценного возобновления экспорта на все зарубежные рынки. За январь – август Россия экспортировала в страны Центральной Азии и Афганистан около 2,5 млн тонн дизельного топлива против 2,6 млн тонн за тот же период 2025 года. https://24.kg/english/390712_Russia_and_.body: Russia and Kazakhstan account for 90.3 % of Kyrgyzstan’s oil product imports - | 24.KG English 16:43, 25 September 2026 , Bishkek - 24.kg news agency , by Aibek SULTANOV Russia and Kazakhstan account for 90.3 % of Kyrgyzstan’s oil product imports 16:43, 25 September 2026 , Bishkek - 24.kg news agency , by Aibek SULTANOV Kyrgyzstan imported $499,889.4 million worth of oil products in the first seven months of 2026. The value of imports increased by 11.4 percent, while volumes fell by 17.3 percent, data from the National Statistical Committee say. The country also resumed imports of crude oil. From January to July, Kyrgyzstan imported 6,391.8 tonnes of crude oil, including gas condensate, worth $3,229.7 million. Kazakhstan was the sole supplier. No crude oil was imported in 2025. Oil product purchases from Azerbaijan increased sharply, rising 142.5 times to $4,641.6 million. Supplies from Turkey grew 2.7 times to $9,084.8 million, while imports from China increased 3.4 times to $4,621.5 million. Who dominates the fuel market Imports of gasoline and crude oil into Kyrgyzstan in January-July totaled $503,119.1 million, or 588,100.6 tonnes. The total cost of imports rose by 11.4 percent, while volumes declined by 17.3 percent. Kyrgyzstan imported $196,385.5 million worth of motor gasoline (377,441.5 million liters). Compared with the same period last year, the value and volume of gasoline imports fell by 18.2 percent and 29.1 percent, respectively. Russia was the main supplier. Additional shipments were purchased from Belarus, Kazakhstan and the UAE. Crude oil, including gas condensate, was imported for $3,229.7 million, totaling 6,391.8 tonnes. All supplies came from Kazakhstan. Top three suppliers of oil products: Russia — 69.9 percent, compared with 67.6 percent a year earlier; Kazakhstan — 20.4 percent, compared with 25.3 percent previously; Turkey — 1.8 percent, compared with 0.7 percent previously. Trade balance in the red In January-July, Kyrgyzstan recorded an absolute trade deficit of $503,119.1 million in oil and oil products, as there were no exports in these categories, according to the data. The country’s fuel and lubricant market is characterized by a high degree of consolidation: Russia and Kazakhstan account for 90.3 percent of total oil product imports. Following the meeting, the two sides signed a protocol amending and supplementing the agreement between the governments of Uzbekistan and China on international road transport. The document is aimed at improving the legal framework for road transportation and creating more favorable conditions for national carriers. Its implementation is expected to expand opportunities for Uzbek and Chinese companies to carry out international transport operations, reduce administrative barriers, and increase mutual and transit freight flows. The sides also discussed further development of international road transport, increasing cargo volumes and improving the efficiency of transport and logistics links. Particular attention was paid to the development of civil aviation, including increasing the number of flights between cities in Uzbekistan and China, expanding the geography of air routes, and creating additional opportunities for passenger and cargo transportation. https://kaktus.media/doc/554027_kitay_po.body: kaktus.media Китай подтвердил военно-техническое сотрудничество с Узбекистаном на фоне поставок J-10CE В мире 694 27 сентября 2026 12:20 Kaktus Все самое интересное в Telegram Министерство обороны Китая подтвердило развитие военно-технического сотрудничества с Узбекистаном. Об этом 24 сентября на пресс-конференции заявил официальный представитель ведомства Цзян Бин. По его словам, Китай и Узбекистан, а также вооруженные силы двух стран поддерживают дружественные отношения. Он отметил, что развитие военно-торгового сотрудничества соответствует международному праву и международной практике и не направлено против третьих стран. На этом фоне Узбекистан стал вторым после Пакистана зарубежным оператором китайских истребителей J-10CE. J-10CE - экспортная версия китайского многоцелевого истребителя поколения 4.5, разработанного Chengdu Aircraft Corporation. Photo: Sputnik The issue was discussed on September 23 by Uzbekistan’s Transport Minister Ilhom Mahkamov and China’s Transport Minister Liu Wei during talks on expanding bilateral cooperation in transport. Following the meeting, the two sides signed a protocol introducing amendments and additions to the agreement between the governments of Uzbekistan and China on international road transport. The document is intended to strengthen the legal framework for road transportation and improve conditions for national carriers. Its implementation is expected to expand opportunities for Uzbek and Chinese companies to conduct international freight operations, reduce administrative barriers and increase bilateral and transit cargo flows. The ministers also discussed expanding international road freight, increasing cargo volumes and improving transport and logistics links between the two countries. Civil aviation was another focus of the talks. The sides discussed increasing the number of flights between cities in Uzbekistan and China, expanding flight routes and creating additional opportunities for passenger and cargo transportation. Uzbekistan’s Transport Ministry said the new protocol would also support the development of international transport corridors linking China with Central Asia and other regions. The two sides agreed to continue working together to implement the agreements reached during the meeting.

https://en.kabar.kg/news/president-zhapa.body: Bishkek, Sept. 23, 2026 /Kabar/. On September 22, President of the Kyrgyz Republic Sadyr Zhaparov met with President of the European Council António Costa on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, the Presidential Administration of the Kyrgyz Republic reported. At the beginning of the meeting, António Costa congratulated the head of state on Kyrgyzstan's election as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council and on the successful hosting of the SCO summit in Bishkek earlier that month. The parties discussed key issues regarding cooperation between Kyrgyzstan and the European Union. In particular, they noted the importance of maintaining political dialogue—both bilaterally and within the "Central Asia – European Union" framework—and of developing cooperation under the Global Gateway program. The interlocutors paid special attention to the issue of sanctions. For his part, Sadyr Zhaparov expressed concern regarding the sanctions policy pursued by Western and European partners toward Kyrgyzstan, noting that Kyrgyzstan maintains constant contact and regularly exchanges information with relevant European Union officials. The head of state cited the closure this year of 50 companies in Kyrgyzstan that had engaged in high-risk sanctions-related activities, and emphasized a readiness for open dialogue as well as an interest in developing cooperation with Western and European partners. In the economic sphere, the parties discussed prospects for implementing specific joint projects—including in the transport sector—taking into account Kyrgyzstan’s aim to develop its transit potential and integrate into multimodal corridors. In conclusion, António Costa invited Sadyr Zhaparov to visit Brussels to give fresh impetus to their cooperation. The head of state graciously accepted the invitation. Print

https://en.kabar.kg/news/kyrgyzstan-and-.body: Presidential administration Bishkek, Sept. 23, 2026 /Kabar/. Erlist Akunbekov, Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers and Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry of the Kyrgyz Republic, held meetings with the heads of leading Chinese oil and gas corporations—CNPC and Sinopec—during his working visit to the PRC, the Cabinet of Ministers reported. During the visit, negotiations were held with Dai Houliang, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC), and Hou Qijun, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation (Sinopec). The parties discussed the development of joint projects, including the construction of an oil refinery in Kyrgyzstan, the exploration and development of oil fields, and the construction of a pipeline to transport petroleum products across the border between the two countries. Erlist Akunbekov noted that one of the objectives of his working visit to Beijing was to meet with companies operating in the oil sector, in accordance with President Sadyr Zhaparov’s directive to ensure stable and uninterrupted supplies of petroleum products to the country. Given the current situation in the Central Asian oil market, the importance of further deepening cooperation in this sector was emphasized. Companies operating in Kyrgyzstan are currently concluding agreements with the Chinese corporations CNPC and Sinopec, thereby ensuring regular supplies of petroleum products to Kyrgyzstan. Representatives of domestic companies were included in the Kyrgyz delegation to facilitate the conclusion of new agreements between the Chinese corporations and Kyrgyz firms. Furthermore, to reduce logistics costs, the possibility of constructing oil storage facilities (oil depots) near the Torugart and Irkeshtam border checkpoints on the Kyrgyz-Chinese border is being considered. https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/09/25/chin.body: China News Security China confirms delivery of J-10CE fighter jets to Uzbekistan Tashkent has become the second foreign customer of Chinese fighter jets after Pakistan. The exact number of aircraft delivered has not yet been disclosed. asia+ 25.09.2026 16:42 Telegram Facebook WhatsApp Copy URL China’s Ministry of National Defense has officially confirmed for the first time that it has delivered J-10CE multirole fighter jets to Uzbekistan, Fergana news agency reports, citing Chinese media outlet Sina . At a press conference on September 24, Chinese Defense Ministry spokesman Jiang Bin confirmed the completion of the aircraft transfer to the Uzbek Air Force in response to a journalist’s question. He said China and Uzbekistan maintain friendly relations, including cooperation in the military sphere. According to Jiang Bin, military-technical cooperation between the two countries is conducted in accordance with international law and common international practice and is not aimed at any third country. With the delivery, Uzbekistan has become the second officially confirmed foreign operator of the J-10CE fighter jets after Pakistan. The J-10CE is an export version of China’s fourth-generation-plus multirole fighter developed by the Chengdu Aircraft Corporation. The aircraft is equipped with an active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar and an advanced electronic warfare system. It is designed for both air-to-air combat and strikes against ground targets. The deployment of J-10CE fighters in Uzbekistan became publicly known in late August 2026, when state television broadcast footage showing at least six aircraft with Uzbek Air Force markings. The report was released ahead of the country’s 35th anniversary of independence and showed the aircraft at the Karshi-Khanabad air base. The exact number of fighters ordered by Uzbekistan has not been officially disclosed. Unconfirmed reports suggest that the contract could include up to 24 aircraft worth around $1 billion. These figures have not been confirmed by either Uzbek or Chinese authorities. The estimated price of a single J-10CE fighter is around $40–50 million, excluding weapons, pilot and technical staff training, and related infrastructure costs. The acquisition is part of Uzbekistan’s efforts to modernize its combat aviation fleet, much of which still relies on Soviet-era aircraft. The country retired its Su-27 fighters by around 2020 due to ageing airframes and difficulties obtaining spare parts. Its MiG-29 and Su-25 aircraft also remain older platforms. Previously, Tashkent considered purchasing Russian Su-30SM fighters. Negotiations on a possible deal had been ongoing since 2017, but Uzbekistan eventually chose Chinese-made aircraft. Interest in the J-10CE increased after their reported combat use by Pakistan’s Air Force during the India-Pakistan aerial confrontation in May 2025. Chinese state media later claimed that the fighters had successfully participated in air-to-air engagements. China’s military equipment is already in service with Uzbekistan. In particular, FD-2000 surface-to-air missile systems supplied by China were publicly displayed for the first time during Uzbekistan’s air defense exercises in 2018. Join us on social media! https://www.azernews.az/nation/264454.ht.body: Caucasus after Karabakh: from conflict zone to connectivity corridor 27 September 2026 10:30 (UTC+04:00) By Mazahir Afandiyev, in collaboration with the Editorial Team The 27th of September 2020 began for the entire Azerbaijani people as a long-awaited and proud day. It once again demonstrated the strength, determination and bravery of the victorious Azerbaijani Army, a strength that Azerbaijan had experienced throughout its history of statehood and that was demonstrated to the whole world. On that very day, the Armenian armed forces, which grossly violated the ceasefire regime, launched another aggression against Azerbaijan by intensively striking the positions of the Azerbaijani armed forces along the entire front line, while deliberately subjecting populated areas of the Tartar, Aghdam, Fuzuli and Jabrayil districts to artillery fire. As a result, alongside military personnel, 11 Azerbaijani civilians, including two children, were killed. Guided by the norms and principles of international law, as well as the four well-known resolutions of the United Nations Security Council that had remained on paper for 27 years, and with the aim of repelling the enemy's military provocation and putting an end to its aggression, as well as ending the occupation of our territories that had continued for more than 30 years, Supreme Commander-in-Chief and Great Commander, President Ilham Aliyev, immediately ordered the Azerbaijani Army to launch a counter-offensive along the entire front. Thus, our activities aimed at liberating Karabakh, for which we had yearned for 30 years, began on September 27 with the “Iron Fist” counter-offensive operations and turned into the 44-day Second Karabakh–Patriotic War, ending with the liberation of Shusha, the pearl of Karabakh, from occupation. As a result of successful military operations, by November 9, five cities, four settlements and 286 villages were liberated from occupation, while the victorious Azerbaijani Army defeated the Armenian armed forces and the terrorist groups formed in Karabakh. On November 10 of the same year, following Armenia's official appeal to the Russian Federation, the war was stopped with the direct participation of Russia and by agreement of the heads of all three states. A declaration consisting of nine provisions was adopted between Azerbaijan and Armenia, and thus Armenia signed an act of capitulation. As stated by Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, Armenia had no choice but to accept defeat before our Glorious Army. Therefore, the occupying side admitted its defeat and the conflict was officially brought to an end. Yet the end of active hostilities did not mean that the consequences of the conflict disappeared overnight. The post-war period created a second and equally important task: to turn military victory into a durable political, economic and social reality. This meant restoring communities, rebuilding infrastructure, returning people to their homes, reviving economic life and, ultimately, changing the physical and economic geography of a region that had been shaped by conflict for decades. As a result of continuing the victory achieved on the military front at the political level, within 20 days after the 44-day Patriotic War, three districts—Aghdam on November 20, Kalbajar on November 25, and Lachin on December 1—were handed over to Azerbaijan. On August 26, 2022, the city of Lachin, as well as the villages of Zabukh and Sus, were taken under control. Thus, in accordance with the trilateral statement, the process of peacefully returning the Aghdam, Kalbajar and Lachin districts was completed. The War, which lasted only 44 days, and the bravery of our heroic officers and soldiers turned the centuries-old aspirations of our grateful people into reality, liberated our lands that had been under occupation, and restored historical justice. From the very first day of this war, hundreds of patriotic young Azerbaijanis wholeheartedly volunteered to go to the front and fought heroically against the enemy. Unfortunately, war has its own laws. If there is war, there are also martyrs, veterans and losses. This war was not without casualties either. A total of 2,908 Azerbaijani servicemen made the ultimate sacrifice in the struggle to liberate our lands, while six remain missing and thousands of brave soldiers became war veterans. As President Ilham Aliyev stated, “I once again bow my head before the souls of the martyrs of the First and Second Karabakh Wars and pray to God to have mercy upon them. We avenged their blood! Our heroic soldiers and officers who presented us with this Victory are our source of pride. Their heroism, their bravery and their sacrifice have already become an epic.” It is no coincidence that September 27, which has become a celebration of national will, national spirit and national dignity, is observed every year in the Republic of Azerbaijan as Remembrance Day, in accordance with the Order of President Ilham Aliyev dated December 2, 2020, as a sign of deep respect for our soldiers and officers who fought heroically in the Second Karabakh–Patriotic War and sacrificed their lives for the territorial integrity of our country, as well as for all our martyrs. In general, the Azerbaijani state has always shown the highest respect for the memory of our martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the Motherland, keeping the perpetuation of their memory, as well as the treatment and restoration of the health of our veterans, at the centre of its attention. The Victory Park, created with the aim of perpetuating the names of our martyrs and heroic sons; the Victory Arch, built as a symbol of the 44-day Patriotic War, with a height of 44 metres, a width of 22 metres and 44 columns; the Patriotic War Memorial Complex; and the Victory Museum will always keep alive the heroic epic of our people. But remembrance is only one part of the post-war transformation. The other is rebuilding the geography of everyday life. Roads, railways, airports, energy infrastructure, digital networks, industrial zones, residential settlements and social facilities are changing the physical landscape of Karabakh and Eastern Zangezur. Reconstruction is therefore not simply about repairing what was destroyed. It is about creating the infrastructure through which people, goods, capital and ideas can move again. This is where the meaning of the post-Karabakh period becomes broader than the restoration of territories. The strategic question is increasingly how a region that was once associated with closed borders, military positions and competing territorial claims can become a region of roads, railways, trade routes and economic cooperation. Today, the Azerbaijani people are closer to peace than ever before. The South Caucasus is transforming from a centre of conflict into a region where all peoples can live in prosperity. The signing of the Washington Declaration on August 8, 2025, between President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev, President of the United States Donald Trump and Prime Minister of the Republic of Armenia Nikol Pashinyan, as well as the initialling of the text of the Peace Agreement, became an important point towards achieving lasting peace. The Washington Declaration explicitly emphasised the opening of communications between Azerbaijan and Armenia for domestic, bilateral and international transportation and referred to unimpeded connectivity between mainland Azerbaijan and the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic through the territory of Armenia, with reciprocal benefits for regional connectivity. It also established the framework for the proposed Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity, or TRIPP. This is an important change in the language of the South Caucasus. For decades, the region was discussed primarily through the vocabulary of conflict: ceasefires, front lines, occupied territories, displaced populations, security arrangements and negotiations. https://daryo.uz/en/2024/11/08/trumps-fo.body: Uzbekistan Trump’s foreign policy in Central Asia: balancing acts amid rising influence from China and Russia Traditionally, this region has not been a top priority for American presidents. However, shifting geopolitical dynamics, particularly involving China and Russia, are reshaping the U.S. approach to Central Asia. The adoption of the "U.S. Strategy for Central Asia 2019-2025: Advancing Sovereignty and Economic Prosperity" during the Trump administration marked a strategic shift. How do external forces determine U.S. foreign policy in Central Asia? 8 November 2024, 18:50 11 min read 21,170 views 0 comments 0 With Donald Trump being elected as the next President of the United States, the country's foreign policy in Central Asia is anticipated to be heavily influenced by external factors. Traditionally, this region has not been a top priority for American presidents. However, shifting geopolitical dynamics, particularly involving China and Russia, are reshaping the U.S. approach to Central Asia. The adoption of the "U.S. Strategy for Central Asia 2019-2025: Advancing Sovereignty and Economic Prosperity" during the Trump administration marked a strategic shift. How do external forces determine U.S. foreign policy in Central Asia? Let's explore the transactional nature of past engagements, the objectives of the new strategy, and the challenges and opportunities emerging in the region. USA 2024 Election Results Google Central Asia's Peripheral Status in U.S. Foreign Policy A key indicator of Central Asia's marginal position in U.S. foreign policy is that, historically, no sitting American president had ever visited the region or held a summit with all Central Asian leaders. Central Asia often remained overshadowed by other global priorities. There have been instances where Central Asian leaders visited the United States but did not secure meetings with the American president, underscoring the limited priority given to the region. However, in September 2023, President Biden hosted the first-ever U.S.-Central Asia Summit with the leaders of the five Central Asian countries, signaling a potential shift in engagement. Despite this unprecedented summit, high-level interactions remain infrequent. In 2024, there was only a foreign ministers' meeting , and it is not known whether there will be meetings at the level of heads of state in the future. This indicates that while there may be increasing attention, Central Asia is still not a primary focus in U.S. foreign policy. The Transactional Nature of U.S. Engagement U.S. foreign policy in Central Asia has historically been transactional, often influenced by global events rather than regional priorities. The U.S. engaged in the region not for its intrinsic importance but due to external factors such as the situation in Afghanistan, concerns over China's control of rare earth elements, and attempts to counterbalance Russia's historical influence. Military involvement in Afghanistan heightened Central Asia's strategic importance as a logistical hub and for regional security cooperation. Additionally, the U.S. explored alternative sources of rare earth metals in Central Asia to reduce dependence on China and initiated diplomatic and economic efforts to weaken Russia's ties in the region. The "U.S. Strategy for Central Asia 2019-2025" Adopted during the Trump administration, the "U.S. Strategy for Central Asia 2019-2025: Advancing Sovereignty and Economic Prosperity" signaled a renewed commitment to the region. The strategy aimed to build a more stable and prosperous Central Asia that is free to pursue political, economic, and security interests with a variety of partners on its own terms. The United States emphasized support for the sovereignty and independence of the Central Asian states, aiming to strengthen their resilience against short and long-term threats to their stability. The strategy outlined six overarching objectives : Support Sovereignty and Independence : Enhancing diplomatic engagement and providing assistance to strengthen democratic institutions and economic prosperity, helping Central Asian states function as cooperative partners. Reduce Terrorist Threats : Working with Central Asian nations to develop resilience to extremist ideologies and prevent the region from becoming a haven for terrorist organizations. Support Stability in Afghanistan : Encouraging Central Asian countries to develop economic and trade links with Afghanistan, contributing to regional stability. Encourage Regional Connectivity : Promoting closer ties between Central Asia and Afghanistan across energy, economic, cultural, trade, and security lines. Promote Rule of Law and Human Rights : Assisting in developing and implementing justice sector reforms, strengthening civil society, and enhancing government responsiveness. Promote U.S. Investment : Working with Central Asian countries to undertake reforms needed to attract more foreign investment, including from American businesses. The Future of the C5+1 Format Under Trump The strategy also emphasized the importance of the C5+1 diplomatic platform, which brings together representatives from the five Central Asian states and the United States to address common concerns and promote regional dialogue and cooperation. Under President Trump, the future of the C5+1 format at the presidential level remained uncertain. While the strategy outlined continued support for the platform, the actual engagement depended on the administration's priorities and responses to initiatives by Russia or China in the region. A lack of U.S. response to significant projects launched by these powers could be perceived as a sign of weakness, potentially diminishing American influence. Delegating Institutionalization to External Powers A unique phenomenon in Central Asia is the delegation of institutionalization processes to external actors. Central Asian nations increasingly allow countries like the U.S. and China to guide their institutional frameworks. This raises concerns about the region's autonomy and the long-term implications for regional integration. The reasons behind this delegation include the slow pace of intraregional integration, where countries often unite only in response to crises and prefer bilateral relations during stable periods. This sporadic cooperation opens the door for external powers to introduce their own formats of cooperation. The strong involvement of external powers is evident, with Central Asia showing openness to allowing these players to shape the regional agenda. Structures like the B5+1 Business Forums and the China-Central Asia Secretariat exemplify this trend. Moreover, the lack of a central coordinating body, unlike the European Union or ASEAN, makes Central Asia more dependent on external structures to coordinate policies, further enabling external actors to influence the region's institutional processes. Impact on Regional Integration Delegating institutionalization to external actors has both drawbacks and benefits for Central Asian integration. On the downside, relying on external powers may increase their influence over regional affairs, potentially sidelining the interests of Central Asian countries. Engaging with powerful external actors complicates balancing regional priorities with the interests of these powers. https://daryo.uz/en/2024/04/19/from-chil.body: Uzbekistan From childhood dream to entrepreneurial success: Elyor Bozorov's journey from Uzbekistan to the United States "Becoming an economist was a childhood dream. Why? Because economists know how to make a lot of money." This is how Elyor Bozorov begins his story. Bozorov was the founder of successful enterprises like Elmakon and olcha.uz in Uzbekistan, and now an IT entrepreneur in the United States. 19 April 2024, 20:04 11 min read 4,160 views 0 comments 2 "Becoming an economist was a childhood dream. Why? Because economists know how to make a lot of money." This is how Elyor Bozorov begins his story. Bozorov was the founder of successful enterprises like Elmakon and olcha.uz in Uzbekistan, and now an IT entrepreneur in the United States. Elyor Bozorov It all started with the farm My childhood coincided with the period of the collapse of the Soviet Union when finding normal consumer goods was also a thousand troubles. Our family moved from my hometown of Navoi to the capital, Tashkent, in search of a better life. I grew up under the supervision of my grandparents until I entered the fourth grade. My grandfather, the owner of a large farm, taught me the secrets of agriculture and livestock. Although at that time I did not understand the essence, watching my grandfather's reasonable management in the supply chain, and how he led the workers, I increasingly formed entrepreneurial, leadership skills. It was then that I realized what I wanted to achieve in this life. My parents wanted me to become a doctor, but my dream was to become an economist. The reason being: economists know how to earn money! Childhood adversities, the desire to help the family encouraged me to work on myself in all respects, be progressive in my studies and public affairs. Being an active student, I was repeatedly elected as “Minister of Education" and “President" at the school. When I was in the fifth grade, my mother opened a children's clothing store. Helping her to run the store after school taught me practical knowledge about supply chains, margins, accounting, money circulation. In the ninth grade, I was lucky enough to study for a year in the United States on an exchange program. With a grade point average of 3.7, I became a member of the American Club of Future Business Leaders and presented my business projects at national competitions. I was also awarded a special medal by the President Obama’s Administration for completing 200 hours of volunteer work. That year in America has installed in me the independence and interpersonal skills that are essential for an entrepreneur. Bozorov at his University graduation. A ticket to a happy life Studying at a prestigious university in Uzbekistan was considered as a luxury at that time. I couldn't pass the cost of education on to my parents, because living in the United States taught not only decision-making, but also financial independence. I was lucky to take part in the competition of the Ministry of Transportation in 2011 with my business project for the production of electric cars in Uzbekistan, and won a full four-year grant for any university. At a time when higher education was a dream if you didn’t have the money, this achievement was my ticket to a happy life. This ticket allowed me to become a student at the Faculty of Economics and Finance at the University of Westminster, one of the country’s leading international higher education institutions. The socks business. Next destination is Dubai While studying at university, I started my business. After a three-month market analysis, I came to the conclusion that selling socks is profitable. By showing my business project to my uncle, who is one of the largest distributors of mobile phones in Uzbekistan, I was able to get 100 thousand dollars to get started. During my trip to China, I ordered 30 thousand dollars worth of socks and started a wholesale business. Within three years I opened eight stores, which brought the company an annual revenue of almost $2.5mn. Right after graduating from university, I was invited to work for BM Electronics, a mobile phone and consumer electronics distribution company based in Dubai. It was a big step towards my goal of becoming a top-manager. I was tasked with solving a supply chain problem that was considered a problem point during the first six months of my career at the company. By implementing a new ERP-system in warehouse operations, I managed to expedite the delivery service by 20% - from 15 days to a week. Like Steve Jobs: “E verything was started from a small garage” During my time in Dubai, I founded a new online trading business in Central Asian countries – BMBOX.com. This was my first online project that offered a delivery service for electronics and perfumes from Dubai within a week. The project quickly became popular in Uzbekistan due to the fact that in just three steps it was possible to purchase products from different countries. Almost all new mobile phones were first sold on BMBOX.com and then on the open market. By 2016, the platform had sold almost 4,500 phones and perfumes worth $1.5mn. At the end of 2015, I returned to Uzbekistan and headed the BM Electronics business development team. In those years, young people were inspired by Steve Jobs, and stories in the genre “everything was started from a small garage” were very popular. And I also came up with an idea to assemble a team in my own garage. With this team, we established cooperation with HTC and were able to increase sales of phones of this brand by 60 %. Halal installments – in Elmakon In 2017, Uzbekistan’s economy was reformed and began to open up. To take distribution activities to a new level, I founded the retail chain Elmakon . Elmakon allowed us to directly communicate with customers and gave us a more realistic picture of the market. In two years, I launched 11 stores in different regions of Uzbekistan reaching $2mn monthly sales. In essence, Elmakon was a great opportunity to understand every single aspect of the business, because it involved marketing through all channels, supplying on time, retailing, warehousing, recruiting on a big scale, managing big teams, teamwork, negotiating with partners, and vendors, accounting, forecasting and planning, and everything else. The “cherry” of the Uzbek online business In December 2017, I launched another online sales platform - olcha.uz (olcha – cherry). The goal was to become the cherry on the cake of an online business. Thanks to the comprehensive website and CRM system developed by our team, at a time when the delivery of goods throughout Uzbekistan usually took a week, we set up delivery within 3 days. In 2020, due to the pandemic, online services have reached a new level, in particular, olcha.uz sold 20 thousand units of products worth $2.4mn through it. We have also been able to ensure timely and high-quality delivery of orders even under strict lockdown restrictions. We have brought Huawei to second place in popularity When Huawei started entering the Uzbek market, I received an offer from the company. My main task was to systematize the brand's online and retail sales. However after we started work, because of sanctions implemented by the US on Huawei, it could no longer use the Android system owned by Google. As a result, the company introduced its alternative operating system, HMS. Although the new operating system brought inconveniences to customers, we managed to increase sales of Huawei phones even more than expected (by 20%). By the end of 2019, we managed to make Huawei the most popular mobile phone after its competitor Samsung. Huawei has played an invaluable role in shaping my vision for big business and in shaping my skills of doing business in a large system. Bozorov standing in front of the White House Pandemic. Break. https://daryo.uz/en/2023/12/27/uzbekista.body: Auto Uzbekistan imports 83,800 cars from China in 11M 2023 The average prices for the imported vehicles remained steady at $18,000. 27 December 2023, 00:47 1 min read 4,800 views 0 comments 0 Uzbekistan has witnessed a remarkable surge in the import of passenger cars from China over the course of 11M 2023, marking a sixfold increase, as per the data reported by Tazabek, citing information from the General Administration of Customs of China. BYD car at the Uzbekistan-China Cooperation Expo. Moreover, in 8M 2023, Uzbekistan has significantly bolstered its imports of electric vehicles (EVs), reporting an influx of almost 1,500 EVs at a cost of $46.4mn . This marks an increase of 1,000 units compared to the same period last year. Notably, nearly 90% of these electric cars were imported from China, with the UAE, Germany, and Hong Kong following in the rankings. Additionally, in July, there was a resurgence in the demand for cars, with a 40% increase in sales of electric vehicles. The continuous growth in the car trade underscores the evolving dynamics of the automotive market between China and Uzbekistan. https://www.azernews.az/analysis/264495..body: Six years after war, South Caucasus faces historic chance for lasting peace 26 September 2026 08:30 (UTC+04:00) Ulviyya Poladova Read more For years, the world looked at Karabakh as a frozen conflict. Diplomats wrote their reports, mediators gathered around tables in European capitals, while along the line of contact Azerbaijani soldiers and civilians kept dying, again and again. The occupation dragged on for decades. And still Azerbaijan waited. Time after time Baku sat down at the negotiating table and agreed to principles recognized by the whole world, including the four UN Security Council resolutions that demanded the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of the occupying forces. Those documents stayed on paper. No one intended to carry them out, and the provocations along the border went on. On September 27, 2020, everything changed. The Azerbaijani army launched a counter-offensive operation in response to the large-scale provocations carried out by the Armenian armed forces along the front line. That Patriotic War ended in a glorious Victory that put an end to thirty years of occupation. Azerbaijan took back what was its own. It did not seize anything foreign; it simply returned what belonged to it by every law. These lands can rightly be called the cradle of peace. Because the Azerbaijani people fought for that peace to the very end. Azerbaijan showed that justice sometimes has to be defended on your own, when international mechanisms turn out to be powerless or indifferent. The South Caucasus has undergone a fundamental transformation over the past six years, moving from a region marked by unresolved conflict and instability toward new opportunities for peace, cooperation and development, political analyst Frank Musmar said in a commentary to AzerNEWS . "Six years ago, in 2020, the South Caucasus was a zone of unresolved conflict and chronic instability. Occupation continued, international law was not implemented, ceasefire violations were daily, and the entire regional architecture was hostage to one conflict. The security environment was unpredictable and fragile," he noted. According to the political analyst, the situation today is completely different. He noted that Azerbaijan’s restoration of its territorial integrity and sovereignty had removed the root of what caused the conflict. "With Azerbaijan restoring its territorial integrity and sovereignty in full accordance with international law, the root cause of war in the region has been removed. The long-standing conflict is over," Musmar emphasized. He stressed that the current regional environment provides new opportunities for cooperation and economic development. The expert stressed that Azerbaijan, in particular, has established itself as a responsible state, a reliable energy supplier to Europe. The analyst pointed out that this transformation is taking place against the backdrop of growing instability in several parts of the world. "While wars and crises are escalating in the Middle East, Eastern Europe, and other regions, Azerbaijan has established itself as a responsible state, a reliable energy supplier to Europe, a key pillar of the Middle Corridor, and a country that ensures security and stability not only within its borders but far beyond," Musmar highlighted. He added that the atmosphere in the South Caucasus has changed from confrontation to opportunities for cooperation, connectivity and development. Commenting on the prospects for lasting peace in the region, Musmar said that the current period represents a historic opportunity. "The main opportunity is historic: for the first time in more than 30 years, we have a real chance to achieve lasting peace. The path to that is clear — mutual recognition of territorial integrity, full respect for sovereignty, border delimitation, and the opening of all communications, including the Zangezur corridor," the analyst said. According to him, peace will bring enormous dividends: opening of borders, integration of the South Caucasus into global transport and energy routes, foreign investment, and prosperity for all peoples of the region. "The main challenge is the persistence of revanchist thinking. Lasting peace requires Armenia to finally accept the new realities, abandon territorial claims, amend its constitution and other legal documents that still contain claims against Azerbaijan, and stop arming itself beyond defensive needs," the academic researcher added. Speaking about the forces in Armenia that continue to hold the old mindset and on whether international pressure is needed, Musmar said that such forces remain a challenge to the peace agenda. "Despite the historic chance for peace, there are still revanchist forces in Armenia — remnants of the former junta, nationalist circles, and their sponsors abroad — who live with the myths of the past, who poison their society with hatred, and who openly call for revenge," he said. The analyst stated that such rhetoric could undermine efforts toward peace and argued that Azerbaijan had demonstrated goodwill by putting forward peace proposals. "Azerbaijan has shown goodwill and has proposed peace. But peace cannot be one-sided," Musmar stressed. At the same time, he pointed out that the primary responsibility for choosing the path toward peace rests with Armenia itself. However, Musmar also argued that the international community and countries with interests in the South Caucasus have a role to play. "The support of regional actors who sincerely want stability — first and foremost Türkiye, as well as partners interested in connectivity and energy security — is already important. But consistent international pressure and a principled position against revanchism are needed to ensure that Armenia does not miss this historic window for peace," he added. https://www.azernews.az/nation/264561.ht.body: Azerbaijanis pay tribute to heroes of Second Karabakh War 27 September 2026 09:46 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more Azerbaijan is marking September 27 as Remembrance Day, commemorating the start of the 44-day Second Karabakh War six years ago. Since the early hours of the morning, citizens have been visiting the Second Alley of Martyrs in Baku to pay tribute to servicemen who lost their lives during the war. People are also honoring the fallen in other parts of the country, laying carnations on their graves and remembering their sacrifice. The Second Karabakh War began on September 27, 2020, and lasted 44 days. The conflict ended with Azerbaijan regaining control of significant territories and subsequently restoring its territorial integrity. September 27 was established as Remembrance Day to honor the memory of the servicemen who were killed while fighting for Azerbaijan's territorial integrity and sovereignty. The day is marked annually by commemorative events across the country. On Remembrance Day, people visit the graves and memorials of the fallen, paying tribute to their courage and sacrifice. Various events are also held to preserve the memory of those who lost their lives during the war and to convey their stories of heroism to future generations. The day is observed not only in Baku but also in Azerbaijan's regions and by Azerbaijani communities abroad, where commemorative ceremonies are held in memory of the fallen. Tags: Remembrance Day Azerbaijani martyrs Second Karabakh War
