https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/15.body: Listen (6 mins) Save Share South Korea embraces Central Asian leaders, looking to boost regional clout on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev shakes hands with South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung at the Blue House in Seoul, South Korea, on September 15, 2026, ahead of the first South Korea-Central Asia summit [Jung Yeon-je/Pool via Reuters] By Agnieszka Pikulicka-Wilczewska Published On 15 Sep 2026 15 Sep 2026 South Korea is set to welcome the heads of the five Central Asian states for the first-ever presidential summit between Seoul and the region, a meeting local media have dubbed “historic”. Wednesday’s summit, preceded by bilateral meetings between South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and leaders of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan, aims to deepen economic engagement between Central Asia and the host, and put them on a more permanent footing. “The first expectation is political. The summit will raise a dialogue that has existed since 2007 to the level of heads of state. But the real test is whether it produces a workable agenda in critical minerals, energy, digital technologies and transport,” Sanat Kushkumbayev, from the Kazakhstan Institute for Strategic Studies, told Al Jazeera. “For Central Asia, the value of the meeting is also in showing that the region can engage external partners collectively without giving up national priorities. I would expect a framework for regular high-level cooperation, followed by more detailed bilateral deals.” Central Asian states, which are increasingly positioning themselves as a bloc known as C5+, are looking for investments, access to technology and to diversify their international partnerships beyond Moscow and Beijing, analysts said, while South Korea needs to diversify its economic and supply-chain dependencies. “Currently, South Korea has a limited domestic resource base and a significant supply-chain exposure to China, particularly in critical materials, components and other industrial inputs. Central Asia can offer South Korea critical minerals, energy, alternative production opportunities and greater supply chain diversification. Korea, in return, can provide technology, capital and industrial expertise,” said Sabina Insebayeva, a political scientist at Nazarbayev University. Advertisement She explained that the K-Silk Road initiative, South Korea’s strategy for Central Asia launched in 2024, aims to go beyond securing raw materials to develop processing, manufacturing and technology capacity in partnership with local companies. Central Asia no longer wants to position itself as an exporter of raw materials. Instead, it is seeking the skills and technology needed for domestic industrial hubs. South Korea can act as a long-term partner to achieve this goal, particularly in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. “Kazakhstan already accounts for much of South Korea’s trade and investment presence in the region, so it can reasonably push for larger industrial projects, research facilities and local supplier networks. The difficult part will be moving from assembly and memorandums to genuine localisation and commercial production,” Kushkumbayev explained. By the end of 2025, the lump-sum volume of South Korea’s direct investment in Central Asia reached about $6.4bn. But its appeal in Central Asia goes beyond its potential as an investor and technology provider, as a social connection has long been in place. South Korea’s historical ties to the region In 1937, at the order of Joseph Stalin, more than 170,000 Soviet Koreans were forcibly relocated from the USSR’s Far East to Soviet Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, under the pretext of preventing Japanese sabotage. “When my grandparents arrived in southern Kazakhstan, it was autumn, and it was already cold, but they had no houses to live in. That winter they lived with local Kazakh people who supported them and deportees from other countries,” said Roman Zakharov, a half-Korean artist from Kazakhstan. His grandparents waited for a year to receive housing from the authorities, but as deportees, they had no permission to leave the collective farms they worked on until Stalin’s death. The deportees and their descendants, collectively called Koryo-saram, have sought to stay connected to their roots, but this has not been easy. “Koryo-saram tried to adapt local products like carrots to make Korean pickled food. But local Korean culture changed through time ... My grandmother tried to listen to South Korean programmes on TV, but she couldn’t understand anything. It was a different language than my grandparents spoke,” said Zakharov, whose art pieces were shown at an exhibition in South Korea in 2023. When the Soviet Union collapsed, South Korea began founding cultural centres across Central Asia, where local people, including Koryo-saram, could learn the language and engage with Korean culture. Zakharov’s sister attended traditional Korean dance classes. Advertisement But the breakthrough for Korean soft power in Central Asia came in the 2010s when soap operas and K-pop became the talk of the town. “The South Korean government has been popularising Korean culture in Central Asia and using it as a soft power which is already very strong,” said Aiganym Toleuliyeva, a 28-year-old Kazakh researcher, who moved to South Korea to study in 2019. “In Astana, there is a Korean kimchi festival, and a Korean music festival funded by the Korean embassy. It’s through this kind of soft power and encouraging young people from Central Asia to study in South Korea that Korea is expanding in the region.” When she first visited Korea in 2015, few locals were familiar with her homeland. But as time went by, the relations grew too. Today, Central Asia is a tourist destination for South Koreans and for some in the region, Seoul’s appeal extends beyond music, the beauty industry and soap operas. “Central Asian workers in Korea are also treated better than immigrants in Russia, where the situation is becoming increasingly dangerous,” said Toleuliyeva. “Today Korea offers more opportunities for immigrants from Central Asia; they feel supported. People from Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan – and soon Kazakhstan, too – can join special programmes for labour workers, study the language for free and move to Korea to work on construction sites.” In a region trying to diversify its partnerships beyond China and Russia, South Korea could be seen as a less politically loaded partner. “There is a geopolitical element too. Seoul wants a stronger and more visible position in a region where China, Russia, the European Union, Turkiye and the Gulf states are already active,” Kushkumbayev said. “But the Korean approach is likely to remain commercially driven and relatively low-key, rather than openly geopolitical.”

WASHINGTON -- Ukrainian skeleton racer and Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych is urging US lawmakers and the State Department to deny visas to Russian athletes who seek to compete under the Russian flag at the 2028 Summer Olympic Games in Los Angeles, arguing that Moscow has turned sport into an instrument of war propaganda. Heraskevych, who is visiting Washington to meet with members of Congress and other US decisionmakers, said the United States has a role to play in preventing the Los Angeles Olympics from becoming a platform for Kremlin messaging. His appeal comes after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) moved to restore the Russian Olympic Committee's status and lifted recommendations that had restricted Russian participation in international competitions. "We are living in a real world," Heraskevych told RFE/RL in an interview on September 14. "Competitions are taking place in real countries, in real places." He said that while international sports bodies can make recommendations, governments control access to their territory -- giving the United States a potential means of preventing Russian athletes from taking part. Heraskevych is calling on Washington to maintain restrictions that allow eligible Russian athletes to compete only as neutrals, without Russian flags, symbols, or official delegations. "Our main goal is to show these particular cases, these particular names, and to present that sport is not out of politics," he said. Russian Sport 'Used In Propaganda' Heraskevych said policymakers need to abandon what he called the mistaken assumption that sport can be separated from politics. Many people "believe that sport is out of politics," he said. "But Russian sport is being used in propaganda." He pointed to Russian athletes' participation in political events, support for President Vladimir Putin's ruling political establishment, and activities connected to Russia's war effort against Ukraine. Heraskevych also cited what he described as Russian athletes' involvement in events linked to Ukrainian children who were forcibly taken to Russia and their participation in military-related activities. Embed share With 20,000 Teddy Bears In Washington, Ukrainian Activists Say 'Bring Kids Back' From Russia by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:02:00 0:00 He said the use of sport for political purposes predates Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, pointing to the massive doping scandal surrounding Russian sport and the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. "We all remember how Russian security services were involved in this scandal," he said. Heraskevych said Russia has since expanded its use of sport to promote militarization and normalize the occupation of Ukrainian territory. He cited Russia's so-called Youth Army movement, which he said is aimed at preparing a new generation for military service, as well as sporting competitions in which Russian organizers present occupied Ukrainian territories as part of Russia. "These are just a few examples of how Russia uses sport, uses this platform to spread their propaganda, to empower and to make their war machine powerful," he said. Kateryna Lisunova, a media adviser at the US-based nonprofit Razom for Ukraine, which is supporting Heraskevych's Washington campaign, said the effort is also aimed at warning Americans about how Moscow uses seemingly apolitical institutions. "It is important to inform American representatives and American people as well as for them to not become a tool in Russian hands in war propaganda," Lisunova told RFE/RL. She said Russia has used "many good things such as art and sport" to promote and normalize the war and make audiences feel "as if nothing is happening." Visa Bans Heraskevych said visa restrictions could provide a practical way for the US to enforce its own policy regardless of decisions by international sports organizations. He pointed to recent cases in Europe and Canada in which Russian athletes were denied visas after evidence was presented to authorities of their support for Russia's war or use of pro-Kremlin symbols. He cited a 2026 European Taekwondo Championship in Germany, where Russian athlete Vladislav Larin was denied a visa after evidence was submitted showing that he had publicly collected money for the Russian military. Ukrainian Olympic Athlete: Russia Uses Sports As Part Of 'War Machine" by RFE/RL No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:07 0:00 He also cited a 2026 junior world curling championship where Russian athletes were denied visas after evidence was presented showing them posing with symbols associated with Russia's invasion. Latvia has similarly denied visas to Russian athletes seeking to participate in international competitions, Heraskevych said. "We have cases, successful cases," he said. "I believe it's a great experience, and we should share it with the US." He acknowledged that visa bans alone would not change Russia's policy but argued they could prevent international sports events from being exploited as propaganda platforms. "I believe it's one of the possibilities what we can do, and it's also what lawmakers can do," he said. Heraskevych's Own Olympic Protest The Ukrainian athlete's campaign is also rooted in his own experience at the 2026 Winter Olympics, where he was penalized after displaying a message on his helmet honoring Ukrainian athletes killed during Russia's war against Ukraine. Heraskevych said he still does not understand why he was disqualified , arguing the message was simply an act of remembrance. "I believe it's connected, and it's not a coincidence," he said. For Heraskevych, the dispute is ultimately about what the Olympic movement is supposed to represent. "The Olympic Games and Olympic movement -- it's everything about peace, about peaceful mission, about building bridges," he said. "But when you're allowed to compete and giving this platform to terrorists, then it has nothing to do with peace and peaceful mission." He said the goal of his Washington visit is not to prevent the Olympics from serving as a venue for international competition but to ensure Russia cannot use the event to legitimize its war. "We should protect this platform and we should try to make it a better place, but not a place where Russia will spread their propaganda," Heraskevych said. https://www.rferl.org/a/us-house-panel-a.body: News 'Putin Is Watching': US House Panel Advances Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill By Alex Raufoglu September 15, 2026 10:52 CET 'Putin Is Watching': US House Panel Advances Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google The US House Rules Committee has advanced legislation named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham (pictured). The bill targets Russian banks, energy revenues, and oligarchs. WASHINGTON -- The US House Rules Committee has advanced legislation imposing tougher sanctions on Russia and Iran, clearing a key procedural hurdle for a possible House vote later this week but exposing deep Democratic concerns over the measure's expansion of presidential tariff authority. The committee voted 7-3 late on September 14 to advance a rule setting up debate on the legislation. Debate on the rule is expected to begin around noon local time on September 15. If the rule is approved, the House is expected to consider final passage of the sanctions package on September 16. The legislation, known as the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, is named for the late Republican senator who championed the measure before his death. The Senate approved the legislation by an overwhelming 86-11 vote in August, giving the House a measure with substantial bipartisan backing in the upper chamber. US Representative Wilson: Russia Sanctions Will Impact China, India by RFE/RL No media source currently available 0:00 0:00:53 0:00 The House version was introduced by Republican Representative Michael McCaul of Texas with Democratic Representative Steny Hoyer of Maryland and other bipartisan cosponsors. But the legislation has faced a more difficult path in the House, where Democrats have objected primarily to provisions that would give President Donald Trump broad new authority to impose tariffs on countries buying Russian energy or helping Moscow evade sanctions. McCaul: 'Putin Is Watching' McCaul, a senior Republican voice on foreign policy, urged lawmakers to move quickly. "Putin is watching," McCaul told the committee, warning that Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea were working together to challenge the United States and its allies. He argued that the legislation would target the financial networks supporting Russia's war effort, including Russian officials, oligarchs, financial institutions and the so-called shadow fleet used to transport Russian oil. The bill also extends sanctions on Iran that are due to expire at the end of the year, targeting funding for Iran's energy and weapons sectors. McCaul argued that Russia and Iran could not be treated as separate challenges because of their military cooperation. Embed share Russia Expert Melia Points To 'Evidence That Sanctions Are Working' by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:01 0:00 The legislation would give Trump authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on major purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas and countries accused of helping Moscow evade energy sanctions. Democrats say that authority is too broad and could raise prices for American consumers or be used beyond the bill's stated Russia-related purpose. Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said he strongly supports additional pressure on Russia but opposed the bill in its current form. Meeks said the president already has extensive authority to impose sanctions on Russia and argued that the legislation would do less to force new sanctions than it would to expand presidential control over tariffs. "American families will pay the cost of this bill. Vladimir Putin will not," he argued. SEE ALSO: Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill Could Reach Trump’s Desk Within Days, Says Congressman Meeks and other Democrats proposed amendments that would have removed the secondary tariff provisions, tightened the president's ability to waive sanctions, clarified that the European Union could not be treated as a single "country" for tariff purposes, and provided additional military financing for Ukraine. Another Democratic proposal would have identified 10 countries as initially eligible for tariffs of up to 100 percent because of their purchases of Russian oil and gas or their alleged role in sanctions evasion. The list included China, India, Azerbaijan, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, Hungary, Slovakia, Singapore, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan. Meeks also sought to require that sanctions be waived only when doing so was "vital to the national security of the US." The committee rejected the Democratic amendments. SEE ALSO: Trump Says Russia, Ukraine Agree To Halt Strikes On Energy Targets Hoyer, a Democratic cosponsor of the bill, also sought a change that would specifically identify countries potentially subject to the tariffs. He nevertheless opposed removing the tariff mechanism altogether. "If we do not pass this bill, there will be great joy in the Kremlin and great devastation in Kyiv," Hoyer said. The dispute reflects a broader dilemma for House Democrats: many support stronger measures against Russia and continued assistance for Ukraine, but they have also opposed what they regard as unchecked presidential use of tariff powers. The White House supports the sanctions legislation, and Trump has indicated he wants Congress to provide the administration with additional tools to pressure Russia and countries that continue buying Russian energy. The timing is also significant. The House is scheduled to leave Washington later this week for an extended recess ahead of the midterm elections, potentially making this one of the last opportunities for lawmakers to act on the legislation this year. 'Leverage On Mr. Putin' After the Rules Committee vote, McCaul told RFE/RL in an interview that the legislation was needed to give Washington leverage over Russian President Vladimir Putin and push him toward negotiations. "Without leverage on Mr. Putin, he'll never come to the negotiating table," McCaul argued. He pointed to his meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and argued that Ukraine needs both military and economic support while the United States seeks to pressure Moscow toward a settlement. "We believe that it will put enough economic pressure on Mr. Putin to finally come to the table and negotiate a peaceful settlement," McCaul said. SEE ALSO: Russia's Jet-Powered Drones: A Major New Threat To Ukraine Amid Speeding Arms Race Asked about concerns that the bill could be used against European allies, McCaul rejected the argument that it would give Trump unrestricted authority to expand tariffs. "The bill very narrowly defines the tariffs," he said, arguing that the provisions focus on the largest importers of Russian energy and cannot simply be expanded to other countries. McCaul also pointed to support for the legislation from European officials and Zelenskyy, saying the measure could represent an important moment in efforts to pressure Moscow. "I think this is a moment in time we have a chance to vote on something that can really change the course of history," he said. McCaul said he was confident the bill would be approved if it reached the House floor. "I'm optimistic this will be passed on the floor and will be signed by the president," he said. He also dismissed arguments that the debate should be viewed primarily through the lens of domestic politics. "Putin wants nothing more than for this bill to fail, and it plays right into his hands," McCaul said. "This is not about domestic politics. This is about saving Ukraine from this aggression from Putin. A vote against this bill is a vote for Putin." https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-c.body: Ukraine A Quiet Ukrainian Counteroffensive, A 'Rout' For Russian Forces By Mike Eckel September 15, 2026 17:30 CET A Quiet Ukrainian Counteroffensive, A 'Rout' For Russian Forces Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Ukrainian forces have built a line of defenses, anchored by the two cities of Kramatorsk and Slovyansk, that Russian troops are hellbent on capturing. Sometime around late May, as Russia's all-out invasion neared the 4 1/2-year mark and the summer fighting season shifted into higher gear, Ukrainian commanders quietly ordered some of the country's most battle-hardened units into positions about 50 kilometers north of the Donetsk region city of Slovyansk. Mainly taken from Ukraine's Third Army Corps, the units confronted a bulge in the 1,100-kilometer front line where Russia's 20th Combined Arms Army had been grinding westward, pushing out from a bridgehead on the west bank of the Zherebets River amid villages, farmland, and rolling fields. The goal for Russia: cut off supply lines for Ukrainian forces in Slovyansk, one of two main Ukrainian-held cities in the Donetsk region. Ukrainian soldiers unload supplies from a military vehicle as they arrive for a combat mission in the Donetsk region on September 9. Over the summer months, Ukrainian forces battled northward out of the town of Lyman while also pushing to the south toward the villages of Ridkodub, Katerynivka, and Nove. That effort, according to open-source researchers, experts who have traveled to the battlefield, and Ukrainian and Russian war bloggers, is nearing a remarkable success for Ukrainian forces: Much of the Russian force in the area has been pushed back to the Zherebets River, with small pockets of soldiers encircled and likely to be captured or killed in the coming days. Map: A Quiet Ukrainian Counteroffensive Pushes Russia Back (September 15, 2026) By most accounts, it is shaping up to be one of the largest shifts on the battlefield in months, possibly in a year. For the moment, the success relieves some pressure on the Ukrainian defenses trying to hold the line of cities, towns, and roads running north to south and encompassing Slovyansk and the city of Kramatorsk, a swath known as an "agglomeration." Moreover, the nearly four-month offensive also took place in an unusual information vacuum, with virtually no information leaking out among war bloggers on Telegram in Ukraine or Russia until recent days. "Ukrainians took back some of the territory. Russia lost more territory," Konrad Muzyka, a Polish-based military expert who has spent substantial time on Ukraine's front lines, told RFE/RL. "It's significant, not because of what's happening around Lyman, but because I think it thwarted a big Russian plan that was seeking to envelop the Slovyansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration from the north and from the south." "The Russians keep trying this envelopment" of the entire Donetsk region, said Dara Massicot, an expert on the Russian military with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, a Washington-based think tank. "For now, it looks like the northern attempt is blunted." SEE ALSO: On Ukraine's Battlefield, Russia Has Lost Ground, Experts Say. But Don't Expect A Major Reversal For Kyiv. A chorus on Russian war channels on Telegram, meanwhile, has also pointed to significant Ukrainian gains. "A rout on the Lyman front," said one prominent Telegram blogger named Anatoly Shariy, a former Ukrainian politician who has been convicted in absentia of high treason in Ukraine and sentenced to 15 years in prison. "The situation at Lyman is alarming," said Rybar , a Telegram blogger previously affiliated with the Russian Defense Ministry. "We suffered an unpleasant tactical defeat," said another channel, called Dnevnik Desantnika . "However, encirclement did not occur; most of our personnel were withdrawn, and now everything depends on whether [Ukrainian] forces can exploit this success east of the Zherebets River." At least one pro-Russian blogger, Yury Kotenok , complained specifically about the lack of information that has leaked out from Ukrainian sources. "Ukraine is conducting an offensive near Lyman under information silence," he wrote. "Silence on our part is already customary, but on the enemy's side it seems somewhat unusual, which is alarming. Here we have a deliberate, targeted regime of silence." SEE ALSO: Here's Why Russia's Vladimir Putin Is Fixated On Ukraine's Donbas Ukraine's military press office declined to comment, citing ongoing operations. But in a statement released on September 15, the commander for the Third Army Corps, Brigadier General Andriy Biletskiy, broadly confirmed the counteroffensive. "We confirm reports of a Ukrainian Army offensive in the north of Donetsk Oblast. Maintaining information silence, the units eliminated pockets of enemy infiltration," he was quoted as saying. "There is currently a lot of information in open sources suggesting that the ultimate goal of our offensive operations is to reach the banks of the Zherebets River.... There will be good news." The Russian Defense Ministry did not respond to a query seeking comment. The battlefield success is unlikely to translate into any broader strategic shift for Ukraine, military experts said. Overall, Kyiv remains at a disadvantage, outnumbered and in many places outgunned by Russia. SEE ALSO: On Ukraine's Battlefield, Spring Weather, New Fighting Season, A Big Russian Assault Despite suffering astronomical casualties and losing ground in some places, Russia continues to grind forward along parts of the front line. Military commanders have prioritized trying to capture Slovyansk and Kramatorsk, which would give them control over the entirety of the Donetsk region -- and the entire Donbas. That is a major priority for Putin and the Kremlin. Russia has vowed to capture all of the Donbas by force if Ukraine refuses to cede the territory it still holds, a step Kyiv has firmly ruled out. The issue of territorial control in the Donbas is a key sticking point in the on-again, off-again US-led peace efforts. Still, 2026 has been a relatively stable year for Ukraine's frontline troops; in some places, Kyiv has taken back more territory than Russia has gained. The success of the Lyman counteroffensive also highlights the fighting prowess of some of Ukraine's best units -- including the Third Army Corps -- and some of the continuing problems Russia has had on the battlefield, particularly as it sends new volunteers to the front with minimal training. Ukrainian troops patrol a road near Kramatorsk, Donetsk region, on September 11. "I think it shows that the Russians can concentrate [only] in one main sector at a time, which right now is in southern Donetsk. That occasionally opens a few weaker spots elsewhere that can be exploited," Massicot said. "I get the sense that the 20th Combined Arms Army wasn't the strongest and so it might have been a good spot [for Ukraine] to push on," she said. "Ukraine has now effectively removed the encirclement threat to [Lyman] and are threatening the Russian salient north of the city," said Black Bird Group, a Finnish-based research organization. "The Russian summer campaign of 2026 can be considered a failure," said Emil Kastehelmi, the group's co-founder. https://www.amnesty.org/fr/latest/news/2.body: La Russie a employé des pratiques trompeuses, coercitives et fondées sur l’exploitation, dans le but de recruter des étrangers pour qu’ils rejoignent ses forces armées, et de les envoyer combattre en Ukraine, écrit Amnesty International dans une nouvelle synthèse rendue publique jeudi 10 septembre. Dans de nombreux cas, cela constitue une violation des droits humains et relève de la traite des personnes, qui reste étendue en Russie et dont la communauté internationale doit se préoccuper en urgence. Les recherches effectuées décrivent comment des recruteurs ont attiré sous des prétextes fallacieux au sein des forces armées russes des individus venant de l’étranger, et ont exploité la situation précaire de migrants et de réfugiés déjà présents en Russie. Les personnes prises pour cible sont majoritairement issues de pays à faible revenu du sud global. « Les recherches effectuées par Amnesty montrent que l’armée russe renforce ses rangs avec des étrangers vulnérables sur le plan économique, et les utilise comme chair à canon dans la guerre d’agression contre l’Ukraine. Le niveau d’exploitation et de coercition que cela implique nous a amenés à conclure que dans de nombreux cas, cela relève de la traite des êtres humains, ainsi que la définit le Protocole de Palerme », a déclaré Agnès Callamard, secrétaire générale d’Amnesty International. « S’appuyant sur des voies migratoires pré-existantes caractérisées par l’exploitation et des pratiques abusives à l’égard des migrant·e·s et des réfugié·e·s en Russie, des recruteurs ont établi un système de coercition, de fraude et de tromperie, notamment des promesses creuses faisant miroiter des emplois civils ou non-combattants, afin d’engager des étrangers dans l’armée. Une fois que les victimes ont signé les documents qu’on leur présente, souvent dans une langue qu’elles ne comprennent pas, des commandants militaires restreignent leurs mouvements, les déploient en première ligne avec une préparation minimale, et menacent ceux qui cherchent à s’en extraire. » La synthèse s’appuie sur les témoignages de personnes originaires du Brésil, de Colombie, de Cuba, d’Égypte, de Sierra Leone, du Sri Lanka, de Somalie et d’Afrique du Sud, recueillis dans deux camps ukrainiens de prisonniers de guerre entre 2024 et 2026, et sur des conversations avec des étrangers servant actuellement au sein des forces russes, ainsi que des membres de leur famille, des avocat·e·s, des défenseur·e·s des droits humains et des journalistes. Parmi leurs principaux outils pour recruter des étrangers, les autorités russes ont tiré parti de la situation irrégulière de personnes restées sur le territoire au-delà de la durée de leur visa de travail, ainsi que de la situation précaire d’étrangers accusés d’infractions pénales, leur présentant un engagement au sein de l’armée comme une solution préférable à une arrestation et une expulsion. Les recherches effectuées par Amnesty montrent que l’armée russe renforce ses rangs avec des étrangers vulnérables sur le plan économique, et les utilise comme chair à canon. Agnès Callamard, secrétaire générale d’Amnesty International Amnesty International a recueilli les propos de deux Sri-Lankais recrutés après avoir dépassé la durée de leur visa de travail, ainsi que de personnes originaires de Cuba et d’Égypte, incarcérées pour détention présumée de stupéfiants, qui se sont vu proposer la possibilité de signer des contrats militaires au lieu de purger ou terminer leur peine de prison. L’organisation a également reçu le témoignage d’un réfugié originaire d’Afrique centrale qui a été placé en détention après l’expiration de son statut de protection temporaire, et qui a été menacé d’expulsion à moins qu’il ne s’engage au sein des forces armées de la Russie. Passer sous silence ou présenter sous un faux jour les risques encourus et la nature spécifique du travail proposé est devenu un élément clé du recrutement de migrants par l’armée russe. Le service militaire est généralement présenté comme une fonction de soutien non-combattante, comme le fait de travailler dans une cantine militaire ou comme chauffeur loin de la première ligne des combats. Les deux Sri-Lankais interrogés ont déclaré qu’on leur avait fait croire qu’ils travailleraient comme cuisiniers, mais ont en fait été envoyés se battre en première ligne. Ils ont été capturés au bout de quelques semaines par les forces ukrainiennes. « L’ampleur des combats est inimaginable. On ne voit pas de soldats ukrainiens, seulement des drones. Des drones partout », a dit l’un d’eux. « Jamais je n’y retournerais. » Des agents locaux et des offres d’emploi trompeuses sur Internet ont joué un rôle central dans le système visant à duper des étrangers au sein même de leur pays. Des personnes originaires du Brésil, de Colombie, de Sierra Leone, de Somalie, d’Afrique du Sud et du Sri Lanka, recrutées hors de Russie, ont déclaré qu’on leur avait fait de fausses promesses d’emplois civils dans les secteurs de la sécurité, de la logistique, de la construction, de l’informatique, entre autres, souvent avec l’assurance qu’elles percevraient des salaires élevés et bénéficieraient d’une procédure accélérée d’obtention de la nationalité russe – pour se retrouver finalement engagées de manière frauduleuse dans les forces armées à leur arrivée. Un Sud-Africain qui avait postulé en ligne pour un emploi de chauffeur en Pologne a reçu de la part d’un agent sur WhatsApp des instructions lui demandant de prendre un vol pour Moscou afin d’aller récupérer un camion qu’il devait ensuite conduire jusqu’en Pologne, a déclaré son épouse à Amnesty International. « À son arrivée à Moscou, on lui a tout pris [...] On lui a dit qu’il n’irait pas en Pologne et qu’il allait devenir soldat. » De nombreuses recrues ont reçu des promesses de salaires lucratifs et de bonus d’embauche qui ne se sont pas concrétisées. Si certaines ont perçu des paiements partiels avant d’être capturées, beaucoup ont indiqué n’avoir rien reçu du tout. Au-delà de la rémunération, toutes les personnes interrogées ont dit avoir été particulièrement motivées par les promesses concernant les procédures d’obtention de la nationalité russe. Toutes ont signalé que leur liberté de mouvement avait fait l’objet de lourdes restrictions après qu’elles ont signé les contrats militaires. Des recrues venues du Brésil et du Sri Lanka ont déclaré que leurs passeports et téléphones portables leur ont été confisqués durant leur entraînement ou avant leur déploiement en première ligne. D’autres ont signalé qu’elles ne pouvaient pas quitter les centres où elles ont été conduites après la signature des papiers, et que les divers trajets s’effectuaient dans le secret et de manière strictement contrôlée. Pedro, un informaticien brésilien, recruté après avoir signé ce qu’il pensait être un contrat pour un emploi bien rémunéré dans le domaine de la technologie en Russie, a déclaré qu’il avait dit à son commandant qu’il voulait partir, mais que celui-ci lui avait répondu : « Si vous essayez de vous enfuir, soit vous irez en prison soit nous vous tuerons. » Le manque d’expérience militaire semble ne constituer aucun obstacle au recrutement, et la plupart des engagés sont déployés dans des zones de combat actif au bout d’à peine deux semaines d’entraînement. Un grand nombre ont signalé un manque de préparation, des équipements insuffisants, et une communication limitée avec les commandants en raison de la barrière de la langue. Cela suggère que le recrutement d’étrangers est nourri par la volonté des troupes russes d’augmenter le nombre de soldats en première ligne, sans guère se soucier de leur aptitude au combat et en affichant un mépris manifeste pour la vie humaine. Les pratiques recensées dans le cadre de ces recherches suscitent de graves inquiétudes, tant la Russie a bafoué ses obligations en vertu du droit international, notamment en se livrant semble-t-il à la traite des êtres humains, et en s’abstenant : de poursuivre et combattre cette trai

Les autorités tunisiennes doivent libérer le responsable de l’opposition Rached Ghannouchi , annuler ses condamnations et mettre fin aux poursuites à caractère politique qui le visent, marquées par de graves violations du droit à un procès équitable, a déclaré Amnesty International jeudi 10 septembre. Dans l’attente de sa libération, l’organisation les appelle également à lui permettre sans délai d’accéder à des soins médicaux adaptés. Ce dirigeant du parti Ennahda et ancien président du Parlement, âgé de 84 ans, est détenu arbitrairement depuis son arrestation en avril 2023 et a fait l’objet de multiples poursuites à caractère politique. Les autorités ont engagé au moins 12 procédures pénales distinctes contre lui, qui ont abouti à la prononciation de plusieurs condamnations et de peines d’emprisonnement qui, cumulées, s’élèvent à 107 ans et viennent s’ajouter à une peine de réclusion à perpétuité prononcée contre lui le 1 er juin 2026 dans l’affaire de l’« appareil sécuritaire secret ». « Le dernier jugement rendu à l’encontre de Rached Ghannouchi est la première condamnation à perpétuité d’un responsable politique de premier plan depuis la révolution de 2011 en Tunisie et constitue une nette escalade du recours des autorités à la justice pénale pour s’en prendre à des figures de l’opposition, a déclaré Heba Morayef, directrice régionale pour le Moyen-Orient et l’Afrique du Nord à Amnesty International. « Les procès et poursuites à répétition dont il a fait l’objet montrent à quel point les autorités sont déterminées à étouffer la dissidence politique. Ils révèlent aussi combien le système judiciaire est politisé, au mépris du droit à un procès équitable. » Les demandes d’Amnesty International font écho aux conclusions du Groupe de travail des Nations unies sur la détention arbitraire, qui a estimé dans son avis n° 63/2025 que la détention de Rached Ghannouchi était arbitraire, en invoquant l’absence de base juridique, le non-respect des normes internationales relatives au droit à un procès équitable et la discrimination fondée sur l’opinion politique. Les différentes condamnations de Rached Ghannouchi ont fait suite à des procédures gravement entachées d’irrégularités, notamment la privation d’accès à une assistance juridique, des procès en son absence sans qu’il en soit avisé et le recours à des vidéos trafiquées, des témoignages anonymes et des accusations dénuées de fondement sans que sa défense ait la possibilité de contester ces éléments. Les poursuites à son encontre – pour des accusations allant d’infractions concernant des propos protégés par le droit à la liberté d’expression à des allégations de délits financiers liées à un don caritatif fait en public en 2016 au Croissant-Rouge tunisien – représentent une violation manifeste de ses droits à la liberté d’expression et d’association, à un procès équitable et à la participation politique. La détention prolongée de Rached Ghannouchi s’est accompagnée d’une grave dégradation de son état de santé. Il est atteint de la maladie de Parkinson et souffre d’apnée du sommeil et de vives douleurs dans une jambe. Ces problèmes ont été exacerbés par le fait d’être détenu dans des cellules non ventilées lors d’épisodes de chaleur où les températures dépassaient 50 °C. Il a perdu deux fois connaissance lors d’un entretien avec son avocat le 17 juillet et a été hospitalisé cinq fois entre juillet et août 2026. Lors de ses séjours à l’hôpital, les autorités ont interdit arbitrairement les visites de sa famille et de ses avocat·e·s. « La situation de Rached Ghannouchi illustre le grave recul des droits humains dans le pays depuis que le président Kaïs Saïed est au pouvoir, facilité par l’érosion de l’indépendance du pouvoir judiciaire. Pendant que le président ne cesse d’accuser publiquement les opposant·e·s politiques et les personnes qui critiquent le gouvernement d’être des “traîtres” ou des “terroristes”, nous voyons la justice devenir de plus en plus subordonnée aux intérêts politiques de l’exécutif », a déclaré Heba Morayef. Amnesty International demande que les autorités tunisiennes libèrent immédiatement Rached Ghannouchi, arrêtent d’utiliser abusivement le système judiciaire pour cibler des personnalités de l’opposition et respectent les obligations internationales du pays en matière de droits humains.

Après des années de mobilisation d’organisations de la société civile, de journalistes et de militant·e·s, le Liban a adopté une nouvelle loi sur les médias qui introduit d’importantes réformes fondées sur les droits humains, mais ne parvient pas à apporter tous les changements nécessaires pour garantir le respect, la protection et la réalisation du droit à la liberté d’expression dans le pays, a déclaré Amnesty International le 9 septembre 2026. Le 11 août 2026, le Parlement libanais a adopté une loi sur les médias très attendue, qui remplace les textes obsolètes de 1962 et 1994. Publiée au Journal officiel le 3 septembre, elle instaure plusieurs garanties majeures pour les journalistes, les professionnel·le·s des médias et les personnes exerçant leur droit à la liberté d’expression en ligne : dépénalisation de l’insulte et de la diffamation dans certains cas, meilleure protection des sources, interdiction de la détention provisoire dans les affaires liées aux médias, limitation de la juridiction des tribunaux militaires dans ce type d’affaires et renforcement des protections pour l’expression en ligne. Cependant, le Parlement a manqué l’occasion de s’attaquer à d’autres menaces pesant sur le droit à la liberté d’expression, notamment en conservant dans le Code pénal des dispositions qui prévoient des peines d’emprisonnement pour des propos protégés par cette liberté , tels que l’injure ou la diffamation à l’égard d’États étrangers, et en instaurant une nouvelle infraction pénale relative aux « informations fausses ou préjudiciables ». « Après des années de campagne menée par Amnesty International et d’autres organisations de défense des droits humains en faveur d’une réforme législative visant à protéger la liberté d’expression au Liban, la nouvelle loi sur les médias marque une avancée à plusieurs égards : elle supprime les sanctions pénales pour certaines infractions liées à l’insulte et à la diffamation et renforce les protections en matière de liberté d’expression en ligne. Toutefois, d’anciennes dispositions de la législation libanaise qui érigent en infraction des formes d’expression protégées restent en vigueur et pourraient finir par compromettre les progrès vers la dépénalisation que le Parlement s’est évertué à négocier, a déclaré Reina Wehbi, chargée de campagne sur le Liban à Amnesty International. « Ces dernières années, au Liban, des personnes ayant publié ou écrit sur des sujets controversés, ou ayant critiqué des personnalités influentes, ont été convoquées dans le cadre d’une enquête pénale ou traduites en justice pour avoir exercé pacifiquement leur droit à la liberté d’expression, sur la base d’articles vagues relatifs à l’injure et à la diffamation. Le Parlement libanais ne doit pas fermer les yeux sur les dispositions légales susceptibles de permettre de poursuivre et d’intimider des personnes ayant exprimé pacifiquement leurs opinions et doit mener à terme le processus de réforme ; il s’agit d’abroger le délit d’ » informations fausses ou préjudiciables « , qui ne constitue pas une infraction reconnue par le droit international, de dépénaliser totalement la diffamation et d’abroger le délit d’injure. » La nouvelle loi régit les propos diffusés par les médias, les publications, les sites Internet, les plateformes en ligne et d’autres moyens électroniques, mais les protections et les exemptions qu’elle définit ne s’appliquent pas nécessairement dans d’autres contextes où la liberté d’expression pourrait s’exercer. Adoption de nouvelles garanties L’un des aspects positifs de la loi sur les médias réside dans le fait qu’elle met en place des garanties visant à réduire le risque que le droit pénal, les institutions militaires ou les pouvoirs d’investigation ne servent à museler la critique ou le journalisme. L’article 114 interdit la détention provisoire pour les infractions commises par le biais des médias et des moyens électroniques régis par la loi, quels que soient le statut ou la profession de la personne mise en cause. En étendant expressément cette protection à la liberté d’expression en ligne, cet article lève une précédente ambiguïté, en vertu de laquelle les journalistes, les créateurs de contenu et les personnes publiant des contenus en ligne pouvaient être poursuivis en vertu du Code pénal et privés des garanties de procédure prévues dans les affaires liées à la publication. La loi renforce les dispositions du droit libanais relatives à l’incitation au conflit entre les communautés ou à la violence à l’encontre d’individus ou de groupes en raison de leur appartenance raciale, religieuse, confessionnelle ou ethnique, réelle ou présumée, de leur couleur de peau ou de leur sexe, en exigeant des tribunaux qu’ils prennent en compte des facteurs tels que le contexte, l’intention, l’influence, la diffusion et le risque de préjudice lorsqu’ils évaluent si un discours s’apparente à une incitation illégale à la haine, conformément aux normes internationales relatives aux droits humains. Ces garanties permettent de faire la distinction entre l’incitation réelle et l’expression protégée, même si des inquiétudes subsistent quant à la notion imprécise de « conflit intercommunautaire ». L’article 113 retire aux tribunaux militaires la compétence sur toutes les affaires relatives aux médias et à l’expression régies par la loi. Il répond à une préoccupation de longue date d’Amnesty International, qui a mis en lumière des cas dans lesquels des civil·e·s, dont des journalistes, ont été poursuivis devant des tribunaux militaires pour des atteintes à la liberté d’expression. Les articles 115 et 116 établissent des garanties explicites en matière d’indépendance éditoriale, protègent les journalistes contre toute ingérence, intimidation ou représailles visant à influencer leur travail, garantissent leur droit de se syndiquer et offrent une protection solide aux sources confidentielles en limitant les mesures de divulgation, de surveillance, de perquisition et de saisie susceptibles de révéler l’identité d’une source, sauf dans des circonstances strictement définies et soumises à contrôle judiciaire. Par ailleurs, la loi modernise le cadre régissant les médias au Liban : elle reconnaît expressément les médias numériques et définit un système clair d’enregistrement par notification pour les sites et les plateformes médiatiques, qui ne sont pas soumis à une autorisation préalable ni à l’octroi d’une licence. Elle supprime l’obligation d’obtenir une autorisation préalable pour les publications périodiques et abroge les restrictions imposées au nombre de périodiques politiques, efface la distinction entre publications politiques et non politiques, permet aux médias en ligne et diffusés par satellite d’exercer leurs activités grâce à une simple déclaration (au lieu d’un régime d’octroi de licence), et abolit la censure préalable sur l’impression, la publication et la distribution des publications non périodiques. L’article 98 confère un poids juridique considérable à l’intérêt public, en protégeant explicitement les reportages qui dénoncent la corruption, s’intéressent aux responsables publics ou traitent d’autres sujets d’inquiétude légitimes pour la population. « Ces nouvelles garanties sont le fruit d’un travail assidu et déterminé mené depuis des années par des militant·e·s, des défenseur·e·s des droits et des journalistes afin d’améliorer l’environnement en matière de liberté d’expression au Liban. Il appartient désormais à l’État de veiller à ce qu’elles soient rigoureusement respectées dans les jours et les mois à venir », a déclaré Reina Wehbi. De graves lacunes en matière de liberté d’expression perdurent Malgré ces avancées majeures, la loi présente un certain nombre de lacunes qui n’ont pas permis de rectifier des dispositions problématiques encore en vigueur et qui portent atteinte à la liberté d’expression. En effet, elle marque une régression en érigeant la désinformation en infraction pénale, sans la définir clairement. L’article 1

En réaction à l’annonce faite par le Canada, le Danemark, l’Espagne, la Finlande, la France, l’Islande, l’Irlande, la Norvège, la Pologne, le Portugal, le Royaume-Uni et la Suède, qui prévoient de restreindre les transactions commerciales avec les colonies israéliennes illégales en Territoire palestinien occupé et envisagent d’autres mesures, Erika Guevara Rosas, directrice générale de la recherche, du plaidoyer, des politiques et des campagnes à Amnesty International, a déclaré : « L’annonce selon laquelle 12 États prévoient d’instaurer des restrictions sur les échanges commerciaux avec les colonies israéliennes, illégales au regard du droit international humanitaire, constitue une avancée bienvenue, bien que tardive, qui doit ouvrir la voie à l’adoption d’autres mesures visant à mettre fin à l’occupation illégale d’Israël et au système institutionnalisé d’apartheid imposé à la population palestinienne. « Les mesures annoncées jusqu’à présent, certes importantes, sont loin de répondre aux instructions données en juillet 2024 par la Cour internationale de justice aux États, leur enjoignant de » ne pas prêter aide ou assistance » au maintien de l’occupation illégale du territoire palestinien par Israël. « La création et l’expansion des colonies – la violence perpétrée par des colons, avec le soutien de l’État, étant désormais un instrument central entraînant déplacement de population et spoliation à une échelle sans précédent sous le gouvernement israélien en place – sont une composante essentielle de la politique d’Israël et ne peuvent être dissociées de son système global d’apartheid. « Des villages palestiniens entiers risquent de façon imminente d’être rayés de la carte en Cisjordanie, dans le cadre d’une campagne de nettoyage ethnique . Dans le même temps, les Palestinien·ne·s dans la bande de Gaza occupée luttent pour leur survie face au génocide perpétré par Israël. Afin de mettre un terme aux violations découlant des colonies illégales, les États ne doivent pas s’arrêter là : ils doivent s’attaquer de front aux infrastructures qui financent, entretiennent et soutiennent l’occupation illégale Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International « Afin de mettre un terme aux violations découlant des colonies illégales, les États ne doivent pas s’arrêter là : ils doivent s’attaquer de front aux infrastructures qui financent, entretiennent et soutiennent l’occupation illégale. Ce qui suppose d’imposer des mesures à des organes clés, dont les ministères du gouvernement israélien, impliqués dans la création, le maintien et l’apport d’aide matérielle aux colonies illégales et à leurs infrastructures, et d’agir de manière efficace en vue de prévenir et de mettre un terme au transfert forcé de Palestinien·ne·s. « Tous les États doivent affirmer clairement qu’ils ne fourniront plus de soutien politique, financier et militaire contribuant aux violations graves et systématiques du droit international imputables à Israël. « Ils doivent imposer des sanctions ciblées, notamment des interdictions de voyager et des gels d’actifs, à l’encontre de Benjamin Netanyahou, Bezalel Smotrich, Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israël Katz et Orit Strock, en tant que responsables israéliens directement impliqués dans la campagne de nettoyage ethnique et le transfert forcé des Palestinien·ne·s en Cisjordanie, ainsi que dans le maintien de l’occupation illégale et de l’apartheid. Enfin, ils doivent interdire le transfert d’armes et d’équipements de sécurité risquant de faciliter les violations commises par Israël. « De leur côté, les États membres de l’UE doivent demander à la présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, de leur présenter une proposition visant à interdire, à l’échelle de l’UE, toute transaction commerciale avec les colonies, et inciter les principaux États, notamment l’Italie et l’Allemagne, à la soutenir. Enfin, ils doivent passer à la prochaine étape logique et suspendre l’Accord d’association entre l’UE et Israël. « L’heure n’est plus aux excuses, aux tergiversations ni aux demi-mesures. L’inaction face aux violations massives commises par Israël à l’encontre des Palestinien·ne·s envoie un signal dangereux, à savoir que les États ne sont pas disposés à respecter leurs propres obligations juridiques ; ce qui encourage les autorités israéliennes à continuer de bafouer le droit international en toute impunité, tout en privant les Palestinien·ne·s d’une réelle protection. »

https://bih.osce.org/news/mission-bosnia.body: News News Item OSCE reaffirms firm support for the Dayton Peace Agreement and the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina Issued on: 14 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina Fields of work: Conflict prevention and resolution SARAJEVO, 14 September 2026 - The OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina reaffirms its unwavering support for the Dayton Peace Agreement and the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which forms an integral part of the Agreement. Rhetoric that suggests an end to the state of BiH or of the entities within that state contradicts the Dayton Peace Agreement, threatens the stability and unity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and risks undermining both regional stability and the progress achieved to date. The Mission therefore urges all political actors, particularly those holding public office, to refrain from divisive rhetoric and actions that fuel tension or mistrust, including through the exploitation of ethnic prejudice, and instead focus on achieving tangible progress in the interests of all citizens.

News News Item Building stronger responses to hate crimes against religious communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina Issued on: 15 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina Strengthening co-operation between law enforcement and religious communities and improving responses to hate crimes were at the centre of a two-day OSCE workshop that concluded in Sarajevo on 15 September 2026. Organized by the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR), in co-operation with the OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH), the event brought together representatives of religious communities, law enforcement, civil society and international experts to discuss practical ways to prevent and respond to anti-Christian, anti-Muslim and anti-Semitic hate crimes. “In times when hate crimes are rising, it is important to address all of them in their specificity. We must increase the monitoring, awareness and training on this, and build trust and dialogue between religious communities and law enforcement through regular coordination and exchanges,” said Prof. Dr. Wolfgang Palaver, Personal Representative of the OSCE Chairperson-in-Office on Combating Racism, Xenophobia and Discrimination, also focusing on Intolerance and Discrimination against Christians and Members of Other Religions. Highlighting the broader impact of intolerance on society and institutions, Ambassador Evren Dağdelen Akgün, Personal Representative of the OSCE Chairperson-in-Office on Combating Intolerance and Discrimination against Muslims, said: “Anti-Muslim hatred and intolerance and discrimination against Muslims are not only threats to Muslim communities; they are a test of equal citizenship and institutional credibility, as well as of safety and security across the OSCE region, and in the world.” The importance of effective state action in protecting religious communities was also emphasized by Rabbi Andrew Baker, Personal Representative of the OSCE Chairperson-in-Office on Combating Anti-Semitism. “Governments not only have an obligation to provide the security necessary for Jews to gather and worship safely, but also to address the broader climate in which such threats can take root,” he said. Participants examined challenges in identifying, reporting, investigating and prosecuting hate crimes, and discussed ways to strengthen communication and trust between authorities and religious communities, particularly in areas where these communities are in the minority. Drawing on ODIHR’s practical guides on addressing anti-Christian, anti-Muslim and anti-Semitic hate crimes, the workshop concluded by identifying effective measures to improve institutional responses and better address the security needs of religious communities in BiH.

https://www.fidh.org/en/en/region/europe.body: 15/09/2026 Press release Russia European Court of Human Rights MATEUSZ WLODARCZYK / NURPHOTO / NURPHOTO VIA AFP The International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) strongly condemns the decision of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) to strike out 879 applications against Russia from its list of pending cases, leaving more than 1,500 individuals and organisations without a judicial examination of their complaints. Paris, 15 September 2026. On 3 September 2026, the Court decided to discontinue the examination of 879 applications, some of which had been pending since 2007. The cases concerned serious human rights violations, including, among others, unlawful detention, torture, destruction of property, restrictions on freedom of expression, assembly and association, and deprivation of life. In the Lebedeva and Others against Russia judgment, the Court announced that it would continue to examine only interstate and individual applications against Russia connected with the armed conflicts in Ukraine and Georgia. The Court justified its decision on administrative and resource grounds, concluding that, following Russia’s exclusion from the Council of Europe, examining the remaining cases would require significant judicial resources without making a sufficient contribution to its case law. In the words of the Court, the discarded cases " do not raise issues of marked importance for the Russian Federation’s responsibility under the Convention, nor do they call for the development or clarification of the Court’s case-law. " However, the European Convention on Human Rights provides that proceedings should continue where respect for human rights so requires. " This decision by the ECtHR is incomprehensible. The guardian of human rights in the Council of Europe region has chosen expediency over redress. In doing so, it has done harm to the thousands of victims of violations of human rights in Russia, and undermined itself and the entire international human rights protection system at a time of arguably its biggest crisis, " said Ilya Nuzov, the director of Eastern Europe and Central Asia Desk at FIDH . Victims awaiting justice for two decades left without recourse These are not abstract cases or merely numbers in the Court’s backlog, they represent real victims of grave human rights abuses, some of whom had been waiting for justice for almost two decades. They include residents of the village of Vremenny in Dagestan whose homes were destroyed during a counter-terrorism operation, victims of bombings during the Second Chechen War, relatives of people killed in the Kolskaya drilling rig disaster in 2011, relatives of journalist and human rights defender Timur Kuashev, who was killed by Russian security services in 2014 and relatives of the Syrian Muhammad Taha Al‐Ismai, who was tortured and killed by members of so-called Wagner Group in Syria in 2017. The decision also sends a deeply troubling message to victims who spent years exhausting domestic remedies and gathering evidence in the hope that Strasbourg would provide an independent assessment of their claims. Many are now being told, after years of waiting, to restart the process by seizing another international mechanism. Even where this remains legally possible, such decisions might not be binding or offer any concrete remedies to plaintiffs, which could have been enforceable had they come from the European Court, even if years down the road. At the same time, the Council of Europe has yet to establish effective mechanisms to ensure payment of compensation already awarded by the Court in cases against Russia. FIDH member organisation in Russia, Memorial Human Rights Defense Center, has repeatedly proposed concrete solutions, including the creation of a dedicated fund within the Council of Europe system and mechanisms for recovering compensation from Russian state assets abroad. " I am outraged by the Court’s decision, which has left Russian applicants without hope of obtaining justice. The Council of Europe has the means to act. Memorial has repeatedly proposed concrete mechanisms to ensure that Russian citizens receive the compensation awarded to them by the Court. This would be an unusual and extraordinary decision, requiring political will, but there are solid legal grounds for it ," stressed Natalia Morozova, the co-chair of the Memorial Human Rights Defense Center . Denial of accountability for Russia’s crimes in Syria Among the cases struck out is the application concerning Al-Ismail, a Syrian national who was tortured and killed by alleged members of the so-called Wagner Group in 2017. His family has spent years seeking truth and justice for his killing and for the grave violations he suffered. The application, concerning violations of Articles 2 and 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, was submitted on behalf of Al‐Ismail’s relatives, with legal and documentation support from FIDH, Memorial Human Rights Defence Center and and the Syrian Center for Media and Freedom of Expression (SCM), and raised important questions concerning Russia’s responsibility under the Convention for extraterritorial violations committed by actors alleged to operate as its de facto agents. The decision means that allegations concerning torture and unlawful killing of a Syrian national in Syria by members of the so-called Wagner group, will never receive a judicial examination by the European Court. " I am deeply disappointed by the Court’s decision to strike out the Al-Ismail case. This is not merely a procedural closure; it is a serious judicial setback that deprives his family of an authoritative examination of the torture and killing he suffered. It is also a missed opportunity to develop the Court’s jurisprudence concerning extraterritorial crimes committed by private military structures and other de facto agents operating under the direction or control of a State ," said Mazen Darwish, Director General of SCM . FIDH calls on the European Court of Human Rights to reconsider its decision and on the Council of Europe and its member states to ensure that victims of human rights violations committed by Russia are not abandoned. Russia’s refusal to cooperate with the Court cannot become a reason to deny victims justice, truth and reparation. The consequences of a State’s refusal to cooperate with an international human rights mechanism must not be borne by the victims of the alleged violations. Where applicants have complied with the applicable requirements and have waited for years for an independent judicial examination, the absence of cooperation by the respondent State should not, in itself, extinguish their opportunity to have serious allegations of torture, unlawful killing and other grave human rights violations examined. This principle is particularly important in cases involving serious violations committed outside the territory of the respondent State, where access to effective remedies may already be severely limited. International accountability mechanisms should seek to ensure that procedural and institutional difficulties do not create an additional barrier to justice for victims and their families. Украинаның АҚШ-тағы бұрынғы елшісі Ольга Стефанишина Азаттықтың Украин қызметіне берген сұхбатында АҚШ-тың Киевке Каспий құбыр консорциумын (КҚК) атқыламау туралы өтініші туралы да айтады. “Вашингтонда болған кезіңізде америкалық шенеуніктерден Новороссийскіге шабуыл жасамау жөнінде өтініш қаншалықты жиі түсті?” деген сұраққа тамыздың басында қызметінен кеткен бұрынғы елші "Chevron мен Exxon кемелеріне қатысты" болмаса, басқа өзге соққыға қатысты [түспеді] дейді. "Қазақстанмен бұрыннан бері және жақсы қарым-қатынасым бар. Қазақстан елшісімен хабарласып тұрдық. Бір жағынан, жағдайды түсіну бар; екінші жағынан, бұл Қазақстанның бюджетін құрайтын және АҚШ-тың тіке экономикалық мүддесіне қатысты сала. Қазақтар да, Exxon мен Chevron да Украинаның ұстанымын түсінетінін айқын жеткізеді, бірақ баламасыз бағыт қателік болғанын мойындайды" деді бұрынғы елші. Оның сөзінше, балама жол табу "тез шешіле салатын нәрсе" емес. "Мұны жақсы білетін ресейліктер де өздерінің әскери нысандарын коммерциялық инфрақұрылымға барынша жақын орналастырған" деді ол. Каспий құбыр консорциумы Қазақстан мұнайының басым бөлігін халықаралық нарыққа тасымалдайды. Бұған дейін украин дрондары консорциумның инфрақұрылымына бірнеше рет шабуылдап, бірнеше күн бұрын да соның салдарынан мұнай тиеу кідірген еді. Осыған дейін АҚШ жағы Украинаға КҚК-ның инфрақұрылымына шабуылдамау жөнінде өтініш айтқаны хабарланған еді. КҚК-ның акционерлері қатарында қазақстандық "Қазмұнайгаз", ресейлік, "Транснефть", америкалық Chevron мен ExxonMobil да бар. https://www.azattyq.org/a/baq-qazaqstand.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР БАҚ: Қазақстанда қамауда отырған шешен азаматы Мансур Мовлаев өзіне қол салмақ болған 15 қыркүйек 2026 жыл, 16:30 БАҚ: Қазақстанда қамауда отырған шешен азаматы Мансур Мовлаев өзіне қол салмақ болған Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Мансур Мовлаев Ресейдің сұрауымен Қазақстанда ұсталып, қамауда отырған, кез келген сәтте Ресейге экстрадициялануы мүмкін шешен азаматы Мансур Мовлаев тергеу абақтысында өзіне қол салуға әрекет жасаған. Мұны оның мүддесін қорғаушы заңгер Вадим Дроздовтың сөзіне сүйеніп "Новая газета Европа" жазды. Медициналық көмек алған Мовлаевтың өміріне қазір қауіп төніп тұрған жоқ деді басылым. Өзіне қол жұмсамас бұрын жазып қалдырған хатында Мовлаев "әділетсіздіктен қажығанын" айтқан. "Сот та, прокуратура да біздің үнімізді естімейді! Олар [Рамзан Қадыровтың адамдары] мені азаптап, қорлап, өлтіреді және соны өзім жасағандай етіп айтады. Енді өзімді азаптауға жол бермеймін! 16 ай бойы мен экстрадицияланудан қорқып, үміт үзбей өмір сүрдім... Енді тек қорқыныш қалды!" деп жазған Мовлаев. Ол сондай-ақ ресейлік белсенді, марқұм Алексей Навальныйдың Санкт-Петербургтегі штаб-пәтерінің бұрынғы қызметкері, қазір Қазақстанда тергеу абақтысында отырған Юлия Емельянованы Ресейге экстрадицияланудан құтқаруды сұраған. Осы жаңалық жарияланған сәтке дейін Қазақстанның ішкі істер министрлігінің Қылмыстық-атқару жүйесі комитеті Мовлаев жөнінде тараған ақпаратқа байланысты түсініктеме беруді сұраған Азаттықтың сауалхатына жауап бермеді. Мансур Мовлаев 2025 жылдың мамыр айында Ресейдің сұрауы бойынша Алматыда ұсталған. Ресей билігі оған экстремизм айыбын тағып отыр. 2026 жылдың қаңтарында Қазақстанның Бас прокуратурасы оны Ресейге экстрадициялауды мақұлдаған. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ БАҚ: Қазақстан соғысқа қарсы ресейліктерді жаппай депортациялауға дайындалып жатыр Кавказ.Реалий сайтының дерегінше , 2020 жылы Мовлаев Шешенстанда заңсыз есірткі айналымы туралы іс бойынша сотталған. 2022 жылы шартты бостандық алып, қамаудан шыққан. 2022 жылдың тамыз айында оны Шешенстанның Шали аудандық ішкі істер бөлімінің қызметкерлері тағы да ұрлап әкетіп , түрмеде ұстаған. Амалын тауып қашып шыққан Мовлаев Қырғызстан аумағына құжатсыз, заңсыз кірген. 2023 жылдың қазан айында Бішкек соты оны шекараны заңсыз кесіп өтті деген айыппен алты айға бостандығынан айырып , жазасын өтегеннен кейін депортациялау туралы үкім шығарған. Қамаудан босап шыққан соң Мовлаев Қазақстанға кеткен. Ақпан айында БҰҰ-ның Адам құқықтары жөніндегі комитеті Қазақстанды Мовлаевтың шағымын қарағанға дейін оны Ресейге экстрадицияламауға шақырған. Осыдан кейін Қазақстанның Жоғарғы соты пана сұраған адамның ісі қаралып болғанға дейін экстрадицияны уақытша тоқтатқан. Қазақстан соты Мансур Мовлаевқа босқын мәртебесін беруден бас тартты. 11 қыркүйекте кассациялық сот төменгі соттардың шешімдерін күшінде қалдырды. Биыл Мовлаевты қолдау тобы оның Шешенстандағы туыстарына қысым жасалғанын хабарлады. Маусым айында белсенділер оның бауырына зорлық-зомбылық көрсетілгенін және ата-анасы ұрланғанын мәлімдеді. Кейінірек Мовлаевтың адвокаты ата-анасы үйіне оралды деп хабарлады. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Құқық қорғаушылар Тоқаевты ресейлік екі белсендіні экстрадиция жасамауға үндеді Шешенстанда ұрлап әкетілген Мансур Мавлоевтың ата-анасы үйіне оралды Апелляция ресейлік белсенділер Мовлаев пен Емельянованың пана сұрау бойынша шағымын қанағаттандырмады Алматы соты бір жылға жуық уақыттан бері абақтыда отырған Мовлаевты қамауда ұстау мерзімін тағы созды Сот Мовлаевқа босқын мәртебесін бермеу туралы шешімді заңсыз деп танудан бас тартты БАҚ: Қазақстанда қамауда отырған шешен азаматы Мансур Мовлаев өзіне қол салмақ болған

https://www.azattyq.org/a/ozbekstanda-ty.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР Өзбекстан тыйым салған партияның басшысының бауыры "Алға Қарақалпақстан" деген сөзі үшін жазаланды 15 қыркүйек 2026 жыл, 15:31 Өзбекстан тыйым салған партияның басшысының бауыры "Алға Қарақалпақстан" деген сөзі үшін жазаланды Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Аман Сағидуллаев Өзбекстанда тыйым салынған "Алға Қарақалпақстан" партиясының жетекшісі Аман Сағидуллаевтың бауыры Жолдас Сағидуллаев үш күн әкімшілік қамауда отырып шықты, оған келесі жолы үстінен қылмыстық іс қозғалатынын ескерткен деп хабарлады Түрікмен Хельсинки қоры. Адам құқықтарын қорғаушы қордың мәліметінше, 63 жастағы Жолдас Сағидуллаев 20 тамызда Қараөзек ауданындағы милиция ғимаратында "Алға Қарақалпақстан" деп айтқан сөзі үшін әкімшілік жауапқа тартылған. Сол күні өз әрекетін Өзбекстандағы әлеуметтік саясатқа наразымын деп түсіндірген Сағидуллаев ұсталып, түнге қарай босатылған. Арада үш апта өткенде Сағидуллаев аудандық сотқа шақырылған. Жабық өткен сот отырысында ол "ұсақ бұзақылық" жасағаны және "қоғам қауіпсіздігіне қауіп төндіретін жалған ақпарат таратқаны" үшін кінәлі деп танылған. Сот Сағидуллаевты үш күнге әкімшілік қамауға алу туралы шешім шығарып, ол Нөкістегі арнайы қамау орнына жөнелтілген деп хабарлады адам құқығын қорғаушы топ. Жолдас Сағидуллаев "Алға Қарақалпақстан" деген сөзі үшін бұған дейін де жауапқа тартылған: сәуір айында ол жеті күн қамауда отырып шыққан. Құқық бұзғаны туралы толтырылған хаттамада ол көшеде балағат сөздер айтып, ұсақ бұзақылық жасады деп көрсетілген. "Аудандық ішкі істер бөлімі қызметкерлері қарсылық мазмұндағы сөздерді хаттамаға қоспау туралы нұсқау бар деп түсіндірген. Бұл жолы хаттамаға да әдейі бұрмалап жазған, – дейді Түркіменстан Хельсинки қоры. – Сағидуллаев сот шешімі әлі күнге қолына тимегенін, бірақ интернетте немесе басқа жерде ешқандай жалған ақпарат таратпағанын айтады. Соған қарамастан, арнайы ұстау мекемесінің әкімшілігі келесі жолы ол қылмыстық айып бойынша жауапқа тартылуы мүмкін екенін ескерткен". Адам құқығын қорғаушы қор Қарақалпақстанда азаматтық белсенділікпен айналысатын қарақалпақ ұлты өкілдерінің үстінен жалған айыптар бойынша саяси астары бар әкімшілік іс қозғау кең тарағанын айтады. Ресми Ташкент ешкім саяси ұстаным-көзқарасына бола қудаланбайды дейді. 2023 жылы Қарақалпақстандағы сот қазір Еуропада тұрып жатқан Аман Сағидуллаевты 2022 жылдың шілдесінде Нөкісте болған жаппай наразылықтарға қатысы бар деп тауып, сырттай 18 жылға бостандығынан айырған. Сағидуллаев сырттай сот процесін "қисынсыз" деп атаған. 2022 жылы Өзбекстан билігі референдумға шығаруға ұсынған Конституцияның жаңа жобасында Қарақалпақстанның егемендігі мен Өзбекстаннан бөлініп шығу құқығы туралы баптардың болмауы Қарақалпақстанда елдің наразылығын туғызды. Шілденің басында жаппай халық наразылығын үкімет күш қолданып басып-жаншыды. Ресми дерек бойынша, 21 адам өліп, 200-ден астам адам жараланған. Құқық қорғаушылар бұдан да көп адам өлген болуы мүмкін деп санайды. 500 адам ұсталған. Көтеріліс Қарақалпақ астанасы Нөкісте басталғандықтан, ол "Нөкіс оқиғасы" аталып кетті. Наразылықтан кейін Ташкент халық пікірін ескеретінін айтып, даулы өзгерістерден бас тартқан. Бірақ осы оқиғадан кейін Өзбекстан билігі қарақалпақ белсенділерін ел ішінде және шетелде қудалауды күшейткен. Сот журналиске үш жарым жыл шартты жаза беріп, бес жыл материал жариялауға тыйым салды. Бұл туралы Азаттыққа Омаровтың адвокаты Төлеген Шайықов айтты. Құқық қорғаушы Бақытжан Төреғожина да Омаровтың сот залынан босатылғанын хабарлады. "Ахуал сегодня" YouTube-арнасының авторы Омаров шілдеде Қылмыстық кодекстің 174-бабымен ("Әлеуметтік, ұлттық, рулық, нәсілдік, таптық немесе діни араздықты қоздыру") күдікке ілініп, екі айға қамауға алынған. Сот қаулысында журналистің президент туралы сатиралық сөздер айтқаны баяндалған. Шілдедегі қаулыда "бейнежазбада Омаров қазіргі президент жайлы сатиралық пікірлер айтады, әлеуметтік-экономикалық саясат және мемлекет қызметі туралы мәселелерді қозғайды. Оның сөздері ирония мен сыни сипатта, осылайша халық арасында теріс пікір қалыптастырады" деп жазылған еді. Азамат Омаров YouTube платформасында "Ахуал сегодня" арнасын ашып, елдегі қоғамдық-саяси оқиғаларды әзілмен жеткізіп жүрген. Баспасөз еркіндігін қорғаумен айналысатын "Шекарасыз тілшілер" (RSF) халықаралық ұйымы Азамат Омаров екі айға қамауға алынғанда қолдау білдіріп мәлімдеме жасаған. "Шекарасыз тілшілер" Омаровтың үкіметтің атына сатиралық пікір айтқан видеоға бола екі айға қамауға алынуын айыптайды. Оған тағылып отырған "араздық қоздыру" айыбы алынып, оның жабдықтары өзіне қайтарылуы керек" деген еді RSF ұйымы мәлімдемесінде. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ "Алаңдатарлық үрдіс". https://www.azattyq.org/a/pravoslav-shir.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР Бұрынғы діни қызметкер Иаков Воронцовтан "есірткі притонын ұйымдастыру" айыбы алынды 15 қыркүйек 2026 жыл, 14:41 Бұрынғы діни қызметкер Иаков Воронцовтан "есірткі притонын ұйымдастыру" айыбы алынды Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Иаков Воронцов Қазақстандағы Орыс православ шіркеуінің бұрынғы діни қызметкері Иаков Воронцовқа тағылған "есірткі притонын ұйымдастыру" айыбы күшін жойды. Қылмыстық кодекстің 302-бабының 1-бөлігінде қарастырылған айып Воронцовқа берілген прокурор актісінде жоқ деп хабарлады оның адвокаты Ғалым Нұрпейісов Азаттық Азияға. Қорғаушы айыпты алып тастауға не себеп болғанын білмейді. "Прокурор оны айтқан жоқ. Ол айып тағушы ғой. Біз тек айыптауға келіспейтінімізді білдірдік", – деді Нұрпейісов. 40 жастағы Воронцовқа "есірткі заттарын сату ниетімен заңсыз өндіру, өңдеу, сатып алу, сақтау немесе тасымалдау" (296-баптың 4-бөлігі бойынша) айыбы да тағылған. Бұл айып әлі күшінде. Воронцов биыл 13 ақпанда ол "есірткі заттарын тұтынған" деген күдікпен әуелі 10 күнге қамалған . Соның алдында түнде оның Алматыдағы үйінде тінту жүргізген полиция тыйым салынған зат салынған үш пакет табылғанын хабарлаған. Воронцов өзіне тағылған айыптарды жоққа шығарды. Ол 23 ақпанда 10 күндік қамаудан босап шығуға тиіс еді, алайда сол күні таңертең оны тергеушіге жауап беруге әкеткен. Адвокатының айтуынша, сол кезде оны "есірткі притонын ұстаған" және "сату мақсатын көздемей есірткі заттарын сақтаған" деген күдікпен екі айға қамаған . Иаков Воронцов 2022 жылы Ресей Украинаға қарсы бастаған соғысты тоқтатуды талап еткен православ діни қызметкерлерінің ашық үндеуіне қол қойғандардың бірі ретінде көпшілікке танылған. 2023 жылы тамызда Орыс православ шіркеуі оны діни дәрежесінен айырды. Содан кейін Воронцов Қазақстанда Мәскеу патриархатына бағынбайтын, өзін-өзі басқаратын дербес православ діни бірлестігін құруға талпынды. Алматы қаласының әділет департаменті ол ұйымды тіркеуден бас тартты. Бұған келіспеген Воронцов әділет министрлігінің үстінен сотқа жүгінген еді, бірақ бірнеше күннен кейін өзі ұсталды. Воронцов қамауда болған кезде билік оны мәжбүрлеп емдеуге Алматы облысындағы психиатриялық ауруханаға бір айға жатқызды. Сол кезде қазақстандық адам құқықтары және заңдылықты сақтау бюросы дәрігерлер Воронцовтың денсаулығынан ешқандай психикалық ауытқу таппады деп хабарлаған. Кейін оны қайтадан тергеу абақтысына ауыстырды. Тамыз айының аяғында Иаков Воронцовтың үстінен қозғалған қылмыстық іс бойынша тергеу аяқталып , материалдары сотқа жіберілгені мәлім болды. Сот процесі өткен жұмада басталуы керек еді, бірақ отырыс кейінге қалдырылды. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Бұрынғы дін қызметшісі Иаков Воронцов психиатриялық ауруханадан тергеу абақтысына ауыстырылды Апелляция соты экс-священник Иаков Воронцовты психиатриялық емханада қалдырды Репрессив тактика ма, заңды сараптама ма?
